[[別表神社]] |創建 = [[斉衡]]3年（[[856年]]） |本殿 = [[流造]] |別名 = |札所等 = |例祭 = [[8月25日]] |神事 = |地図 = Japan Ibaraki }} [[File:酒列磯前神社 一の鳥居.JPG|thumb|200px|一の鳥居
額「酒列磯前神社」は[[小松宮彰仁親王|彰仁親王]]の書。]] '''酒列磯前神社'''（さかつらいそさきじんじゃ）は、[[茨城県]][[ひたちなか市]]にある[[神社]]。[[式内社]]（[[名神大社]]）。[[近代社格制度|旧社格]]は[[国幣中社]]で、現在は[[神社本庁]]の[[別表神社]]。 == 概要 == [[茨城県]]の東部、[[太平洋]]に面した岬の丘上に鎮座する。[[那珂川]]対岸の[[大洗町]]にある[[大洗磯前神社]]と深い関係にあると言われ、2社で1つの信仰を形成している。 == 祭神 == '''主祭神''' * '''[[少彦名命]]'''（すくなひこなのみこと） *: 大名持命とともに国造りを行ったとされる。 '''配祀神''' * [[大国主|大名持命]] （おおなもちのみこと） *: [[大国主|大国主命]]（大己貴命）の別名。[[大洗磯前神社]]祭神で、その分霊。少彦名命の力を借りて国造りを行ったとされる。 国造りにおいて『[[古事記]]』・『[[日本書紀]]』・『[[風土記]]』などの神話では大名持命と少彦名命の2神が併せて登場することから、当社に限らずこの2神の組み合わせで祀る神社は多い。また、当社では少彦名命を[[七福神]]の[[えびす]]、大名持命を[[大黒天]]とも見なしている。 == 歴史 == === 創建 === 『[[日本文徳天皇実録]]』によると、[[斉衡]]3年（[[856年]]）に[[常陸国]][[鹿島郡 (茨城県)|鹿島郡]]の大洗磯前に神が現れたとされる。 {{quotation| 常陸国上言。鹿嶋郡大洗磯前有神新降。初郡民有煮海為塩者。夜半望海。光耀属天。明日有両怪石。見在水次。高各尺許。体於神造。非人間石。塩翁私異之去。後一日。亦有廿餘小石。在向石左右。似若侍坐。彩色非常。或形像沙門。唯無耳目。時神憑人云。我是大奈母知少比古奈命也。昔造此国訖。去徃東海。今為済民。更亦来帰。 ある夜、[[塩|製塩業]]の者が海に光るものを見た。次の日、海辺に二つの奇妙な石があった。両方とも一尺ほどだった。さらに次の日には20あまりの小石が怪石の周りに侍坐するように出現した。怪石は彩色が派手で、僧侶の姿をしていた。神霊は人に依って「われは大奈母知（おおなもち）・少比古奈命（すくなひこなのみこと）である。昔、この国を造り終えて、東の海に去ったが、今人々を救うために再び帰ってきた」と託宣した。 |『日本文徳天皇実録』斉衡3年12月戊戌条}} そして、大己貴命（大奈母知）が大洗に、少彦名命（少比古奈命）が酒列に祀られ、両社の創建となったと伝えられている。 当社周辺海岸の岩石群は南に約45度に傾斜して並んでいるが、その内の一部の北に傾いた部分、すなわち「逆列（さかつら）」の地名が社名の由来とされる。のちに酒の神様を祀るところから「酒列」となったとされる[http://www.oyashiro.or.jp/link/0006.html 酒列磯前神社]（茨城県神社庁）。。 === 概史 === 『[[延喜式神名帳]]』には「[[常陸国]][[那珂郡|那賀郡]] 酒烈礒前薬師菩薩神社」と記載され、[[名神大社]]に列している。 [[中世]]には廃絶し社殿もなくなっていた。[[近世]]になって[[水戸藩]]2代藩主・[[徳川光圀]]により造営の起工がなされ、3代藩主・[[徳川綱條|綱條]]により現在地に遷座がなされ再興された。旧鎮座地は一の鳥居の辺りと伝えられている。 [[明治]]18年（[[1885年]]）、[[近代社格制度]]において[[国幣中社]]に列した。現在では公称を「酒列磯前神社」としている。 === 神階 === * [[天安 (日本)|天安]]元年（[[857年]]）8月7日、官社に預かる （『日本文徳天皇実録』） * 天安元年（857年）10月15日、「薬師菩薩名神」の号を授かる （『日本文徳天皇実録』） == 境内 == 拝殿正面上部のリスとブドウの彫刻は、[[左甚五郎]]の作とされる。また、二の鳥居左右の狛犬は、昭和の石工・飯塚兵吉の作である。参道の樹叢は椿・タブノキ・スダジイなどからなる広葉樹林で、茨城県の天然記念物に指定されている。 なお現在の一の鳥居近く、比観亭跡周辺が元の社地とされている（現在は小祠が鎮座）。 酒列磯前神社 本殿.JPG|本殿 酒列磯前神社 拝殿.JPG|拝殿 酒列磯前神社 水戸斉昭公腰かけの石.JPG|[[徳川斉昭|水戸斉昭]]公腰かけの石 酒列磯前神社 二の鳥居.JPG|二の鳥居 酒列磯前神社 参道.JPG|参道の樹叢（県指定天然記念物） == 摂末社 == [[File:酒列鎮霊社 (酒列磯前神社境内社).JPG|thumb|200px|酒列鎮霊社]] [[File:酒列磯前神社 末社群.JPG|thumb|200px|末社5社]] * 酒列鎮霊社 （さかつらちんれいしゃ） ** 祭神：[[日露戦争]]より[[第二次世界大戦]]までの戦没者506柱 *: 本殿の北隣に鎮座。 * 稲荷神社 -祭神：[[ウカノミタマ|倉稲魂命]] * 天満宮 - 祭神：[[菅原道真]]公 * 事比羅神社 - 祭神：[[大物主|大物主命]] * 冨士神社 - 祭神：[[コノハナノサクヤビメ|木花咲耶媛命]]。子安神として信仰されている。 * 水神社 - 祭神：[[ミヅハノメ|罔象女命]] == 文化財 == === 茨城県指定天然記念物 === * 酒列磯前神社の樹叢 - 参道両側や境内周辺に広がる広葉樹林（椿やタブノキ、スダジイなど）。平成17年指定。 == 現地情報 == '''所在地''' * [[茨城県]][[ひたちなか市]]磯崎町4607-2 '''交通アクセス''' * 最寄駅：[[ひたちなか海浜鉄道]][[ひたちなか海浜鉄道湊線|湊線]] [[阿字ヶ浦駅]] （徒歩約15分） - 湊線終着駅。 '''周辺''' * 比観亭跡 - 水戸藩が建てた東屋跡。ひたちなか市指定史跡。 * 観濤所 - 水戸藩主が選定した景勝地。ひたちなか市指定名勝。 * 川子塚古墳 - ひたちなか市指定史跡。 * 平磯白亜紀層 - 周辺海岸。県指定天然記念物。 == 脚注 == {{Short description|Shinto shrine in Ibaraki prefecture}} {{Infobox religious building | religious_affiliation = Shinto | image = Sajatsura Isosaki Jinja Shaden.jpg | deity = [[Sukunabikona]] }} '''Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine''' is a [[Shinto shrine]] in [[Hitachinaka, Ibaraki|Hitachinaka City]], [[Ibaraki Prefecture]] [[Japan]].{{Cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=1P4UAAAAIAAJ&dq=Sakatsura+Isosaki&pg=PA136 |title=Namazu-e and Their Themes: An Interpretative Approach to Some Aspects of Japanese Folk Religion |date=1964 |publisher=Brill Archive |language=en}}{{Cite book |last=Louis-Frédéric |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=35NQAAAAMAAJ&q=Sakatsura+Isosaki |title=Buddhism |date=1995 |publisher=Flammarion |isbn=978-2-08-013558-2 |language=en}}{{Cite book |last1=railways |first1=Japan Department of |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=MXK-sZwXLFgC&q=Sakatsura+Isosaki |title=An Official Guide to Eastern Asia, Trans-continental Connections Between Europe and Asia ...: North eastern Japan. 1914. [2], x, 488 p. 6 pl. (1 col), 13 fold. maps, 12 fold. plans |last2=Railways |first2=Japan Dept of |date=1914 |language=en}} It is a [[Beppyo shrine]]. It is also a {{ill|Myojin Taisha|ja|名神大社}} in the [[Engishiki]]. It was founded in 856. [[File:酒列磯前神社_一の鳥居.JPG|thumb|200x200px| The shrine's first [[Torii]] gate]] It enshrines [[Sukunabikona]]. It is closely linked to [[Oarai Isosaki Shrine]] which also worships [[Sukunabikona]].{{Cite book |last1=Cali |first1=Joseph |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=J1gEEAAAQBAJ&dq=Oarai+Isosaki+Shrine&pg=PA73 |title=Shinto Shrines: A Guide to the Sacred Sites of Japan's Ancient Religion |last2=Dougill |first2=John |date=2012-11-30 |publisher=University of Hawaii Press |isbn=978-0-8248-3775-4 |language=en}}{{Cite web |title=A Study of Shinto: The Religion of the Japanese Nation |url=https://www.routledge.com/A-Study-of-Shinto-The-Religion-of-the-Japanese-Nation/Katu/p/book/9780415845762 |access-date=2023-11-18 |website=Routledge & CRC Press |language=en}}{{Rp|page=29}} ==Overview== {{神社 |名称 = Sakattsura Isosaki Shrine |画像 = [[File:Sajatsura Isosaki Jinja Shaden.jpg|270px]]

Former [[National Middle Shrine|Kokuhei Chūsha]]
[[Bekkaku Shrine]] |創建 = [[Saikō]] 3rd year (856) |本殿 = [[Nagare-zukuri]] |別名 = |札所等 = |例祭 = [[August 25]] |神事 = |地図 = Japan Ibaraki }} [[File:Sakattsura Isosaki Shrine First Torii.JPG|thumb|200px|First Torii
Plaque "Sakattsura Isosaki Shrine" written by [[Prince Komatsu Akihito]]]] '''Sakattsura Isosaki Shrine''' (さかつらいそさきじんじゃ) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Hitachinaka City]], [[Ibaraki Prefecture]]. It is classified as a [[Myōjin Taisha|Myōjin Taisha]] under the [[Engishiki|Engishiki system]]. The former shrine rank was [[National Middle Shrine|Kokuhei Chūsha]], and it is now a [[Bekkaku Shrine]] under the [[Association of Shinto Shrines]]. == Overview == The shrine is situated on a hill facing the [[Pacific Ocean]] in eastern [[Ibaraki Prefecture]]. It is closely related to [[Ōarai Isosaki Shrine]] in [[Ōarai Town]] across the [[Naka River]], and the two shrines form a single faith. == Deities == '''Main Deity''' * '''[[Sukunahikona no Mikoto]]''' (少彦名命) *: Known for helping [[Ōnamuchi no Mikoto]] (Ōkuninushi no Mikoto) in creating the land. '''Enshrined Deity''' * [[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi no Mikoto]] (大名持命) *: Another name for [[Ōkuninushi no Mikoto]] (大己貴命), the deity of [[Ōarai Isosaki Shrine]], and his divided spirit. He is said to have created the land with the help of Sukunahikona no Mikoto. In the myths found in the [[Kojiki]], [[Nihon Shoki]], and [[Fudoki]], these two deities often appear together in the stories of land creation. Many shrines enshrine this combination of deities. At this shrine, Sukunahikona no Mikoto is also considered [[Ebisu]] of the [[Seven Lucky Gods]], and Ōnamuchi no Mikoto is considered [[Daikokuten]]. == History == === Founding === According to the [[Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku]], a deity appeared at Ōarai Isosaki in [[Kashima District, Hitachi Province]] in Saikō 3rd year (856). {{quotation| Hitachi Province reports that a new deity has descended at Ōarai Isosaki in Kashima District. Initially, a salt maker saw a shining light in the sea at midnight. The next day, two strange stones appeared on the shore, each about a foot high. The following day, more than twenty small stones appeared around the strange stones, resembling attendants. The stones were vividly colored and shaped like monks, but without ears or eyes. The divine spirit possessed a person and said, "I am Ōnamuchi and Sukunahikona. We finished creating this land and went to the eastern sea, but we have returned to save the people." |Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku, Saikō 3rd year, December戊戌条}} Thus, Ōkuninushi no Mikoto (Ōnamuchi) was enshrined at Ōarai, and Sukunahikona no Mikoto was enshrined at Sakattsura, marking the founding of the two shrines. The rock formations along the coast near the shrine are tilted about 45 degrees to the south, and the part that tilts to the north is called "Gyaku-retsu" (逆列, Reverse Row), which is said to be the origin of the shrine's name. Later, it came to be known as "Sakattsura" because it enshrined the god of sake (alcohol)[http://www.oyashiro.or.jp/link/0006.html Sakattsura Isosaki Shrine] (Ibaraki Prefecture Shrine Office). === Historical Overview === The [[Engishiki Jinmyocho]] lists the shrine as "Hitachi Province Naka District Sakattsura Isosaki Yakushi Bosatsu Shrine" and classifies it as a Myōjin Taisha. The shrine fell into decline during the [[Middle Ages]] and lost its buildings. In the [[Early Modern Period]], the second lord of the [[Mito Domain]], [[Tokugawa Mitsukuni]], initiated the rebuilding of the shrine, and the third lord, [[Tokugawa Tsunaeda]], relocated and restored it to its current location. The old site is said to be near the first torii. In 1885 (Meiji 18), the shrine was ranked as a [[National Middle Shrine|Kokuhei Chūsha]] under the [[Modern Shrine Rank System]]. It is now officially named "Sakattsura Isosaki Shrine." === Shrine Rankings === * [[Ten'an]] 1st year (857), August 7 - Received official shrine status (Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku) * Ten'an 1st year (857), October 15 - Granted the title "Yakushi Bosatsu Myōjin" (Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku) == Grounds == The carving of a squirrel and grapes on the front of the haiden is said to be the work of [[Hidari Jingorō]]. The guardian dogs (komainu) on either side of the second torii were made by a Showa period stone mason named Heikichi Iizuka. The path to the shrine is lined with camellia, tabunoki, and sudajii trees, forming a broadleaf forest that is designated a Natural Monument by Ibaraki Prefecture. The original shrine site is believed to be near the first torii, around the ruins of Hikantei. It is closely linked to [[Oarai Isosaki Shrine]] which also worships [[Sukunabikona]].{{Cite book |last1=Cali |first1=Joseph |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=J1gEEAAAQBAJ&dq=Oarai+Isosaki+Shrine&pg=PA73 |title=Shinto Shrines: A Guide to the Sacred Sites of Japan's Ancient Religion |last2=Dougill |first2=John |date=2012-11-30 |publisher=University of Hawaii Press |isbn=978-0-8248-3775-4 |language=en}}{{Cite web |title=A Study of Shinto: The Religion of the Japanese Nation |url=https://www.routledge.com/A-Study-of-Shinto-The-Religion-of-the-Japanese-Nation/Katu/p/book/9780415845762 |access-date=2023-11-18 |website=Routledge & CRC Press |language=en}}{{Rp|page=29}} ==Overview== {{神社 |名称 = Sakattsura Isosaki Shrine |画像 = [[File:Sajatsura Isosaki Jinja Shaden.jpg|270px]]

Plaque "Sakattsura Isosaki Shrine" written by [[Prince Komatsu Akihito]]]] '''Sakattsura Isosaki Shrine''' (さかつらいそさきじんじゃ) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Hitachinaka City]], [[Ibaraki Prefecture]]. It is classified as a [[Myōjin Taisha|Myōjin Taisha]] under the [[Engishiki|Engishiki system]]. The former shrine rank was [[National Middle Shrine|Kokuhei Chūsha]], and it is now a [[Bekkaku Shrine]] under the [[Association of Shinto Shrines]]. == Overview == The shrine is situated on a hill facing the [[Pacific Ocean]] in eastern [[Ibaraki Prefecture]]. It is closely related to [[Ōarai Isosaki Shrine]] in [[Ōarai Town]] across the [[Naka River]], and the two shrines form a single faith. == Deities == '''Main Deity''' * '''[[Sukunahikona no Mikoto]]''' (少彦名命) *: Known for helping [[Ōnamuchi no Mikoto]] (Ōkuninushi no Mikoto) in creating the land. '''Enshrined Deity''' * [[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi no Mikoto]] (大名持命) *: Another name for [[Ōkuninushi no Mikoto]] (大己貴命), the deity of [[Ōarai Isosaki Shrine]], and his divided spirit. He is said to have created the land with the help of Sukunahikona no Mikoto. In the myths found in the [[Kojiki]], [[Nihon Shoki]], and [[Fudoki]], these two deities often appear together in the stories of land creation. Many shrines enshrine this combination of deities. At this shrine, Sukunahikona no Mikoto is also considered [[Ebisu]] of the [[Seven Lucky Gods]], and Ōnamuchi no Mikoto is considered [[Daikokuten]]. == History == === Founding === According to the [[Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku]], a deity appeared at Ōarai Isosaki in [[Kashima District, Hitachi Province]] in Saikō 3rd year (856). {{quotation| Hitachi Province reports that a new deity has descended at Ōarai Isosaki in Kashima District. Initially, a salt maker saw a shining light in the sea at midnight. The next day, two strange stones appeared on the shore, each about a foot high. The following day, more than twenty small stones appeared around the strange stones, resembling attendants. The stones were vividly colored and shaped like monks, but without ears or eyes. The divine spirit possessed a person and said, "I am Ōnamuchi and Sukunahikona. We finished creating this land and went to the eastern sea, but we have returned to save the people." |Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku, Saikō 3rd year, December戊戌条}} Thus, Ōkuninushi no Mikoto (Ōnamuchi) was enshrined at Ōarai, and Sukunahikona no Mikoto was enshrined at Sakattsura, marking the founding of the two shrines. The rock formations along the coast near the shrine are tilted about 45 degrees to the south, and the part that tilts to the north is called "Gyaku-retsu" (逆列, Reverse Row), which is said to be the origin of the shrine's name. Later, it came to be known as "Sakattsura" because it enshrined the god of sake (alcohol)[http://www.oyashiro.or.jp/link/0006.html Sakattsura Isosaki Shrine] (Ibaraki Prefecture Shrine Office). === Historical Overview === The [[Engishiki Jinmyocho]] lists the shrine as "Hitachi Province Naka District Sakattsura Isosaki Yakushi Bosatsu Shrine" and classifies it as a Myōjin Taisha. The shrine fell into decline during the [[Middle Ages]] and lost its buildings. In the [[Early Modern Period]], the second lord of the [[Mito Domain]], [[Tokugawa Mitsukuni]], initiated the rebuilding of the shrine, and the third lord, [[Tokugawa Tsunaeda]], relocated and restored it to its current location. The old site is said to be near the first torii. In 1885 (Meiji 18), the shrine was ranked as a [[National Middle Shrine|Kokuhei Chūsha]] under the [[Modern Shrine Rank System]]. It is now officially named "Sakattsura Isosaki Shrine." === Shrine Rankings === * [[Ten'an]] 1st year (857), August 7 - Received official shrine status (Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku) * Ten'an 1st year (857), October 15 - Granted the title "Yakushi Bosatsu Myōjin" (Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku) == Grounds == The carving of a squirrel and grapes on the front of the haiden is said to be the work of [[Hidari Jingorō]]. The guardian dogs (komainu) on either side of the second torii were made by a Showa period stone mason named Heikichi Iizuka. The path to the shrine is lined with camellia, tabunoki, and sudajii trees, forming a broadleaf forest that is designated a Natural Monument by Ibaraki Prefecture. The original shrine site is believed to be near the first torii, around the ruins of Hikantei. Designated in 2005. == Location Information == '''Location''' * [[Ibaraki Prefecture]], [[Hitachinaka City]], Isosaki Town 4607-2 '''Transportation Access''' * Nearest station: [[Hitachinaka Seaside Railway]], [[Hitachinaka Seaside Railway Minato Line|Minato Line]], [[Ajigaura Station]] (about 15 minutes on foot) - The terminal station of the Minato Line. '''Nearby''' * Ruins of Hikantei - Ruins of a pavilion built by the Mito Domain. Designated a Historic Site by Hitachinaka City. * Kanto Place - A scenic spot selected by the lords of the Mito Domain. Designated a Scenic Spot by Hitachinaka City. * Kawagozuka Kofun - Designated a Historic Site by Hitachinaka City. * Hiraiso Cretaceous Layer - Nearby coast. Designated a Natural Monument by Ibaraki Prefecture. == References == {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist}} == Related Books == * Anzu Moto, Umeda Yoshihiko, editors and supervisors, "Shinto Dictionary", [[Shinto Shinpōsha]], 1968, p. 31 * [[Eiji Shirai]], Toki Masakuni, editors, "Shrine Dictionary", [[Tōkyōdō Shuppan]], 1979, pp. 154-155 * Ueyama Haruhira, others, "Japan Shrine General Overview", [[Shin Jinbutsu Ōraisha]], 1992, pp. 68-69 * "Shinto no Hon", [[Gakken]], 1992, p. 213 == Related Articles == * [[Yakuojin]] * [[Horide Shrine (Hitachinaka City)]] == External Links == * [http://sakatura.org/ Sakattsura Isosaki Shrine] (Official Site) * [http://www.oyashiro.or.jp/link/0006.html Sakattsura Isosaki Shrine] (Ibaraki Prefecture Shrine Office) * [http://21coe.kokugakuin.ac.jp/db/jinja/206002.html Sakatsura Isosaki Yakushi Bosatsu Shrine] (Kokugakuin University 21st Century COE Program "Shinto and Shrine Historical Materials Collection") {{Shinto Shrines in Ibaraki Prefecture}} {{Normdaten}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Sakattsura Isosaki Shrine}} [[Category:Shinto shrines in Ibaraki Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Hitachinaka City]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Hitachinaka City]] [[Category:Myōjin Taisha]] [[Category:Historic Sites in Hitachi Province]] [[Category:National Middle Shrine]] [[Category:Ibaraki 100 Landscapes]] == See also == * [[Ichinomiya]] * [[Kanpei-taisha]] == References == {{reflist}} [[Category:Beppyo shrines]] [[Category:Myōjin Taisha]] [[Category:Kokuhei Chūsha]] [[en:Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine]][[en:Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine]]

[2], x, 488 p. 6 pl. (1 col), 13 fold. maps, 12 fold. plans |last2=Railways |first2=Japan Dept of |date=1914 |language=en}} It is a [[Beppyo shrine]]. It is also a {{ill|Myojin Taisha|ja|名神大社}} in the [[Engishiki]]. It was founded in 856. [[File:酒列磯前神社_一の鳥居.JPG|thumb|200x200px| The shrine's first [[Torii]] gate]] It enshrines [[Sukunabikona]]. It is closely linked to [[Oarai Isosaki Shrine]] which also worships [[Sukunabikona]].{{Cite book |last1=Cali |first1=Joseph |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=J1gEEAAAQBAJ&dq=Oarai+Isosaki+Shrine&pg=PA73 |title=Shinto Shrines: A Guide to the Sacred Sites of Japan's Ancient Religion |last2=Dougill |first2=John |date=2012-11-30 |publisher=University of Hawaii Press |isbn=978-0-8248-3775-4 |language=en}}{{Cite web |title=A Study of Shinto: The Religion of the Japanese Nation |url=https://www.routledge.com/A-Study-of-Shinto-The-Religion-of-the-Japanese-Nation/Katu/p/book/9780415845762 |access-date=2023-11-18 |website=Routledge & CRC Press |language=en}}{{Rp|page=29}} ==Overview== {{神社 |名称 = Sakattsura Isosaki Shrine |画像 = [[File:Sajatsura Isosaki Jinja Shaden.jpg|270px]]
Haiden {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=12|frame-align=center|frame-width=270|coord={{coord|36|22|56.5|N|140|37|24.5|E}}}} |所在地 = [[Ibaraki Prefecture]], [[Hitachinaka City]], Isosaki Town 4607-2 |緯度度 = 36 | 緯度分 = 22 | 緯度秒 = 56.5 | N(北緯)及びS(南緯) = N |経度度 = 140 |経度分 = 37 | 経度秒 = 24.5 | E(東経)及びW(西経) = E |ラベル位置=left |祭神 = [[Sukunabikona|Sukunahikona no Mikoto]] |社格 = [[式内社]]（[[Myōjin Taisha|Myōjin Taisha]]）

Plaque "Sakattsura Isosaki Shrine" written by [[Prince Komatsu Akihito]]]] '''Sakattsura Isosaki Shrine''' (さかつらいそさきじんじゃ) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Hitachinaka City]], [[Ibaraki Prefecture]]. It is classified as a [[Myōjin Taisha|Myōjin Taisha]] under the [[Engishiki|Engishiki system]]. The former shrine rank was [[National Middle Shrine|Kokuhei Chūsha]], and it is now a [[Bekkaku Shrine]] under the [[Association of Shinto Shrines]]. == Overview == The shrine is situated on a hill facing the [[Pacific Ocean]] in eastern [[Ibaraki Prefecture]]. It is closely related to [[Ōarai Isosaki Shrine]] in [[Ōarai Town]] across the [[Naka River]], and the two shrines form a single faith. == Deities == '''Main deity''' * '''[[Sukunahikona no Mikoto]]''' (少彦名命) *: Known for helping [[Ōnamuchi no Mikoto]] (Ōkuninushi no Mikoto) in creating the land. '''Enshrined deity''' * [[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi no Mikoto]] (大名持命) *: Another name for [[Ōkuninushi no Mikoto]] (大己貴命), the deity of [[Ōarai Isosaki Shrine]], and his divided spirit. He is said to have created the land with the help of Sukunahikona no Mikoto. In the myths found in the [[Kojiki]], [[Nihon Shoki]], and [[Fudoki]], these two deities often appear together in the stories of land creation. Many shrines enshrine this combination of deities. At this shrine, Sukunahikona no Mikoto is also considered [[Ebisu]] of the [[Seven Lucky Gods]], and Ōnamuchi no Mikoto is considered [[Daikokuten]]. == History == === Founding === According to the [[Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku]], a deity appeared at Ōarai Isosaki in [[Kashima District, Hitachi Province]] in Saikō 3rd year (856). {{quotation| Hitachi Province reports that a new deity has descended at Ōarai Isosaki in Kashima District. Initially, a salt maker saw a shining light in the sea at midnight. The next day, two strange stones appeared on the shore, each about a foot high. The following day, more than twenty small stones appeared around the strange stones, resembling attendants. The stones were vividly colored and shaped like monks, but without ears or eyes. The divine spirit possessed a person and said, "I am Ōnamuchi and Sukunahikona. We finished creating this land and went to the eastern sea, but we have returned to save the people." |Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku, Saikō 3rd year, December戊戌条}} Thus, Ōkuninushi no Mikoto (Ōnamuchi) was enshrined at Ōarai, and Sukunahikona no Mikoto was enshrined at Sakattsura, marking the founding of the two shrines. The rock formations along the coast near the shrine are tilted about 45 degrees to the south, and the part that tilts to the north is called "Gyaku-retsu" (逆列, Reverse Row), which is said to be the origin of the shrine's name. Later, it came to be known as "Sakattsura" because it enshrined the god of sake (alcohol)[http://www.oyashiro.or.jp/link/0006.html Sakattsura Isosaki Shrine] (Ibaraki Prefecture Shrine Office). === Historical Overview === The [[Engishiki Jinmyocho]] lists the shrine as "Hitachi Province Naka District Sakattsura Isosaki Yakushi Bosatsu Shrine" and classifies it as a Myōjin Taisha. The shrine fell into decline during the [[Middle Ages]] and lost its buildings. In the [[Early Modern Period]], the second lord of the [[Mito Domain]], [[Tokugawa Mitsukuni]], initiated the rebuilding of the shrine, and the third lord, [[Tokugawa Tsunaeda]], relocated and restored it to its current location. The old site is said to be near the first torii. In 1885 (Meiji 18), the shrine was ranked as a [[National Middle Shrine|Kokuhei Chūsha]] under the [[Modern Shrine Rank System]]. It is now officially named "Sakattsura Isosaki Shrine." === Shrine Rankings === * [[Ten'an]] 1st year (857), August 7 - Received official shrine status (Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku) * Ten'an 1st year (857), October 15 - Granted the title "Yakushi Bosatsu Myōjin" (Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku) == Grounds == The carving of a squirrel and grapes on the front of the haiden is said to be the work of [[Hidari Jingorō]]. The guardian dogs (komainu) on either side of the second torii were made by a Showa period stone mason named Heikichi Iizuka. The path to the shrine is lined with camellia, tabunoki, and sudajii trees, forming a broadleaf forest that is designated a Natural Monument by Ibaraki Prefecture. The original shrine site is believed to be near the first torii, around the ruins of Hikantei. File:Sakattsura Isosaki Shrine Main Hall.JPG|Main Hall File:Sakattsura Isosaki Shrine Worship Hall.JPG|Worship Hall File:Sakattsura Isosaki Shrine Stone where Tokugawa Nariaki sat.JPG|Stone where [[Tokugawa Nariaki]] sat File:Sakattsura Isosaki Shrine Second Torii.JPG|Second Torii File:Sakattsura Isosaki Shrine Approach.JPG|Approach (Prefectural Natural Monument) == Auxiliary Shrines == [[File:Sakattsura Chinjusha (Auxiliary Shrine of Sakattsura Isosaki Shrine).JPG|thumb|200px|Sakattsura Chinjusha]] [[File:Sakattsura Isosaki Shrine Auxiliary Shrines.JPG|thumb|200px|Five Auxiliary Shrines]] * Sakattsura Chinjusha (さかつらちんれいしゃ) ** Enshrined deity: 506 war dead from the [[Russo-Japanese War]] to [[World War II]] *: Located north of the main hall. * Inari Shrine - Enshrined deity: [[Ukanomitama|Ukanomitama no Mikoto]] * Tenmangū - Enshrined deity: [[Sugawara no Michizane]] * Kotohira Shrine - Enshrined deity: [[Ōmononushi no Mikoto]] * Fuji Shrine - Enshrined deity: [[Konohanasakuya-hime]], worshipped as a deity of safe childbirth. * Water Shrine - Enshrined deity: [[Mizuhanome|Mizuhanome no Mikoto]] == Cultural Properties == === Ibaraki Prefecture Designated Natural Monument === * Sakattsura Isosaki Shrine Tree Grove - The broadleaf forest of camellia, tabunoki, and sudajii trees along the approach and surrounding the grounds. Designated in 2005. == Location Information == '''Location''' * [[Ibaraki Prefecture]], [[Hitachinaka City]], Isosaki Town 4607-2 '''Transportation Access''' * Nearest station: [[Hitachinaka Seaside Railway]], [[Hitachinaka Seaside Railway Minato Line|Minato Line]], [[Ajigaura Station]] (about 15 minutes on foot) - The terminal station of the Minato Line. '''Nearby''' * Ruins of Hikantei - Ruins of a pavilion built by the Mito Domain. Designated a Historic Site by Hitachinaka City. * Kanto Place - A scenic spot selected by the lords of the Mito Domain. Designated a Scenic Spot by Hitachinaka City. * Kawagozuka Kofun - Designated a Historic Site by Hitachinaka City. * Hiraiso Cretaceous Layer - Nearby coast. Designated a Natural Monument by Ibaraki Prefecture. == References == {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist}} == Related Books == * Anzu Moto, Umeda Yoshihiko, editors and supervisors, "Shinto Dictionary", [[Shinto Shinpōsha]], 1968, p. 31 * [[Eiji Shirai]], Toki Masakuni, editors, "Shrine Dictionary", [[Tōkyōdō Shuppan]], 1979, pp. 154-155 * Ueyama Haruhira, others, "Japan Shrine General Overview", [[Shin Jinbutsu Ōraisha]], 1992, pp. 68-69 * "Shinto no Hon", [[Gakken]], 1992, p. 213 == Related Articles == * [[Yakuojin]] * [[Horide Shrine (Hitachinaka City)]] == External Links == * [http://sakatura.org/ Sakattsura Isosaki Shrine] (Official Site) * [http://www.oyashiro.or.jp/link/0006.html Sakattsura Isosaki Shrine] (Ibaraki Prefecture Shrine Office) * [http://21coe.kokugakuin.ac.jp/db/jinja/206002.html Sakatsura Isosaki Yakushi Bosatsu Shrine] (Kokugakuin University 21st Century COE Program "Shinto and Shrine Historical Materials Collection") {{Shinto Shrines in Ibaraki Prefecture}} {{Normdaten}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Sakattsura Isosaki Shrine}} [[Category:Shinto shrines in Ibaraki Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Hitachinaka City]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Hitachinaka City]] [[Category:Myōjin Taisha]] [[Category:Historic Sites in Hitachi Province]] [[Category:National Middle Shrine]] [[Category:Ibaraki 100 Landscapes]] == See also == * [[Ichinomiya]] * [[Kanpei-taisha]] == References == {{reflist}} [[Category:Beppyo shrines]] [[Category:Myōjin Taisha]] [[Category:Kokuhei Chūsha]] [[Category:Pages and Categories from wikipedia5]][[en:Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine]][[Category:Pages and Categories from wikipedia5]] [[en:Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine]][[en:Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine]]

[2], x, 488 p. 6 pl. (1 col), 13 fold. maps, 12 fold. plans |last2=Railways |first2=Japan Dept of |date=1914 |language=en}} It is a [[Beppyo shrine]]. It is also a {{ill|Myojin Taisha|ja|名神大社}} in the [[Engishiki]]. It was founded in 856. [[File:酒列磯前神社_一の鳥居.JPG|thumb|200x200px| The shrine's first [[Torii]] gate]] It enshrines [[Sukunabikona]]. It is closely linked to [[Oarai Isosaki Shrine]] which also worships [[Sukunabikona]].{{Cite book |last1=Cali |first1=Joseph |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=J1gEEAAAQBAJ&dq=Oarai+Isosaki+Shrine&pg=PA73 |title=Shinto Shrines: A Guide to the Sacred Sites of Japan's Ancient Religion |last2=Dougill |first2=John |date=2012-11-30 |publisher=University of Hawaii Press |isbn=978-0-8248-3775-4 |language=en}}{{Cite web |title=A Study of Shinto: The Religion of the Japanese Nation |url=https://www.routledge.com/A-Study-of-Shinto-The-Religion-of-the-Japanese-Nation/Katu/p/book/9780415845762 |access-date=2023-11-18 |website=Routledge & CRC Press |language=en}}{{Rp|page=29}} ==Overview== {{神社 |名称 = Sakattsura Isosaki Shrine |画像 = [[File:Sajatsura Isosaki Jinja Shaden.jpg|270px]]

Plaque "Sakattsura Isosaki Shrine" written by [[Prince Komatsu Akihito]]]] '''Sakattsura Isosaki Shrine''' (さかつらいそさきじんじゃ) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Hitachinaka City]], [[Ibaraki Prefecture]]. It is classified as a [[Myōjin Taisha|Myōjin Taisha]] under the [[Engishiki|Engishiki system]]. The former shrine rank was [[National Middle Shrine|Kokuhei Chūsha]], and it is now a [[Bekkaku Shrine]] under the [[Association of Shinto Shrines]]. == Overview == The shrine is situated on a hill facing the [[Pacific Ocean]] in eastern [[Ibaraki Prefecture]]. It is closely related to [[Ōarai Isosaki Shrine]] in [[Ōarai Town]] across the [[Naka River]], and the two shrines form a single faith. == Deities == '''Main deity''' * '''[[Sukunahikona no Mikoto]]''' (少彦名命) *: Known for helping [[Ōnamuchi no Mikoto]] (Ōkuninushi no Mikoto) in creating the land. '''Enshrined deity''' * [[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi no Mikoto]] (大名持命) *: Another name for [[Ōkuninushi no Mikoto]] (大己貴命), the deity of [[Ōarai Isosaki Shrine]], and his divided spirit. He is said to have created the land with the help of Sukunahikona no Mikoto. In the myths found in the [[Kojiki]], [[Nihon Shoki]], and [[Fudoki]], these two deities often appear together in the stories of land creation. Many shrines enshrine this combination of deities. At this shrine, Sukunahikona no Mikoto is also considered [[Ebisu]] of the [[Seven Lucky Gods]], and Ōnamuchi no Mikoto is considered [[Daikokuten]]. == History == === Founding === According to the [[Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku]], a deity appeared at Ōarai Isosaki in [[Kashima District, Hitachi Province]] in Saikō 3rd year (856). {{quotation| Hitachi Province reports that a new deity has descended at Ōarai Isosaki in Kashima District. Initially, a salt maker saw a shining light in the sea at midnight. The next day, two strange stones appeared on the shore, each about a foot high. The following day, more than twenty small stones appeared around the strange stones, resembling attendants. The stones were vividly colored and shaped like monks, but without ears or eyes. The divine spirit possessed a person and said, "I am Ōnamuchi and Sukunahikona. We finished creating this land and went to the eastern sea, but we have returned to save the people." |Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku, Saikō 3rd year, December戊戌条}} Thus, Ōkuninushi no Mikoto (Ōnamuchi) was enshrined at Ōarai, and Sukunahikona no Mikoto was enshrined at Sakattsura, marking the founding of the two shrines. The rock formations along the coast near the shrine are tilted about 45 degrees to the south, and the part that tilts to the north is called "Gyaku-retsu" (逆列, Reverse Row), which is said to be the origin of the shrine's name. Later, it came to be known as "Sakattsura" because it enshrined the god of sake (alcohol)[http://www.oyashiro.or.jp/link/0006.html Sakattsura Isosaki Shrine] (Ibaraki Prefecture Shrine Office). === Historical Overview === The [[Engishiki Jinmyocho]] lists the shrine as "Hitachi Province Naka District Sakattsura Isosaki Yakushi Bosatsu Shrine" and classifies it as a Myōjin Taisha. The shrine fell into decline during the [[Middle Ages]] and lost its buildings. In the [[Early Modern Period]], the second lord of the [[Mito Domain]], [[Tokugawa Mitsukuni]], initiated the rebuilding of the shrine, and the third lord, [[Tokugawa Tsunaeda]], relocated and restored it to its current location. The old site is said to be near the first torii. In 1885 (Meiji 18), the shrine was ranked as a [[National Middle Shrine|Kokuhei Chūsha]] under the [[Modern Shrine rank System]]. It is now officially named "Sakattsura Isosaki Shrine." === Shrine rankings === * [[Ten'an]] 1st year (857), August 7 - Received official shrine status (Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku) * Ten'an 1st year (857), October 15 - Granted the title "Yakushi Bosatsu Myōjin" (Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku) == Grounds == The carving of a squirrel and grapes on the front of the haiden is said to be the work of [[Hidari Jingorō]]. The guardian dogs (komainu) on either side of the second torii were made by a Showa period stone mason named Heikichi Iizuka. The path to the shrine is lined with camellia, tabunoki, and sudajii trees, forming a broadleaf forest that is designated a Natural Monument by Ibaraki Prefecture. The original shrine site is believed to be near the first torii, around the ruins of Hikantei. File:Sakattsura Isosaki Shrine main hall.JPG|main hall File:Sakattsura Isosaki Shrine Worship Hall.JPG|Worship Hall File:Sakattsura Isosaki Shrine Stone where Tokugawa Nariaki sat.JPG|Stone where [[Tokugawa Nariaki]] sat File:Sakattsura Isosaki Shrine Second Torii.JPG|Second Torii File:Sakattsura Isosaki Shrine Approach.JPG|Approach (Prefectural Natural Monument) == Auxiliary Shrines == [[File:Sakattsura Chinjusha (Auxiliary Shrine of Sakattsura Isosaki Shrine).JPG|thumb|200px|Sakattsura Chinjusha]] [[File:Sakattsura Isosaki Shrine Auxiliary Shrines.JPG|thumb|200px|Five Auxiliary Shrines]] * Sakattsura Chinjusha (さかつらちんれいしゃ) ** Enshrined deity: 506 war dead from the [[Russo-Japanese War]] to [[World War II]] *: Located north of the main hall. * Inari Shrine - Enshrined deity: [[Ukanomitama|Ukanomitama no Mikoto]] * Tenmangū - Enshrined deity: [[Sugawara no Michizane]] * Kotohira Shrine - Enshrined deity: [[Ōmononushi no Mikoto]] * Fuji Shrine - Enshrined deity: [[Konohanasakuya-hime]], worshipped as a deity of safe childbirth. * Water Shrine - Enshrined deity: [[Mizuhanome|Mizuhanome no Mikoto]] == Cultural Properties == === Ibaraki Prefecture Designated Natural Monument === * Sakattsura Isosaki Shrine Tree Grove - The broadleaf forest of camellia, tabunoki, and sudajii trees along the approach and surrounding the grounds. Designated in 2005. == location Information == '''location''' * [[Ibaraki Prefecture]], [[Hitachinaka City]], Isosaki Town 4607-2 '''Transportation Access''' * Nearest station: [[Hitachinaka Seaside Railway]], [[Hitachinaka Seaside Railway Minato Line|Minato Line]], [[Ajigaura Station]] (about 15 minutes on foot) - The terminal station of the Minato Line. '''Nearby''' * Ruins of Hikantei - Ruins of a pavilion built by the Mito Domain. Designated a Historic Site by Hitachinaka City. * Kanto Place - A scenic spot selected by the lords of the Mito Domain. Designated a Scenic Spot by Hitachinaka City. * Kawagozuka Kofun - Designated a Historic Site by Hitachinaka City. * Hiraiso Cretaceous Layer - Nearby coast. Designated a Natural Monument by Ibaraki Prefecture. == References == {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist}} == Related Books == * Anzu Moto, Umeda Yoshihiko, editors and supervisors, "Shinto Dictionary", [[Shinto Shinpōsha]], 1968, p. 31 * [[Eiji Shirai]], Toki Masakuni, editors, "Shrine Dictionary", [[Tōkyōdō Shuppan]], 1979, pp. 154-155 * Ueyama Haruhira, others, "Japan Shrine General Overview", [[Shin Jinbutsu Ōraisha]], 1992, pp. 68-69 * "Shinto no Hon", [[Gakken]], 1992, p. 213 == Related Articles == * [[Yakuojin]] * [[Horide Shrine (Hitachinaka City)]] == External Links == * [http://sakatura.org/ Sakattsura Isosaki Shrine] (Official Site) * [http://www.oyashiro.or.jp/link/0006.html Sakattsura Isosaki Shrine] (Ibaraki Prefecture Shrine Office) * [http://21coe.kokugakuin.ac.jp/db/jinja/206002.html Sakatsura Isosaki Yakushi Bosatsu Shrine] (Kokugakuin University 21st Century COE Program "Shinto and Shrine Historical Materials Collection") {{Shinto Shrines in Ibaraki Prefecture}} {{Normdaten}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Sakattsura Isosaki Shrine}} [[Category:Shinto shrines in Ibaraki Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Hitachinaka City]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Hitachinaka City]] [[Category:Myōjin Taisha]] [[Category:Historic Sites in Hitachi Province]] [[Category:National Middle Shrine]] [[Category:Ibaraki 100 Landscapes]] == See also == * [[Ichinomiya]] * [[Kanpei-taisha]] == References == {{reflist}} [[Category:Beppyo shrines]] [[Category:Myōjin Taisha]] [[Category:Kokuhei Chūsha]] [[Category:Pages and Categories from wikipedia5]][[en:Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine]][[Category:Pages and Categories from wikipedia5]] [[en:Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine]][[en:Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine]]

[2], x, 488 p. 6 pl. (1 col), 13 fold. maps, 12 fold. plans |last2=Railways |first2=Japan Dept of |date=1914 |language=en}} It is a [[Beppyo shrine]]. It is also a {{ill|Myojin Taisha|ja|名神大社}} in the [[Engishiki]]. It was founded in 856. [[File:酒列磯前神社_一の鳥居.JPG|thumb|200x200px| The shrine's first [[Torii]] gate]] It enshrines [[Sukunabikona]]. It is closely linked to [[Oarai Isosaki Shrine]] which also worships [[Sukunabikona]].{{Cite book |last1=Cali |first1=Joseph |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=J1gEEAAAQBAJ&dq=Oarai+Isosaki+Shrine&pg=PA73 |title=Shinto Shrines: A Guide to the Sacred Sites of Japan's Ancient Religion |last2=Dougill |first2=John |date=2012-11-30 |publisher=University of Hawaii Press |isbn=978-0-8248-3775-4 |language=en}}{{Cite web |title=A Study of Shinto: The Religion of the Japanese Nation |url=https://www.routledge.com/A-Study-of-Shinto-The-Religion-of-the-Japanese-Nation/Katu/p/book/9780415845762 |access-date=2023-11-18 |website=Routledge & CRC Press |language=en}}{{Rp|page=29}} ==Overview== {{神社 |名称 = Sakattsura Isosaki Shrine |画像 = [[File:Sajatsura Isosaki Jinja Shaden.jpg|270px]]

Plaque "Sakattsura Isosaki Shrine" written by [[Prince Komatsu Akihito]]]] '''Sakattsura Isosaki Shrine''' (さかつらいそさきじんじゃ) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Hitachinaka City]], [[Ibaraki Prefecture]]. It is classified as a [[Myōjin Taisha|Myōjin Taisha]] under the [[Engishiki|Engishiki system]]. The former shrine rank was [[National Middle Shrine|Kokuhei Chūsha]], and it is now a [[Bekkaku Shrine]] under the [[Association of Shinto Shrines]]. == Overview == The shrine is situated on a hill facing the [[Pacific Ocean]] in eastern [[Ibaraki Prefecture]]. It is closely related to [[Ōarai Isosaki Shrine]] in [[Ōarai Town]] across the [[Naka River]], and the two shrines form a single faith. == Deities == '''Main deity''' * '''[[Sukunahikona no Mikoto]]''' (少彦名命) *: Known for helping [[Ōnamuchi no Mikoto]] (Ōkuninushi no Mikoto) in creating the land. '''Enshrined deity''' * [[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi no Mikoto]] (大名持命) *: Another name for [[Ōkuninushi no Mikoto]] (大己貴命), the deity of [[Ōarai Isosaki Shrine]], and his divided spirit. He is said to have created the land with the help of Sukunahikona no Mikoto. In the myths found in the [[Kojiki]], [[Nihon Shoki]], and [[Fudoki]], these two deities often appear together in the stories of land creation. Many shrines enshrine this combination of deities. At this shrine, Sukunahikona no Mikoto is also considered [[Ebisu]] of the [[Seven Lucky Gods]], and Ōnamuchi no Mikoto is considered [[Daikokuten]]. == History == === Founding === According to the [[Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku]], a deity appeared at Ōarai Isosaki in [[Kashima District, Hitachi Province]] in Saikō 3rd year (856). {{quotation| Hitachi Province reports that a new deity has descended at Ōarai Isosaki in Kashima District. Initially, a salt maker saw a shining light in the sea at midnight. The next day, two strange stones appeared on the shore, each about a foot high. The following day, more than twenty small stones appeared around the strange stones, resembling attendants. The stones were vividly colored and shaped like monks, but without ears or eyes. The divine spirit possessed a person and said, "I am Ōnamuchi and Sukunahikona. We finished creating this land and went to the eastern sea, but we have returned to save the people." |Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku, Saikō 3rd year, December戊戌条}} Thus, Ōkuninushi no Mikoto (Ōnamuchi) was enshrined at Ōarai, and Sukunahikona no Mikoto was enshrined at Sakattsura, marking the founding of the two shrines. The rock formations along the coast near the shrine are tilted about 45 degrees to the south, and the part that tilts to the north is called "Gyaku-retsu" (逆列, Reverse Row), which is said to be the origin of the shrine's name. Later, it came to be known as "Sakattsura" because it enshrined the god of sake (alcohol)[http://www.oyashiro.or.jp/link/0006.html Sakattsura Isosaki Shrine] (Ibaraki Prefecture Shrine Office). === Historical Overview === The [[Engishiki Jinmyocho]] lists the shrine as "Hitachi Province Naka District Sakattsura Isosaki Yakushi Bosatsu Shrine" and classifies it as a Myōjin Taisha. The shrine fell into decline during the [[Middle Ages]] and lost its buildings. In the [[Early Modern Period]], the second lord of the [[Mito Domain]], [[Tokugawa Mitsukuni]], initiated the rebuilding of the shrine, and the third lord, [[Tokugawa Tsunaeda]], relocated and restored it to its current location. The old site is said to be near the first torii. In 1885 (Meiji 18), the shrine was ranked as a [[National Middle Shrine|Kokuhei Chūsha]] under the [[Modern Shrine rank System]]. It is now officially named "Sakattsura Isosaki Shrine." === Shrine rankings === * [[Ten'an]] 1st year (857), August 7 - Received official shrine status (Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku) * Ten'an 1st year (857), October 15 - Granted the title "Yakushi Bosatsu Myōjin" (Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku) == Grounds == The carving of a squirrel and grapes on the front of the haiden is said to be the work of [[Hidari Jingorō]]. The guardian dogs (komainu) on either side of the second torii were made by a Showa period stone mason named Heikichi Iizuka. The path to the shrine is lined with camellia, tabunoki, and sudajii trees, forming a broadleaf forest that is designated a Natural Monument by Ibaraki Prefecture. The original shrine site is believed to be near the first torii, around the ruins of Hikantei. File:Sakattsura Isosaki Shrine main hall.JPG|main hall File:Sakattsura Isosaki Shrine Worship Hall.JPG|Worship Hall File:Sakattsura Isosaki Shrine Stone where Tokugawa Nariaki sat.JPG|Stone where [[Tokugawa Nariaki]] sat File:Sakattsura Isosaki Shrine Second Torii.JPG|Second Torii File:Sakattsura Isosaki Shrine Approach.JPG|Approach (Prefectural Natural Monument) == Auxiliary Shrines == [[File:Sakattsura Chinjusha (Auxiliary Shrine of Sakattsura Isosaki Shrine).JPG|thumb|200px|Sakattsura Chinjusha]] [[File:Sakattsura Isosaki Shrine Auxiliary Shrines.JPG|thumb|200px|Five Auxiliary Shrines]] * Sakattsura Chinjusha (さかつらちんれいしゃ) ** Enshrined deity: 506 war dead from the [[Russo-Japanese War]] to [[World War II]] *: Located north of the main hall. * Inari Shrine - Enshrined deity: [[Ukanomitama|Ukanomitama no Mikoto]] * Tenmangū - Enshrined deity: [[Sugawara no Michizane]] * Kotohira Shrine - Enshrined deity: [[Ōmononushi no Mikoto]] * Fuji Shrine - Enshrined deity: [[Konohanasakuya-hime]], worshipped as a deity of safe childbirth. * Water Shrine - Enshrined deity: [[Mizuhanome|Mizuhanome no Mikoto]] == Cultural Properties == === Ibaraki Prefecture Designated Natural Monument === * Sakattsura Isosaki Shrine Tree Grove - The broadleaf forest of camellia, tabunoki, and sudajii trees along the approach and surrounding the grounds. Designated in 2005. == location Information == '''location''' * [[Ibaraki Prefecture]], [[Hitachinaka City]], Isosaki Town 4607-2 '''Transportation Access''' * Nearest station: [[Hitachinaka Seaside Railway]], [[Hitachinaka Seaside Railway Minato Line|Minato Line]], [[Ajigaura Station]] (about 15 minutes on foot) - The terminal station of the Minato Line. '''Nearby''' * Ruins of Hikantei - Ruins of a pavilion built by the Mito Domain. Designated a Historic Site by Hitachinaka City. * Kanto Place - A scenic spot selected by the lords of the Mito Domain. Designated a Scenic Spot by Hitachinaka City. * Kawagozuka Kofun - Designated a Historic Site by Hitachinaka City. * Hiraiso Cretaceous Layer - Nearby coast. Designated a Natural Monument by Ibaraki Prefecture. == References == {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist}} == Related Books == * Anzu Moto, Umeda Yoshihiko, editors and supervisors, "Shinto Dictionary", [[Shinto Shinpōsha]], 1968, p. 31 * [[Eiji Shirai]], Toki Masakuni, editors, "Shrine Dictionary", [[Tōkyōdō Shuppan]], 1979, pp. 154-155 * Ueyama Haruhira, others, "Japan Shrine General Overview", [[Shin Jinbutsu Ōraisha]], 1992, pp. 68-69 * "Shinto no Hon", [[Gakken]], 1992, p. 213 == Related Articles == * [[Yakuojin]] * [[Horide Shrine (Hitachinaka City)]] == External Links == * [http://sakatura.org/ Sakattsura Isosaki Shrine] (Official Site) * [http://www.oyashiro.or.jp/link/0006.html Sakattsura Isosaki Shrine] (Ibaraki Prefecture Shrine Office) * [http://21coe.kokugakuin.ac.jp/db/jinja/206002.html Sakatsura Isosaki Yakushi Bosatsu Shrine] (Kokugakuin University 21st Century COE Program "Shinto and Shrine Historical Materials Collection") {{Shinto Shrines in Ibaraki Prefecture}} {{Normdaten}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Sakattsura Isosaki Shrine}} [[Category:Shinto shrines in Ibaraki Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Hitachinaka City]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Hitachinaka City]] [[Category:Myōjin Taisha]] [[Category:Historic Sites in Hitachi Province]] [[Category:National Middle Shrine]] [[Category:Ibaraki 100 Landscapes]] == See also == * [[Ichinomiya]] * [[Kanpei-taisha]] == References == {{reflist}} [[Category:Beppyo shrines]] [[Category:Myōjin Taisha]] [[Category:Kokuhei Chūsha]] [[Category:Pages and Categories from wikipedia5]][[en:Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine]][[Category:Pages and Categories from wikipedia5]] [[Category:shinto shrines]]{{DEFAULTSORT:Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine}}[[category:shinto shrines]] [[Category:Expanded pages from wikipedia]] [[en:Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine]][[en:Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine]]

It is closely linked to [[Oarai Isosaki Shrine]] which also worships [[Sukunabikona]].{{Cite book |last1=Cali |first1=Joseph |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=J1gEEAAAQBAJ&dq=Oarai+Isosaki+Shrine&pg=PA73 |title=Shinto Shrines: A Guide to the Sacred Sites of Japan's Ancient Religion |last2=Dougill |first2=John |date=2012-11-30 |publisher=University of Hawaii Press |isbn=978-0-8248-3775-4 |language=en}}{{Cite web |title=A Study of Shinto: The Religion of the Japanese Nation |url=https://www.routledge.com/A-Study-of-Shinto-The-Religion-of-the-Japanese-Nation/Katu/p/book/9780415845762 |access-date=2023-11-18 |website=Routledge & CRC Press |language=en}}{{Rp|page=29}} ==Overview== {{神社 |name = Sakattsura Isosaki Shrine |image = [[File:Sajatsura Isosaki Jinja Shaden.jpg|270px]]

Plaque "Sakattsura Isosaki Shrine" written by [[Prince Komatsu Akihito]]]] '''Sakattsura Isosaki Shrine''' (さかつらいそさきじんじゃ) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Hitachinaka City]], [[Ibaraki Prefecture]]. It is classified as a [[Myōjin Taisha|Myōjin Taisha]] under the [[Engishiki|Engishiki system]]. The former shrine rank was [[National Middle Shrine|Kokuhei Chūsha]], and it is now a [[Bekkaku Shrine]] under the [[Association of Shinto Shrines]]. == Overview == The shrine is situated on a hill facing the [[Pacific Ocean]] in eastern [[Ibaraki Prefecture]]. It is closely related to [[Ōarai Isosaki Shrine]] in [[Ōarai Town]] across the [[Naka River]], and the two shrines form a single faith. == Deities == '''Main deity''' * '''[[Sukunahikona no Mikoto]]''' (少彦名命) *: Known for helping [[Ōnamuchi no Mikoto]] (Ōkuninushi no Mikoto) in creating the land. '''Enshrined deity''' * [[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi no Mikoto]] (大名持命) *: Another name for [[Ōkuninushi no Mikoto]] (大己貴命), the deity of [[Ōarai Isosaki Shrine]], and his divided spirit. He is said to have created the land with the help of Sukunahikona no Mikoto. In the myths found in the [[Kojiki]], [[Nihon Shoki]], and [[Fudoki]], these two deities often appear together in the stories of land creation. Many shrines enshrine this combination of deities. At this shrine, Sukunahikona no Mikoto is also considered [[Ebisu]] of the [[Seven Lucky Gods]], and Ōnamuchi no Mikoto is considered [[Daikokuten]]. == History == === Founding === According to the [[Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku]], a deity appeared at Ōarai Isosaki in [[Kashima District, Hitachi Province]] in Saikō 3rd year (856). {{quotation| Hitachi Province reports that a new deity has descended at Ōarai Isosaki in Kashima District. Initially, a salt maker saw a shining light in the sea at midnight. The next day, two strange stones appeared on the shore, each about a foot high. The following day, more than twenty small stones appeared around the strange stones, resembling attendants. The stones were vividly colored and shaped like monks, but without ears or eyes. The divine spirit possessed a person and said, "I am Ōnamuchi and Sukunahikona. We finished creating this land and went to the eastern sea, but we have returned to save the people." |Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku, Saikō 3rd year, December戊戌条}} Thus, Ōkuninushi no Mikoto (Ōnamuchi) was enshrined at Ōarai, and Sukunahikona no Mikoto was enshrined at Sakattsura, marking the founding of the two shrines. The rock formations along the coast near the shrine are tilted about 45 degrees to the south, and the part that tilts to the north is called "Gyaku-retsu" (逆列, Reverse Row), which is said to be the origin of the shrine's name. Later, it came to be known as "Sakattsura" because it enshrined the god of sake (alcohol)[http://www.oyashiro.or.jp/link/0006.html Sakattsura Isosaki Shrine] (Ibaraki Prefecture Shrine Office). === Historical Overview === The [[Engishiki Jinmyocho]] lists the shrine as "Hitachi Province Naka District Sakattsura Isosaki Yakushi Bosatsu Shrine" and classifies it as a Myōjin Taisha. The shrine fell into decline during the [[Middle Ages]] and lost its buildings. In the [[Early Modern Period]], the second lord of the [[Mito Domain]], [[Tokugawa Mitsukuni]], initiated the rebuilding of the shrine, and the third lord, [[Tokugawa Tsunaeda]], relocated and restored it to its current location. The old site is said to be near the first torii. In 1885 (Meiji 18), the shrine was ranked as a [[National Middle Shrine|Kokuhei Chūsha]] under the [[Modern Shrine rank System]]. It is now officially named "Sakattsura Isosaki Shrine." === Shrine rankings === * [[Ten'an]] 1st year (857), August 7 - Received official shrine status (Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku) * Ten'an 1st year (857), October 15 - Granted the title "Yakushi Bosatsu Myōjin" (Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku) == Grounds == The carving of a squirrel and grapes on the front of the haiden is said to be the work of [[Hidari Jingorō]]. The guardian dogs (komainu) on either side of the second torii were made by a Showa period stone mason named Heikichi Iizuka. The path to the shrine is lined with camellia, tabunoki, and sudajii trees, forming a broadleaf forest that is designated a Natural Monument by Ibaraki Prefecture. The original shrine site is believed to be near the first torii, around the ruins of Hikantei. Designated in 2005. == location Information == '''location''' * [[Ibaraki Prefecture]], [[Hitachinaka City]], Isosaki Town 4607-2 '''Transportation Access''' * Nearest station: [[Hitachinaka Seaside Railway]], [[Hitachinaka Seaside Railway Minato Line|Minato Line]], [[Ajigaura Station]] (about 15 minutes on foot) - The terminal station of the Minato Line. '''Nearby''' * Ruins of Hikantei - Ruins of a pavilion built by the Mito Domain. Designated a Historic Site by Hitachinaka City. * Kanto Place - A scenic spot selected by the lords of the Mito Domain. Designated a Scenic Spot by Hitachinaka City. * Kawagozuka Kofun - Designated a Historic Site by Hitachinaka City. * Hiraiso Cretaceous Layer - Nearby coast. Designated a Natural Monument by Ibaraki Prefecture. == References == {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist}} == Related Books == * Anzu Moto, Umeda Yoshihiko, editors and supervisors, "Shinto Dictionary", [[Shinto Shinpōsha]], 1968, p. 31 * [[Eiji Shirai]], Toki Masakuni, editors, "Shrine Dictionary", [[Tōkyōdō Shuppan]], 1979, pp. 154-155 * Ueyama Haruhira, others, "Japan Shrine General Overview", [[Shin Jinbutsu Ōraisha]], 1992, pp. 68-69 * "Shinto no Hon", [[Gakken]], 1992, p. 213 == Related Articles == * [[Yakuojin]] * [[Horide Shrine (Hitachinaka City)]] == External Links == * [http://sakatura.org/ Sakattsura Isosaki Shrine] (Official Site) * [http://www.oyashiro.or.jp/link/0006.html Sakattsura Isosaki Shrine] (Ibaraki Prefecture Shrine Office) * [http://21coe.kokugakuin.ac.jp/db/jinja/206002.html Sakatsura Isosaki Yakushi Bosatsu Shrine] (Kokugakuin University 21st Century COE Program "Shinto and Shrine Historical Materials Collection") {{Shinto Shrines in Ibaraki Prefecture}} {{Normdaten}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Sakattsura Isosaki Shrine}} [[Category:Shinto shrines in Ibaraki Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Hitachinaka City]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Hitachinaka City]] [[Category:Myōjin Taisha]] [[Category:Historic Sites in Hitachi Province]] [[Category:National Middle Shrine]] [[Category:Ibaraki 100 Landscapes]] == See also == * [[Ichinomiya]] * [[Kanpei-taisha]] == References == {{reflist}} [[Category:Beppyo shrines]] [[Category:Myōjin Taisha]] [[Category:Kokuhei Chūsha]] [[Category:Pages and Categories from wikipedia5]][[en:Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine]][[Category:Pages and Categories from wikipedia5]] [[Category:shinto shrines]]{{DEFAULTSORT:Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine}}[[category:shinto shrines]] [[Category:Expanded pages from wikipedia]] [[en:Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine]][[en:Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine]]

Plaque "Sakattsura Isosaki Shrine" written by [[Prince Komatsu Akihito]]]] '''Sakattsura Isosaki Shrine''' (さかつらいそさきじんじゃ) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Hitachinaka City]], [[Ibaraki Prefecture]]. It is classified as a [[Myōjin Taisha|Myōjin Taisha]] under the [[Engishiki|Engishiki system]]. The former shrine rank was [[National Middle Shrine|Kokuhei Chūsha]], and it is now a [[Bekkaku Shrine]] under the [[Association of Shinto Shrines]]. == Overview == The shrine is situated on a hill facing the [[Pacific Ocean]] in eastern [[Ibaraki Prefecture]]. It is closely related to [[Ōarai Isosaki Shrine]] in [[Ōarai Town]] across the [[Naka River]], and the two shrines form a single faith. == Deities == '''Main deity''' * '''[[Sukunahikona no Mikoto]]''' (少彦名命) *: Known for helping [[Ōnamuchi no Mikoto]] (Ōkuninushi no Mikoto) in creating the land. '''Enshrined deity''' * [[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi no Mikoto]] (大名持命) *: Another name for [[Ōkuninushi no Mikoto]] (大己貴命), the deity of [[Ōarai Isosaki Shrine]], and his divided spirit. He is said to have created the land with the help of Sukunahikona no Mikoto. In the myths found in the [[Kojiki]], [[Nihon Shoki]], and [[Fudoki]], these two deities often appear together in the stories of land creation. Many shrines enshrine this combination of deities. At this shrine, Sukunahikona no Mikoto is also considered [[Ebisu]] of the [[Seven Lucky Gods]], and Ōnamuchi no Mikoto is considered [[Daikokuten]]. == History == === Founding === According to the [[Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku]], a deity appeared at Ōarai Isosaki in [[Kashima District, Hitachi Province]] in Saikō 3rd year (856). {{quotation| Hitachi Province reports that a new deity has descended at Ōarai Isosaki in Kashima District. Initially, a salt maker saw a shining light in the sea at midnight. The next day, two strange stones appeared on the shore, each about a foot high. The following day, more than twenty small stones appeared around the strange stones, resembling attendants. The stones were vividly colored and shaped like monks, but without ears or eyes. The divine spirit possessed a person and said, "I am Ōnamuchi and Sukunahikona. We finished creating this land and went to the eastern sea, but we have returned to save the people." |Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku, Saikō 3rd year, December戊戌条}} Thus, Ōkuninushi no Mikoto (Ōnamuchi) was enshrined at Ōarai, and Sukunahikona no Mikoto was enshrined at Sakattsura, marking the founding of the two shrines. The rock formations along the coast near the shrine are tilted about 45 degrees to the south, and the part that tilts to the north is called "Gyaku-retsu" (逆列, Reverse Row), which is said to be the origin of the shrine's name. Later, it came to be known as "Sakattsura" because it enshrined the god of sake (alcohol)[http://www.oyashiro.or.jp/link/0006.html Sakattsura Isosaki Shrine] (Ibaraki Prefecture Shrine Office). === Historical Overview === The [[Engishiki Jinmyocho]] lists the shrine as "Hitachi Province Naka District Sakattsura Isosaki Yakushi Bosatsu Shrine" and classifies it as a Myōjin Taisha. The shrine fell into decline during the [[Middle Ages]] and lost its buildings. In the [[Early Modern Period]], the second lord of the [[Mito Domain]], [[Tokugawa Mitsukuni]], initiated the rebuilding of the shrine, and the third lord, [[Tokugawa Tsunaeda]], relocated and restored it to its current location. The old site is said to be near the first torii. In 1885 (Meiji 18), the shrine was ranked as a [[National Middle Shrine|Kokuhei Chūsha]] under the [[Modern Shrine rank System]]. It is now officially named "Sakattsura Isosaki Shrine." === Shrine rankings === * [[Ten'an]] 1st year (857), August 7 - Received official shrine status (Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku) * Ten'an 1st year (857), October 15 - Granted the title "Yakushi Bosatsu Myōjin" (Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku) == Grounds == The carving of a squirrel and grapes on the front of the haiden is said to be the work of [[Hidari Jingorō]]. The guardian dogs (komainu) on either side of the second torii were made by a Showa period stone mason named Heikichi Iizuka. The path to the shrine is lined with camellia, tabunoki, and sudajii trees, forming a broadleaf forest that is designated a Natural Monument by Ibaraki Prefecture. The original shrine site is believed to be near the first torii, around the ruins of Hikantei. Designated in 2005. == location Information == '''location''' * [[Ibaraki Prefecture]], [[Hitachinaka City]], Isosaki Town 4607-2 '''Transportation Access''' * Nearest station: [[Hitachinaka Seaside Railway]], [[Hitachinaka Seaside Railway Minato Line|Minato Line]], [[Ajigaura Station]] (about 15 minutes on foot) - The terminal station of the Minato Line. '''Nearby''' * Ruins of Hikantei - Ruins of a pavilion built by the Mito Domain. Designated a Historic Site by Hitachinaka City. * Kanto Place - A scenic spot selected by the lords of the Mito Domain. Designated a Scenic Spot by Hitachinaka City. * Kawagozuka Kofun - Designated a Historic Site by Hitachinaka City. * Hiraiso Cretaceous Layer - Nearby coast. Designated a Natural Monument by Ibaraki Prefecture. == References == {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist}} == Related Books == * Anzu Moto, Umeda Yoshihiko, editors and supervisors, "Shinto Dictionary", [[Shinto Shinpōsha]], 1968, p. 31 * [[Eiji Shirai]], Toki Masakuni, editors, "Shrine Dictionary", [[Tōkyōdō Shuppan]], 1979, pp. 154-155 * Ueyama Haruhira, others, "Japan Shrine General Overview", [[Shin Jinbutsu Ōraisha]], 1992, pp. 68-69 * "Shinto no Hon", [[Gakken]], 1992, p. 213 == Related Articles == * [[Yakuojin]] * [[Horide Shrine (Hitachinaka City)]] == External Links == * [http://sakatura.org/ Sakattsura Isosaki Shrine] (Official Site) * [http://www.oyashiro.or.jp/link/0006.html Sakattsura Isosaki Shrine] (Ibaraki Prefecture Shrine Office) * [http://21coe.kokugakuin.ac.jp/db/jinja/206002.html Sakatsura Isosaki Yakushi Bosatsu Shrine] (Kokugakuin University 21st Century COE Program "Shinto and Shrine Historical Materials Collection") {{Shinto Shrines in Ibaraki Prefecture}} {{Normdaten}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Sakattsura Isosaki Shrine}} [[Category:Shinto shrines in Ibaraki Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Hitachinaka City]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Hitachinaka City]] [[Category:Myōjin Taisha]] [[Category:Historic Sites in Hitachi Province]] [[Category:National Middle Shrine]] [[Category:Ibaraki 100 Landscapes]] == See also == * [[Ichinomiya]] * [[Kanpei-taisha]] == References == {{reflist}} [[Category:Beppyo shrines]] [[Category:Myōjin Taisha]] [[Category:Kokuhei Chūsha]] [[Category:Pages and Categories from wikipedia5]][[en:Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine]][[Category:Pages and Categories from wikipedia5]] [[Category:shinto shrines]]{{DEFAULTSORT:Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine}}[[category:shinto shrines]] [[Category:Expanded pages from wikipedia]] [[en:Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine]][[en:Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine]]

'''Enshrined deity''' * [[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi no Mikoto]] (大名持命) *: Another name for [[Ōkuninushi no Mikoto]] (大己貴命), the deity of [[Ōarai Isosaki Shrine]], and his divided spirit. He is said to have created the land with the help of Sukunahikona no Mikoto. In the myths found in the [[Kojiki]], [[Nihon Shoki]], and [[Fudoki]], these two deities often appear together in the stories of land creation. Many shrines enshrine this combination of deities. At this shrine, Sukunahikona no Mikoto is also considered [[Ebisu]] of the [[Seven Lucky Gods]], and Ōnamuchi no Mikoto is considered [[Daikokuten]]. == History == === Founding === According to the [[Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku]], a deity appeared at Ōarai Isosaki in [[Kashima District, Hitachi Province]] in Saikō 3rd year (856). {{quotation| Hitachi Province reports that a new deity has descended at Ōarai Isosaki in Kashima District. Initially, a salt maker saw a shining light in the sea at midnight. The next day, two strange stones appeared on the shore, each about a foot high. The following day, more than twenty small stones appeared around the strange stones, resembling attendants. The stones were vividly colored and shaped like monks, but without ears or eyes. The divine spirit possessed a person and said, "I am Ōnamuchi and Sukunahikona. We finished creating this land and went to the eastern sea, but we have returned to save the people." |Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku, Saikō 3rd year, December戊戌条}} Thus, Ōkuninushi no Mikoto (Ōnamuchi) was enshrined at Ōarai, and Sukunahikona no Mikoto was enshrined at Sakattsura, marking the founding of the two shrines. The rock formations along the coast near the shrine are tilted about 45 degrees to the south, and the part that tilts to the north is called "Gyaku-retsu" (逆列, Reverse Row), which is said to be the origin of the shrine's name. Later, it came to be known as "Sakattsura" because it enshrined the god of sake (alcohol)[http://www.oyashiro.or.jp/link/0006.html Sakattsura Isosaki Shrine] (Ibaraki Prefecture Shrine Office). === Historical Overview === The [[Engishiki Jinmyocho]] lists the shrine as "Hitachi Province Naka District Sakattsura Isosaki Yakushi Bosatsu Shrine" and classifies it as a Myōjin Taisha. The shrine fell into decline during the [[Middle Ages]] and lost its buildings. In the [[Early Modern Period]], the second lord of the [[Mito Domain]], [[Tokugawa Mitsukuni]], initiated the rebuilding of the shrine, and the third lord, [[Tokugawa Tsunaeda]], relocated and restored it to its current location. The old site is said to be near the first torii. In 1885 (Meiji 18), the shrine was ranked as a [[National Middle Shrine|Kokuhei Chūsha]] under the [[Modern Shrine rank System]]. It is now officially named "Sakattsura Isosaki Shrine." === Shrine rankings === * [[Ten'an]] 1st year (857), August 7 - Received official shrine status (Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku) * Ten'an 1st year (857), October 15 - Granted the title "Yakushi Bosatsu Myōjin" (Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku) == Grounds == The carving of a squirrel and grapes on the front of the haiden is said to be the work of [[Hidari Jingorō]]. The guardian dogs (komainu) on either side of the second torii were made by a Showa period stone mason named Heikichi Iizuka. The path to the shrine is lined with camellia, tabunoki, and sudajii trees, forming a broadleaf forest that is designated a Natural Monument by Ibaraki Prefecture. The original shrine site is believed to be near the first torii, around the ruins of Hikantei. We finished creating this land and went to the eastern sea, but we have returned to save the people." |Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku, Saikō 3rd year, December戊戌条}} Thus, Ōkuninushi no Mikoto (Ōnamuchi) was enshrined at Ōarai, and Sukunahikona no Mikoto was enshrined at Sakattsura, marking the founding of the two shrines. Later, it came to be known as "Sakattsura" because it enshrined the god of sake (alcohol)[http://www.oyashiro.or.jp/link/0006.html Sakattsura Isosaki Shrine] (Ibaraki Prefecture Shrine Office). === Historical Overview === The [[Engishiki Jinmyocho]] lists the shrine as "Hitachi Province Naka District Sakattsura Isosaki Yakushi Bosatsu Shrine" and classifies it as a Myōjin Taisha. The shrine fell into decline during the [[Middle Ages]] and lost its buildings. In the [[Early Modern Period]], the second lord of the [[Mito Domain]], [[Tokugawa Mitsukuni]], initiated the rebuilding of the shrine, and the third lord, [[Tokugawa Tsunaeda]], relocated and restored it to its current location. The old site is said to be near the first torii. In 1885 (Meiji 18), the shrine was ranked as a [[National Middle Shrine|Kokuhei Chūsha]] under the [[Modern Shrine rank System]]. It is now officially named "Sakattsura Isosaki Shrine." === Shrine rankings === * [[Ten'an]] 1st year (857), August 7 - Received official shrine status (Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku) * Ten'an 1st year (857), October 15 - Granted the title "Yakushi Bosatsu Myōjin" (Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku) == Grounds == The carving of a squirrel and grapes on the front of the haiden is said to be the work of [[Hidari Jingorō]]. Plaque "Sakattsura Isosaki Shrine" written by [[Prince Komatsu Akihito]]]] '''Sakattsura Isosaki Shrine''' (さかつらいそさきじんじゃ) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Hitachinaka City]], [[Ibaraki Prefecture]]. It is classified as a [[Myōjin Taisha|Myōjin Taisha]] under the [[Engishiki|Engishiki system]]. The former shrine rank was [[National Middle Shrine|Kokuhei Chūsha]], and it is now a [[Bekkaku Shrine]] under the [[Association of Shinto Shrines]]. == Overview == The shrine is situated on a hill facing the [[Pacific Ocean]] in eastern [[Ibaraki Prefecture]]. It is closely related to [[Ōarai Isosaki Shrine]] in [[Ōarai Town]] across the [[Naka River]], and the two shrines form a single faith. == Deities == '''Main deity''' * '''[[Sukunahikona no Mikoto]]''' (少彦名命) *: Known for helping [[Ōnamuchi no Mikoto]] (Ōkuninushi no Mikoto) in creating the land. '''Enshrined deity''' * [[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi no Mikoto]] (大名持命) *: Another name for [[Ōkuninushi no Mikoto]] (大己貴命), the deity of [[Ōarai Isosaki Shrine]], and his divided spirit. He is said to have created the land with the help of Sukunahikona no Mikoto. In the myths found in the [[Kojiki]], [[Nihon Shoki]], and [[Fudoki]], these two deities often appear together in the stories of land creation. Many shrines enshrine this combination of deities. At this shrine, Sukunahikona no Mikoto is also considered [[Ebisu]] of the [[Seven Lucky Gods]], and Ōnamuchi no Mikoto is considered [[Daikokuten]]. == History == === Founding === According to the [[Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku]], a deity appeared at Ōarai Isosaki in [[Kashima District, Hitachi Province]] in Saikō 3rd year (856). {{quotation| Hitachi Province reports that a new deity has descended at Ōarai Isosaki in Kashima District. Initially, a salt maker saw a shining light in the sea at midnight. The next day, two strange stones appeared on the shore, each about a foot high. The following day, more than twenty small stones appeared around the strange stones, resembling attendants. The stones were vividly colored and shaped like monks, but without ears or eyes. The divine spirit possessed a person and said, "I am Ōnamuchi and Sukunahikona. We finished creating this land and went to the eastern sea, but we have returned to save the people." |Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku, Saikō 3rd year, December戊戌条}} Thus, Ōkuninushi no Mikoto (Ōnamuchi) was enshrined at Ōarai, and Sukunahikona no Mikoto was enshrined at Sakattsura, marking the founding of the two shrines. Later, it came to be known as "Sakattsura" because it enshrined the god of sake (alcohol)[http://www.oyashiro.or.jp/link/0006.html Sakattsura Isosaki Shrine] (Ibaraki Prefecture Shrine Office). === Historical Overview === The [[Engishiki Jinmyocho]] lists the shrine as "Hitachi Province Naka District Sakattsura Isosaki Yakushi Bosatsu Shrine" and classifies it as a Myōjin Taisha. The shrine fell into decline during the [[Middle Ages]] and lost its buildings. In the [[Early Modern Period]], the second lord of the [[Mito Domain]], [[Tokugawa Mitsukuni]], initiated the rebuilding of the shrine, and the third lord, [[Tokugawa Tsunaeda]], relocated and restored it to its current location. The old site is said to be near the first torii. In 1885 (Meiji 18), the shrine was ranked as a [[National Middle Shrine|Kokuhei Chūsha]] under the [[Modern Shrine rank System]]. It is now officially named "Sakattsura Isosaki Shrine." === Shrine rankings === * [[Ten'an]] 1st year (857), August 7 - Received official shrine status (Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku) * Ten'an 1st year (857), October 15 - Granted the title "Yakushi Bosatsu Myōjin" (Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku) == Grounds == The carving of a squirrel and grapes on the front of the haiden is said to be the work of [[Hidari Jingorō]]. The guardian dogs (komainu) on either side of the second torii were made by a Showa period stone mason named Heikichi Iizuka. The path to the shrine is lined with camellia, tabunoki, and sudajii trees, forming a broadleaf forest that is designated a Natural Monument by Ibaraki Prefecture. The original shrine site is believed to be near the first torii, around the ruins of Hikantei. Plaque "Sakattsura Isosaki Shrine" written by [[Prince Komatsu Akihito]]]] '''Sakattsura Isosaki Shrine''' (さかつらいそさきじんじゃ) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Hitachinaka City]], [[Ibaraki Prefecture]]. It is classified as a [[Myōjin Taisha|Myōjin Taisha]] under the [[Engishiki|Engishiki system]]. The former shrine rank was [[National Middle Shrine|Kokuhei Chūsha]], and it is now a [[Bekkaku Shrine]] under the [[Association of Shinto Shrines]]. == Overview == The shrine is situated on a hill facing the [[Pacific Ocean]] in eastern [[Ibaraki Prefecture]]. It is closely related to [[Ōarai Isosaki Shrine]] in [[Ōarai Town]] across the [[Naka River]], and the two shrines form a single faith. == Deities == '''Main deity''' * '''[[Sukunahikona no Mikoto]]''' (少彦名命) *: Known for helping [[Ōnamuchi no Mikoto]] (Ōkuninushi no Mikoto) in creating the land. '''Enshrined deity''' * [[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi no Mikoto]] (大名持命) *: Another name for [[Ōkuninushi no Mikoto]] (大己貴命), the deity of [[Ōarai Isosaki Shrine]], and his divided spirit. He is said to have created the land with the help of Sukunahikona no Mikoto. In the myths found in the [[Kojiki]], [[Nihon Shoki]], and [[Fudoki]], these two deities often appear together in the stories of land creation. Many shrines enshrine this combination of deities. At this shrine, Sukunahikona no Mikoto is also considered [[Ebisu]] of the [[Seven Lucky Gods]], and Ōnamuchi no Mikoto is considered [[Daikokuten]]. == History == === Founding === According to the [[Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku]], a deity appeared at Ōarai Isosaki in [[Kashima District, Hitachi Province]] in Saikō 3rd year (856). {{quotation| Hitachi Province reports that a new deity has descended at Ōarai Isosaki in Kashima District. Initially, a salt maker saw a shining light in the sea at midnight. The next day, two strange stones appeared on the shore, each about a foot high. The following day, more than twenty small stones appeared around the strange stones, resembling attendants. The stones were vividly colored and shaped like monks, but without ears or eyes. The divine spirit possessed a person and said, "I am Ōnamuchi and Sukunahikona. We finished creating this land and went to the eastern sea, but we have returned to save the people." |Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku, Saikō 3rd year, December戊戌条}} Thus, Ōkuninushi no Mikoto (Ōnamuchi) was enshrined at Ōarai, and Sukunahikona no Mikoto was enshrined at Sakattsura, marking the founding of the two shrines. The rock formations along the coast near the shrine are tilted about 45 degrees to the south, and the part that tilts to the north is called "Gyaku-retsu" (逆列, Reverse Row), which is said to be the origin of the shrine's name. Later, it came to be known as "Sakattsura" because it enshrined the god of sake (alcohol)[http://www.oyashiro.or.jp/link/0006.html Sakattsura Isosaki Shrine] (Ibaraki Prefecture Shrine Office). === Historical Overview === The [[Engishiki Jinmyocho]] lists the shrine as "Hitachi Province Naka District Sakattsura Isosaki Yakushi Bosatsu Shrine" and classifies it as a Myōjin Taisha. The shrine fell into decline during the [[Middle Ages]] and lost its buildings. In the [[Early Modern Period]], the second lord of the [[Mito Domain]], [[Tokugawa Mitsukuni]], initiated the rebuilding of the shrine, and the third lord, [[Tokugawa Tsunaeda]], relocated and restored it to its current location. The old site is said to be near the first torii. In 1885 (Meiji 18), the shrine was ranked as a [[National Middle Shrine|Kokuhei Chūsha]] under the [[Modern Shrine rank System]]. It is now officially named "Sakattsura Isosaki Shrine." === Shrine rankings === * [[Ten'an]] 1st year (857), August 7 - Received official shrine status (Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku) * Ten'an 1st year (857), October 15 - Granted the title "Yakushi Bosatsu Myōjin" (Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku) == Grounds == The carving of a squirrel and grapes on the front of the haiden is said to be the work of [[Hidari Jingorō]]. The guardian dogs (komainu) on either side of the second torii were made by a Showa period stone mason named Heikichi Iizuka. The path to the shrine is lined with camellia, tabunoki, and sudajii trees, forming a broadleaf forest that is designated a Natural Monument by Ibaraki Prefecture. The original shrine site is believed to be near the first torii, around the ruins of Hikantei. Plaque "Sakattsura Isosaki Shrine" written by [[Prince Komatsu Akihito]]]] '''Sakattsura Isosaki Shrine''' (さかつらいそさきじんじゃ) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Hitachinaka City]], [[Ibaraki Prefecture]]. It is classified as a [[Myōjin Taisha|Myōjin Taisha]] under the [[Engishiki|Engishiki system]]. The former shrine rank was [[National Middle Shrine|Kokuhei Chūsha]], and it is now a [[Beppyo Shrine]] under the [[Association of Shinto Shrines]]. == Overview == The shrine is situated on a hill facing the [[Pacific Ocean]] in eastern [[Ibaraki Prefecture]]. It is closely related to [[Ōarai Isosaki Shrine]] in [[Ōarai Town]] across the [[Naka River]], and the two shrines form a single faith. == Deities == '''Main deity''' * '''[[Sukunahikona no Mikoto]]''' (少彦名命) *: Known for helping [[Ōnamuchi no Mikoto]] (Ōkuninushi no Mikoto) in creating the land. '''Enshrined deity''' * [[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi no Mikoto]] (大名持命) *: Another name for [[Ōkuninushi no Mikoto]] (大己貴命), the deity of [[Ōarai Isosaki Shrine]], and his divided spirit. He is said to have created the land with the help of Sukunahikona no Mikoto. In the myths found in the [[Kojiki]], [[Nihon Shoki]], and [[Fudoki]], these two deities often appear together in the stories of land creation. Many shrines enshrine this combination of deities. At this shrine, Sukunahikona no Mikoto is also considered [[Ebisu]] of the [[Seven Lucky Gods]], and Ōnamuchi no Mikoto is considered [[Daikokuten]]. == History == === Founding === According to the [[Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku]], a deity appeared at Ōarai Isosaki in [[Kashima District, Hitachi Province]] in Saikō 3rd year (856). {{quotation| Hitachi Province reports that a new deity has descended at Ōarai Isosaki in Kashima District. Initially, a salt maker saw a shining light in the sea at midnight. The next day, two strange stones appeared on the shore, each about a foot high. The following day, more than twenty small stones appeared around the strange stones, resembling attendants. The stones were vividly colored and shaped like monks, but without ears or eyes. The divine spirit possessed a person and said, "I am Ōnamuchi and Sukunahikona. We finished creating this land and went to the eastern sea, but we have returned to save the people." |Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku, Saikō 3rd year, December戊戌条}} Thus, Ōkuninushi no Mikoto (Ōnamuchi) was enshrined at Ōarai, and Sukunahikona no Mikoto was enshrined at Sakattsura, marking the founding of the two shrines. The rock formations along the coast near the shrine are tilted about 45 degrees to the south, and the part that tilts to the north is called "Gyaku-retsu" (逆列, Reverse Row), which is said to be the origin of the shrine's name. Later, it came to be known as "Sakattsura" because it enshrined the god of sake (alcohol)[http://www.oyashiro.or.jp/link/0006.html Sakattsura Isosaki Shrine] (Ibaraki Prefecture Shrine Office). === Historical Overview === The [[Engishiki Jinmyocho]] lists the shrine as "Hitachi Province Naka District Sakattsura Isosaki Yakushi Bosatsu Shrine" and classifies it as a Myōjin Taisha. The shrine fell into decline during the [[Middle Ages]] and lost its buildings. In the [[Early Modern Period]], the second lord of the [[Mito Domain]], [[Tokugawa Mitsukuni]], initiated the rebuilding of the shrine, and the third lord, [[Tokugawa Tsunaeda]], relocated and restored it to its current location. The old site is said to be near the first torii. In 1885 (Meiji 18), the shrine was ranked as a [[National Middle Shrine|Kokuhei Chūsha]] under the [[Modern Shrine rank System]]. It is now officially named "Sakattsura Isosaki Shrine." === Shrine rankings === * [[Ten'an]] 1st year (857), August 7 - Received official shrine status (Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku) * Ten'an 1st year (857), October 15 - Granted the title "Yakushi Bosatsu Myōjin" (Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku) == Grounds == The carving of a squirrel and grapes on the front of the haiden is said to be the work of [[Hidari Jingorō]]. The guardian dogs (komainu) on either side of the second torii were made by a Showa period stone mason named Heikichi Iizuka. The path to the shrine is lined with camellia, tabunoki, and sudajii trees, forming a broadleaf forest that is designated a Natural Monument by Ibaraki Prefecture. The original shrine site is believed to be near the first torii, around the ruins of Hikantei.
