'''酒列磯前神社'''（さかつらいそさきじんじゃ）は、{{jalink|茨城県|Q83273}}{{jalink|ひたちなか市|Q696772}}にある{{jalink|神社|Q845945}}。{{jalink|式内社}}（{{jalink|名神大社|Q9610964}}）。{{jalink|近代社格制度|Q712534|旧社格}}は{{jalink|国幣中社}}で、現在は{{jalink|神社本庁|Q908077}}の{{jalink|別表神社|Q10898274}}。 === 概要 === {{jalink|茨城県|Q83273}}の東部、{{jalink|太平洋|Q98}}に面した岬の丘上に鎮座する。{{jalink|那珂川|Q1076983}}対岸の{{jalink|大洗町|Q1349185}}にある{{jalink|大洗磯前神社|Q11437230}}と深い関係にあると言われ、2社で1つの信仰を形成している。 === 祭神 === '''主祭神''' * '''{{jalink|少彦名命}}'''（すくなひこなのみこと） *: 大名持命とともに国造りを行ったとされる。 '''配祀神''' * {{jalink|大国主|Q276944|大名持命}} （おおなもちのみこと） *: {{jalink|大国主|Q276944|大国主命}}（大己貴命）の別名。{{jalink|大洗磯前神社|Q11437230}}祭神で、その分霊。少彦名命の力を借りて国造りを行ったとされる。 国造りにおいて『{{jalink|古事記|Q813031}}』・『{{jalink|日本書紀|Q813935}}』・『{{jalink|風土記|Q1194534}}』などの神話では大名持命と少彦名命の2神が併せて登場することから、当社に限らずこの2神の組み合わせで祀る神社は多い。また、当社では少彦名命を{{jalink|七福神|Q846858}}の{{jalink|えびす|Q1129330}}、大名持命を{{jalink|大黒天|Q1759916}}とも見なしている。 === 歴史 === === 創建 === 『{{jalink|日本文徳天皇実録|Q1052905}}』によると、{{jalink|斉衡|Q1324664}}3年（{{jalink|856年|Q30370}}）に{{jalink|常陸国|Q1055353}}{{jalink|鹿島郡 (茨城県)|Q6374307|鹿島郡}}の大洗磯前に神が現れたとされる。 {{quotation| 常陸国上言。鹿嶋郡大洗磯前有神新降。初郡民有煮海為塩者。夜半望海。光耀属天。明日有両怪石。見在水次。高各尺許。体於神造。非人間石。塩翁私異之去。後一日。亦有廿餘小石。在向石左右。似若侍坐。彩色非常。或形像沙門。唯無耳目。時神憑人云。我是大奈母知少比古奈命也。昔造此国訖。去徃東海。今為済民。更亦来帰。 ある夜、{{jalink|塩|Q11254|製塩業}}の者が海に光るものを見た。次の日、海辺に二つの奇妙な石があった。両方とも一尺ほどだった。さらに次の日には20あまりの小石が怪石の周りに侍坐するように出現した。怪石は彩色が派手で、僧侶の姿をしていた。神霊は人に依って「われは大奈母知（おおなもち）・少比古奈命（すくなひこなのみこと）である。昔、この国を造り終えて、東の海に去ったが、今人々を救うために再び帰ってきた」と託宣した。 |『日本文徳天皇実録』斉衡3年12月戊戌条}} そして、大己貴命（大奈母知）が大洗に、少彦名命（少比古奈命）が酒列に祀られ、両社の創建となったと伝えられている。 当社周辺海岸の岩石群は南に約45度に傾斜して並んでいるが、その内の一部の北に傾いた部分、すなわち「逆列（さかつら）」の地名が社名の由来とされる。のちに酒の神様を祀るところから「酒列」となったとされる[http://www.oyashiro.or.jp/link/0006.html 酒列磯前神社]（茨城県神社庁）。。 === 概史 === 『{{jalink|延喜式神名帳|Q11064932}}』には「{{jalink|常陸国|Q1055353}}{{jalink|那珂郡|Q1062968|那賀郡}} 酒烈礒前薬師菩薩神社」と記載され、{{jalink|名神大社|Q9610964}}に列している。 {{jalink|中世|Q12554}}には廃絶し社殿もなくなっていた。{{jalink|近世|Q5308718}}になって{{jalink|水戸藩|Q1146904}}2代藩主・{{jalink|徳川光圀|Q1194944}}により造営の起工がなされ、3代藩主・{{jalink|徳川綱條|Q6997897|綱條}}により現在地に遷座がなされ再興された。旧鎮座地は一の鳥居の辺りと伝えられている。 {{jalink|明治|Q3125096}}18年（{{jalink|1885年|Q7821}}）、{{jalink|近代社格制度|Q712534}}において{{jalink|国幣中社}}に列した。現在では公称を「酒列磯前神社」としている。 === 神階 === * {{jalink|天安 (日本)|Q1075611|天安}}元年（{{jalink|857年|Q30374}}）8月7日、官社に預かる （『日本文徳天皇実録』） * 天安元年（857年）10月15日、「薬師菩薩名神」の号を授かる （『日本文徳天皇実録』） === 境内 === 拝殿正面上部のリスとブドウの彫刻は、{{jalink|左甚五郎|Q2668220}}の作とされる。また、二の鳥居左右の狛犬は、昭和の石工・飯塚兵吉の作である。参道の樹叢は椿・タブノキ・スダジイなどからなる広葉樹林で、茨城県の天然記念物に指定されている。 なお現在の一の鳥居近く、比観亭跡周辺が元の社地とされている（現在は小祠が鎮座）。 酒列磯前神社 本殿.JPG|本殿 酒列磯前神社 祭神：{{jalink|菅原道真|Q382005}}公 * 事比羅神社 - 祭神：{{jalink|大物主|Q10936701|大物主命}} * 冨士神社 - 祭神：{{jalink|コノハナノサクヤビメ|Q1781862|木花咲耶媛命}}。子安神として信仰されている。 * 水神社 - 祭神：{{jalink|ミヅハノメ|Q8191796|罔象女命}} === 文化財 === === 茨城県指定天然記念物 === * 酒列磯前神社の樹叢 - 参道両側や境内周辺に広がる広葉樹林（椿やタブノキ、スダジイなど）。平成17年指定。 === 現地情報 === '''所在地''' * {{jalink|茨城県|Q83273}}{{jalink|ひたちなか市|Q696772}}磯崎町4607-2 '''交通アクセス''' * 額「酒列磯前神社」は[[小松宮彰仁親王|彰仁親王]]の書。]] '''酒列磯前神社'''（さかつらいそさきじんじゃ）は、{{jalink|茨城県|Q83273}}{{jalink|ひたちなか市|Q696772}}にある{{jalink|神社|Q845945}}。{{jalink|式内社}}（{{jalink|名神大社|Q9610964}}）。{{jalink|近代社格制度|Q712534|旧社格}}は{{jalink|国幣中社}}で、現在は{{jalink|神社本庁|Q908077}}の{{jalink|別表神社|Q10898274}}。 === 概要 === {{jalink|茨城県|Q83273}}の東部、{{jalink|太平洋|Q98}}に面した岬の丘上に鎮座する。{{jalink|那珂川|Q1076983}}対岸の{{jalink|大洗町|Q1349185}}にある{{jalink|大洗磯前神社|Q11437230}}と深い関係にあると言われ、2社で1つの信仰を形成している。 === 祭神 === '''主祭神''' * '''{{jalink|少彦名命}}'''（すくなひこなのみこと） *: 大名持命とともに国造りを行ったとされる。 '''配祀神''' * {{jalink|大国主|Q276944|大名持命}} （おおなもちのみこと） *: {{jalink|大国主|Q276944|大国主命}}（大己貴命）の別名。{{jalink|大洗磯前神社|Q11437230}}祭神で、その分霊。少彦名命の力を借りて国造りを行ったとされる。 国造りにおいて『{{jalink|古事記|Q813031}}』・『{{jalink|日本書紀|Q813935}}』・『{{jalink|風土記|Q1194534}}』などの神話では大名持命と少彦名命の2神が併せて登場することから、当社に限らずこの2神の組み合わせで祀る神社は多い。また、当社では少彦名命を{{jalink|七福神|Q846858}}の{{jalink|えびす|Q1129330}}、大名持命を{{jalink|大黒天|Q1759916}}とも見なしている。 === 歴史 === === 創建 === 『{{jalink|日本文徳天皇実録|Q1052905}}』によると、{{jalink|斉衡|Q1324664}}3年（{{jalink|856年|Q30370}}）に{{jalink|常陸国|Q1055353}}{{jalink|鹿島郡 (茨城県)|Q6374307|鹿島郡}}の大洗磯前に神が現れたとされる。 {{quotation| 常陸国上言。鹿嶋郡大洗磯前有神新降。初郡民有煮海為塩者。夜半望海。光耀属天。明日有両怪石。見在水次。高各尺許。体於神造。非人間石。塩翁私異之去。後一日。亦有廿餘小石。在向石左右。似若侍坐。彩色非常。或形像沙門。唯無耳目。時神憑人云。我是大奈母知少比古奈命也。昔造此国訖。去徃東海。今為済民。更亦来帰。 ある夜、{{jalink|塩|Q11254|製塩業}}の者が海に光るものを見た。次の日、海辺に二つの奇妙な石があった。両方とも一尺ほどだった。さらに次の日には20あまりの小石が怪石の周りに侍坐するように出現した。怪石は彩色が派手で、僧侶の姿をしていた。神霊は人に依って「われは大奈母知（おおなもち）・少比古奈命（すくなひこなのみこと）である。昔、この国を造り終えて、東の海に去ったが、今人々を救うために再び帰ってきた」と託宣した。 |『日本文徳天皇実録』斉衡3年12月戊戌条}} そして、大己貴命（大奈母知）が大洗に、少彦名命（少比古奈命）が酒列に祀られ、両社の創建となったと伝えられている。 当社周辺海岸の岩石群は南に約45度に傾斜して並んでいるが、その内の一部の北に傾いた部分、すなわち「逆列（さかつら）」の地名が社名の由来とされる。のちに酒の神様を祀るところから「酒列」となったとされる[http://www.oyashiro.or.jp/link/0006.html 酒列磯前神社]（茨城県神社庁）。。 === 概史 === 『{{jalink|延喜式神名帳|Q11064932}}』には「{{jalink|常陸国|Q1055353}}{{jalink|那珂郡|Q1062968|那賀郡}} 酒烈礒前薬師菩薩神社」と記載され、{{jalink|名神大社|Q9610964}}に列している。 {{jalink|中世|Q12554}}には廃絶し社殿もなくなっていた。{{jalink|近世|Q5308718}}になって{{jalink|水戸藩|Q1146904}}2代藩主・{{jalink|徳川光圀|Q1194944}}により造営の起工がなされ、3代藩主・{{jalink|徳川綱條|Q6997897|綱條}}により現在地に遷座がなされ再興された。旧鎮座地は一の鳥居の辺りと伝えられている。 {{jalink|明治|Q3125096}}18年（{{jalink|1885年|Q7821}}）、{{jalink|近代社格制度|Q712534}}において{{jalink|国幣中社}}に列した。現在では公称を「酒列磯前神社」としている。 === 神階 === * {{jalink|天安 (日本)|Q1075611|天安}}元年（{{jalink|857年|Q30374}}）8月7日、官社に預かる （『日本文徳天皇実録』） * 天安元年（857年）10月15日、「薬師菩薩名神」の号を授かる （『日本文徳天皇実録』） === 境内 === 拝殿正面上部のリスとブドウの彫刻は、{{jalink|左甚五郎|Q2668220}}の作とされる。また、二の鳥居左右の狛犬は、昭和の石工・飯塚兵吉の作である。参道の樹叢は椿・タブノキ・スダジイなどからなる広葉樹林で、茨城県の天然記念物に指定されている。 なお現在の一の鳥居近く、比観亭跡周辺が元の社地とされている（現在は小祠が鎮座）。 酒列磯前神社 本殿.JPG|本殿 酒列磯前神社 拝殿.JPG|拝殿 酒列磯前神社 水戸斉昭公腰かけの石.JPG|{{jalink|徳川斉昭|Q1323770|水戸斉昭}}公腰かけの石 酒列磯前神社 二の鳥居.JPG|二の鳥居 酒列磯前神社 参道.JPG|参道の樹叢（県指定天然記念物） === 摂末社 === [[File:酒列鎮霊社 (酒列磯前神社境内社).JPG|thumb|200px|酒列鎮霊社]] [[File:酒列磯前神社 末社群.JPG|thumb|200px|末社5社]] * 酒列鎮霊社 （さかつらちんれいしゃ） ** 祭神：{{jalink|日露戦争|Q159950}}より{{jalink|第二次世界大戦|Q362}}までの戦没者506柱 *: 本殿の北隣に鎮座。 * 稲荷神社 -祭神：{{jalink|ウカノミタマ|Q3080728|倉稲魂命}} * 天満宮 - 祭神：{{jalink|菅原道真|Q382005}}公 * 事比羅神社 - 祭神：{{jalink|大物主|Q10936701|大物主命}} * 冨士神社 - 祭神：{{jalink|コノハナノサクヤビメ|Q1781862|木花咲耶媛命}}。子安神として信仰されている。 * 水神社 - 祭神：{{jalink|ミヅハノメ|Q8191796|罔象女命}} === 文化財 === === 茨城県指定天然記念物 === * 酒列磯前神社の樹叢 - 参道両側や境内周辺に広がる広葉樹林（椿やタブノキ、スダジイなど）。平成17年指定。 === 現地情報 === '''所在地''' * {{jalink|茨城県|Q83273}}{{jalink|ひたちなか市|Q696772}}磯崎町4607-2 '''交通アクセス''' * 最寄駅：{{jalink|ひたちなか海浜鉄道|Q11276223}}{{jalink|ひたちなか海浜鉄道湊線|Q6863245|湊線}} {{jalink|阿字ヶ浦駅|Q4699733}} （徒歩約15分） - 湊線終着駅。 '''周辺''' * 比観亭跡 - 水戸藩が建てた東屋跡。ひたちなか市指定史跡。 * 観濤所 - 水戸藩主が選定した景勝地。ひたちなか市指定名勝。 * 川子塚古墳 - ひたちなか市指定史跡。 * 平磯白亜紀層 - 周辺海岸。県指定天然記念物。 === 脚注 === {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist}} === 関連図書 === * 安津素彦・梅田義彦編集兼監修者『神道辞典』{{jalink|神社新報|Q11590705}}社、1968年、31頁 * '''酒列磯前神社'''（さかつらいそさきじんじゃ）は、{{jalink|茨城県|Q83273}}{{jalink|ひたちなか市|Q696772}}にある{{jalink|神社|Q845945}}。{{jalink|式内社}}（{{jalink|名神大社|Q9610964}}）。{{jalink|近代社格制度|Q712534|旧社格}}は{{jalink|国幣中社}}で、現在は{{jalink|神社本庁|Q908077}}の{{jalink|別表神社|Q10898274}}。 === 概要 === {{jalink|茨城県|Q83273}}の東部、{{jalink|太平洋|Q98}}に面した岬の丘上に鎮座する。{{jalink|那珂川|Q1076983}}対岸の{{jalink|大洗町|Q1349185}}にある{{jalink|大洗磯前神社|Q11437230}}と深い関係にあると言われ、2社で1つの信仰を形成している。 === 祭神 === '''主祭神''' * '''{{jalink|少彦名命}}'''（すくなひこなのみこと） *: 大名持命とともに国造りを行ったとされる。 '''配祀神''' * {{jalink|大国主|Q276944|大名持命}} （おおなもちのみこと） *: {{jalink|大国主|Q276944|大国主命}}（大己貴命）の別名。{{jalink|大洗磯前神社|Q11437230}}祭神で、その分霊。少彦名命の力を借りて国造りを行ったとされる。 国造りにおいて『{{jalink|古事記|Q813031}}』・『{{jalink|日本書紀|Q813935}}』・『{{jalink|風土記|Q1194534}}』などの神話では大名持命と少彦名命の2神が併せて登場することから、当社に限らずこの2神の組み合わせで祀る神社は多い。また、当社では少彦名命を{{jalink|七福神|Q846858}}の{{jalink|えびす|Q1129330}}、大名持命を{{jalink|大黒天|Q1759916}}とも見なしている。 === 歴史 === === 創建 === 『{{jalink|日本文徳天皇実録|Q1052905}}』によると、{{jalink|斉衡|Q1324664}}3年（{{jalink|856年|Q30370}}）に{{jalink|常陸国|Q1055353}}{{jalink|鹿島郡 (茨城県)|Q6374307|鹿島郡}}の大洗磯前に神が現れたとされる。 {{quotation| 常陸国上言。鹿嶋郡大洗磯前有神新降。初郡民有煮海為塩者。夜半望海。光耀属天。明日有両怪石。見在水次。高各尺許。体於神造。非人間石。塩翁私異之去。後一日。亦有廿餘小石。在向石左右。似若侍坐。彩色非常。或形像沙門。唯無耳目。時神憑人云。我是大奈母知少比古奈命也。昔造此国訖。去徃東海。今為済民。更亦来帰。 ある夜、{{jalink|塩|Q11254|製塩業}}の者が海に光るものを見た。次の日、海辺に二つの奇妙な石があった。両方とも一尺ほどだった。さらに次の日には20あまりの小石が怪石の周りに侍坐するように出現した。怪石は彩色が派手で、僧侶の姿をしていた。神霊は人に依って「われは大奈母知（おおなもち）・少比古奈命（すくなひこなのみこと）である。昔、この国を造り終えて、東の海に去ったが、今人々を救うために再び帰ってきた」と託宣した。 |『日本文徳天皇実録』斉衡3年12月戊戌条}} そして、大己貴命（大奈母知）が大洗に、少彦名命（少比古奈命）が酒列に祀られ、両社の創建となったと伝えられている。 当社周辺海岸の岩石群は南に約45度に傾斜して並んでいるが、その内の一部の北に傾いた部分、すなわち「逆列（さかつら）」の地名が社名の由来とされる。のちに酒の神様を祀るところから「酒列」となったとされる[http://www.oyashiro.or.jp/link/0006.html 酒列磯前神社]（茨城県神社庁）。。 === 概史 === 『{{jalink|延喜式神名帳|Q11064932}}』には「{{jalink|常陸国|Q1055353}}{{jalink|那珂郡|Q1062968|那賀郡}} 酒烈礒前薬師菩薩神社」と記載され、{{jalink|名神大社|Q9610964}}に列している。 {{jalink|中世|Q12554}}には廃絶し社殿もなくなっていた。{{jalink|近世|Q5308718}}になって{{jalink|水戸藩|Q1146904}}2代藩主・{{jalink|徳川光圀|Q1194944}}により造営の起工がなされ、3代藩主・{{jalink|徳川綱條|Q6997897|綱條}}により現在地に遷座がなされ再興された。旧鎮座地は一の鳥居の辺りと伝えられている。 {{jalink|明治|Q3125096}}18年（{{jalink|1885年|Q7821}}）、{{jalink|近代社格制度|Q712534}}において{{jalink|国幣中社}}に列した。現在では公称を「酒列磯前神社」としている。 === 神階 === * {{jalink|天安 (日本)|Q1075611|天安}}元年（{{jalink|857年|Q30374}}）8月7日、官社に預かる （『日本文徳天皇実録』） * 天安元年（857年）10月15日、「薬師菩薩名神」の号を授かる （『日本文徳天皇実録』） === 境内 === 拝殿正面上部のリスとブドウの彫刻は、{{jalink|左甚五郎|Q2668220}}の作とされる。また、二の鳥居左右の狛犬は、昭和の石工・飯塚兵吉の作である。参道の樹叢は椿・タブノキ・スダジイなどからなる広葉樹林で、茨城県の天然記念物に指定されている。 なお現在の一の鳥居近く、比観亭跡周辺が元の社地とされている（現在は小祠が鎮座）。 酒列磯前神社 本殿.JPG|本殿 酒列磯前神社 拝殿.JPG|拝殿 酒列磯前神社 水戸斉昭公腰かけの石.JPG|{{jalink|徳川斉昭|Q1323770|水戸斉昭}}公腰かけの石 酒列磯前神社 二の鳥居.JPG|二の鳥居 酒列磯前神社 参道.JPG|参道の樹叢（県指定天然記念物） === 摂末社 === [[File:酒列鎮霊社 (酒列磯前神社境内社).JPG|thumb|200px|酒列鎮霊社]] [[File:酒列磯前神社 末社群.JPG|thumb|200px|末社5社]] * 酒列鎮霊社 （さかつらちんれいしゃ） ** 祭神：{{jalink|日露戦争|Q159950}}より{{jalink|第二次世界大戦|Q362}}までの戦没者506柱 *: 本殿の北隣に鎮座。 * 稲荷神社 -祭神：{{jalink|ウカノミタマ|Q3080728|倉稲魂命}} * 天満宮 - 祭神：{{jalink|菅原道真|Q382005}}公 * 事比羅神社 - 祭神：{{jalink|大物主|Q10936701|大物主命}} * 冨士神社 - 祭神：{{jalink|コノハナノサクヤビメ|Q1781862|木花咲耶媛命}}。子安神として信仰されている。 * 水神社 - 祭神：{{jalink|ミヅハノメ|Q8191796|罔象女命}} === 文化財 === === 茨城県指定天然記念物 === * 酒列磯前神社の樹叢 - 参道両側や境内周辺に広がる広葉樹林（椿やタブノキ、スダジイなど）。平成17年指定。 === 現地情報 === '''所在地''' * {{jalink|茨城県|Q83273}}{{jalink|ひたちなか市|Q696772}}磯崎町4607-2 '''交通アクセス''' * 最寄駅：{{jalink|ひたちなか海浜鉄道|Q11276223}}{{jalink|ひたちなか海浜鉄道湊線|Q6863245|湊線}} {{jalink|阿字ヶ浦駅|Q4699733}} （徒歩約15分） - 湊線終着駅。 '''周辺''' * 比観亭跡 - 水戸藩が建てた東屋跡。ひたちなか市指定史跡。 * 観濤所 - 水戸藩主が選定した景勝地。ひたちなか市指定名勝。 * 川子塚古墳 - ひたちなか市指定史跡。 * 平磯白亜紀層 - 周辺海岸。県指定天然記念物。 === 脚注 === {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist}} === 関連図書 === * 安津素彦・梅田義彦編集兼監修者『神道辞典』{{jalink|神社新報|Q11590705}}社、1968年、31頁 * {{jalink|白井永二|Q11579387}}・土岐昌訓編集『神社辞典』{{jalink|東京堂出版|Q11524645}}、1979年、154-155頁 * 上山春平他『日本「神社」総覧』{{jalink|新人物往来社|Q11501312}}、1992年、68-69頁 * 『神道の本』{{jalink|Gakken|Q86741099|学研}}、1992年、213頁 === 関連項目 === The plaque calligraphy is by Prince Akihito Komatsu.]] '''Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine''' (さかつらいそさきじんじゃ) is a Shinto shrine in Hitachinaka, Ibaraki. It is a Meishin-taisha listed in the Engishiki, formerly ranked kokuhei chusha, and currently a Beppyo shrine of Jinja Honcho. === Overview === The shrine stands on a coastal cape facing the Pacific Ocean. It is closely connected with {{jalink|Oarai Isosaki Shrine|Q11437230}} across the Naka River, and the two are often regarded as forming a paired cult. === Enshrined deities === ; Main deity * {{jalink|Sukunahikona|Q3275687|Sukunahikona-no-Mikoto}} ; Co-enshrined * {{jalink|Okuninushi|Q276944|Onamochi-no-Mikoto}} The two-deity pairing is common because both appear together in kuni-zukuri myths. At this shrine, Sukunahikona is also associated with Ebisu and Onamochi with Daikokuten. === History === According to the ''Nihon Montoku Tenno Jitsuroku'' (856), divine signs appeared at Oarai Isosaki, with miraculous stones and an oracle declaring the returning deities Onamochi and Sukunahikona. Tradition says Onamochi was enshrined at Oarai and Sukunahikona at Sakatsura, establishing both shrines. The shrine name is linked to a local "reverse-tilting" rock formation (saka-tsura). Later, it came to be written with the character for sake (酒). In the Engishiki, it appears as "Sakare Isosaki Yakushi Bosatsu Shrine" in Naka District, Hitachi Province, and is listed as Meishin-taisha. It declined in the medieval period and lost its buildings; in the early modern period it was restored under Mito domain patronage by Tokugawa Mitsukuni and Tokugawa Tsunaeda, with relocation to the current site. In 1885 it was ranked kokuhei chusha. The official modern name is Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine. === Divine rank === * 857-08-07: entered official shrine register * 857-10-15: granted title "Yakushi Bosatsu Meishin" === Precinct === Notable features include: * Carving of squirrels and grapes above the haiden front (traditionally attributed to Jingoro Hidari) * Komainu at the second torii by Showa-era stonemason Iizuka Hyokichi * Broadleaf tree-lined approach (camellia, tabunoki, sudajii), designated natural monument of Ibaraki Prefecture 酒列磯前神社 本殿.JPG|Honden 酒列磯前神社 拝殿.JPG|Haiden 酒列磯前神社 水戸斉昭公腰かけの石.JPG|Seat stone of Tokugawa Nariaki 酒列磯前神社 二の鳥居.JPG|Second torii 酒列磯前神社 参道.JPG|Approach woodland (prefectural natural monument) === Subsidiary shrines === * Sakatsura Chinreisha (for 506 war dead from Russo-Japanese War to WWII) * Inari Shrine * Tenmangu * Kotohira Shrine * Fuji Shrine * Suijin Shrine === Cultural properties === === Ibaraki Prefecture designated natural monument === * Woodland of Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine (designated 2005) === Site information === * Address: Isozaki-cho 4607-2, Hitachinaka, Ibaraki * Access: Hitachinaka Seaside Railway Minato Line, Ajigaura Station, about 15 minutes on foot === Notes === {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist}} === External links === * [https://sakatura.org/ Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine] (official site) * Ibaraki Association of Shinto Shrines page * Kokugakuin source compilation page {{神道 横}}{{茨城県の神社一覧目次}} {{Normdaten}} {{DEFAULTSORT:さかつらいそさきしんしや}} == Categories == [[Category:Wikidata generated shikinaisha pages|Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine]][[Category:Shikinaisha|Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine]][[Category:pages]][[Category:pages]] [[Category:Beppyo Shrine]] [[Category:Kokuhei-sha]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Hitachi Province]] [[Category:pages]] [[Category:茨城県の神社]] [[Category:ひたちなか市の歴史]] [[Category:ひたちなか市の建築物]] [[Category:名神大社]] [[Category:常陸国の式内社|名さかつらいそさきしんしや]] [[Category:国幣中社]] [[Category:別表神社]] [[Category:茨城百景]] [[Category:need translation]]

{{jalink|Beppyo shrine|Q10898274}} | founded = 856 | architecture = {{jalink|nagare-zukuri|Q210684}} | annual_festival = {{jalink|August 25|Q2819}} }} [[File:酒列磯前神社 一の鳥居.JPG|thumb|200px|First torii. The plaque calligraphy is by Prince Akihito Komatsu.]] '''Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine''' (さかつらいそさきじんじゃ) is a Shinto shrine in Hitachinaka, Ibaraki. It is a Meishin-taisha listed in the Engishiki, formerly ranked kokuhei chusha, and currently a Beppyo shrine of Jinja Honcho. === Overview === The shrine stands on a coastal cape facing the Pacific Ocean. It is closely connected with {{jalink|Oarai Isosaki Shrine|Q11437230}} across the Naka River, and the two are often regarded as forming a paired cult. === Enshrined deities === ; Main deity * {{jalink|Sukunahikona|Q3275687|Sukunahikona-no-Mikoto}} ; Co-enshrined * {{jalink|Okuninushi|Q276944|Onamochi-no-Mikoto}} The two-deity pairing is common because both appear together in kuni-zukuri myths. At this shrine, Sukunahikona is also associated with Ebisu and Onamochi with Daikokuten. === History === According to the ''Nihon Montoku Tenno Jitsuroku'' (856), divine signs appeared at Oarai Isosaki, with miraculous stones and an oracle declaring the returning deities Onamochi and Sukunahikona. Tradition says Onamochi was enshrined at Oarai and Sukunahikona at Sakatsura, establishing both shrines. The shrine name is linked to a local "reverse-tilting" rock formation (saka-tsura). Later, it came to be written with the character for sake (酒). In the Engishiki, it appears as "Sakare Isosaki Yakushi Bosatsu Shrine" in Naka District, Hitachi Province, and is listed as Meishin-taisha. It declined in the medieval period and lost its buildings; in the early modern period it was restored under Mito domain patronage by Tokugawa Mitsukuni and Tokugawa Tsunaeda, with relocation to the current site. In 1885 it was ranked kokuhei chusha. The official modern name is Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine. === Divine rank === * 857-08-07: entered official shrine register * 857-10-15: granted title "Yakushi Bosatsu Meishin" === Precinct === Notable features include: * Carving of squirrels and grapes above the haiden front (traditionally attributed to Jingoro Hidari) * Komainu at the second torii by Showa-era stonemason Iizuka Hyokichi * Broadleaf tree-lined approach (camellia, tabunoki, sudajii), designated natural monument of Ibaraki Prefecture 酒列磯前神社 本殿.JPG|Honden 酒列磯前神社 拝殿.JPG|Haiden 酒列磯前神社 水戸斉昭公腰かけの石.JPG|Seat stone of Tokugawa Nariaki 酒列磯前神社 二の鳥居.JPG|Second torii 酒列磯前神社 参道.JPG|Approach woodland (prefectural natural monument) === Subsidiary shrines === * Sakatsura Chinreisha (for 506 war dead from Russo-Japanese War to WWII) * Inari Shrine * Tenmangu * Kotohira Shrine * Fuji Shrine * Suijin Shrine === Cultural properties === === Ibaraki Prefecture designated natural monument === * Woodland of Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine (designated 2005) === Site information === * Address: Isozaki-cho 4607-2, Hitachinaka, Ibaraki * Access: Hitachinaka Seaside Railway Minato Line, Ajigaura Station, about 15 minutes on foot === Notes === {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist}} === External links === * [https://sakatura.org/ Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine] (official site) * Ibaraki Association of Shinto Shrines page * Kokugakuin source compilation page {{神道 横}}{{茨城県の神社一覧目次}} {{Normdaten}} {{DEFAULTSORT:さかつらいそさきしんしや}} == Categories == [[Category:Wikidata generated shikinaisha pages|Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine]][[Category:Shikinaisha|Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine]][[Category:pages]][[Category:pages]] [[Category:Beppyo Shrine]] [[Category:Kokuhei-sha]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Hitachi Province]] [[Category:pages]] [[Category:茨城県の神社]] [[Category:ひたちなか市の歴史]] [[Category:ひたちなか市の建築物]] [[Category:名神大社]] [[Category:常陸国の式内社|名さかつらいそさきしんしや]] [[Category:国幣中社]] [[Category:別表神社]] [[Category:茨城百景]] [[Category:need translation]]

The plaque calligraphy is by Prince Akihito Komatsu.]] '''Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine''' (さかつらいそさきじんじゃ) is a Shinto shrine in Hitachinaka, Ibaraki. It is a Meishin-taisha listed in the Engishiki, formerly ranked kokuhei chusha, and currently a Beppyo shrine of Jinja Honcho. === Overview === The shrine stands on a coastal cape facing the Pacific Ocean. It is closely connected with {{jalink|Oarai Isosaki Shrine|Q11437230}} across the Naka River, and the two are often regarded as forming a paired cult. === Enshrined deities === ; Main deity * {{jalink|Sukunahikona|Q3275687|Sukunahikona-no-Mikoto}} ; Co-enshrined * {{jalink|Okuninushi|Q276944|Onamochi-no-Mikoto}} The two-deity pairing is common because both appear together in kuni-zukuri myths. At this shrine, Sukunahikona is also associated with Ebisu and Onamochi with Daikokuten. === History === According to the ''Nihon Montoku Tenno Jitsuroku'' (856), divine signs appeared at Oarai Isosaki, with miraculous stones and an oracle declaring the returning deities Onamochi and Sukunahikona. Tradition says Onamochi was enshrined at Oarai and Sukunahikona at Sakatsura, establishing both shrines. The shrine name is linked to a local "reverse-tilting" rock formation (saka-tsura). Later, it came to be written with the character for sake (酒). In the Engishiki, it appears as "Sakare Isosaki Yakushi Bosatsu Shrine" in Naka District, Hitachi Province, and is listed as Meishin-taisha. It declined in the medieval period and lost its buildings; in the early modern period it was restored under Mito domain patronage by Tokugawa Mitsukuni and Tokugawa Tsunaeda, with relocation to the current site. In 1885 it was ranked kokuhei chusha. The official modern name is Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine. === Divine rank === * 857-08-07: entered official shrine register * 857-10-15: granted title "Yakushi Bosatsu Meishin" === Precinct === Notable features include: * Carving of squirrels and grapes above the haiden front (traditionally attributed to Jingoro Hidari) * Komainu at the second torii by Showa-era stonemason Iizuka Hyokichi * Broadleaf tree-lined approach (camellia, tabunoki, sudajii), designated natural monument of Ibaraki Prefecture 酒列磯前神社 本殿.JPG|Honden 酒列磯前神社 拝殿.JPG|Haiden 酒列磯前神社 水戸斉昭公腰かけの石.JPG|Seat stone of Tokugawa Nariaki 酒列磯前神社 二の鳥居.JPG|Second torii 酒列磯前神社 参道.JPG|Approach woodland (prefectural natural monument) === Subsidiary shrines === * Sakatsura Chinreisha (for 506 war dead from Russo-Japanese War to WWII) * Inari Shrine * Tenmangu * Kotohira Shrine * Fuji Shrine * Suijin Shrine === Cultural properties === === Ibaraki Prefecture designated natural monument === * Woodland of Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine (designated 2005) === Site information === * Address: Isozaki-cho 4607-2, Hitachinaka, Ibaraki * Access: Hitachinaka Seaside Railway Minato Line, Ajigaura Station, about 15 minutes on foot === Notes === {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist}} === External links === * [https://sakatura.org/ Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine] (official site) * Ibaraki Association of Shinto Shrines page * Kokugakuin source compilation page {{神道 横}}{{茨城県の神社一覧目次}} {{Normdaten}} {{DEFAULTSORT:さかつらいそさきしんしや}} == Categories == [[Category:Wikidata generated shikinaisha pages|Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine]][[Category:Shikinaisha|Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine]][[Category:pages]][[Category:pages]] [[Category:Beppyo Shrine]] [[Category:Kokuhei-sha]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Hitachi Province]] [[Category:pages]] [[Category:茨城県の神社]] [[Category:ひたちなか市の歴史]] [[Category:ひたちなか市の建築物]] [[Category:名神大社]] [[Category:常陸国の式内社|名さかつらいそさきしんしや]] [[Category:国幣中社]] [[Category:別表神社]] [[Category:茨城百景]] [[Category:need translation]]

{{jalink|Beppyo shrine|Q10898274}} | founded = 856 | architecture = {{jalink|nagare-zukuri|Q210684}} | annual_festival = {{jalink|August 25|Q2819}} }} [[File:酒列磯前神社 一の鳥居.JPG|thumb|200px|First torii. The plaque calligraphy is by Prince Akihito Komatsu.]] '''Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine''' (さかつらいそさきじんじゃ) is a Shinto shrine in Hitachinaka, Ibaraki. It is a Meishin-taisha listed in the Engishiki, formerly ranked kokuhei chusha, and currently a Beppyo shrine of Jinja Honcho. === Overview === The shrine stands on a coastal cape facing the Pacific Ocean. It is closely connected with {{jalink|Oarai Isosaki Shrine|Q11437230}} across the Naka River, and the two are often regarded as forming a paired cult. === Enshrined deities === ; Main deity * {{jalink|Sukunahikona|Q3275687|Sukunahikona-no-Mikoto}} ; Co-enshrined * {{jalink|Okuninushi|Q276944|Onamochi-no-Mikoto}} The two-deity pairing is common because both appear together in kuni-zukuri myths. At this shrine, Sukunahikona is also associated with Ebisu and Onamochi with Daikokuten. === History === According to the ''Nihon Montoku Tenno Jitsuroku'' (856), divine signs appeared at Oarai Isosaki, with miraculous stones and an oracle declaring the returning deities Onamochi and Sukunahikona. Tradition says Onamochi was enshrined at Oarai and Sukunahikona at Sakatsura, establishing both shrines. The shrine name is linked to a local "reverse-tilting" rock formation (saka-tsura). Later, it came to be written with the character for sake (酒). In the Engishiki, it appears as "Sakare Isosaki Yakushi Bosatsu Shrine" in Naka District, Hitachi Province, and is listed as Meishin-taisha. It declined in the medieval period and lost its buildings; in the early modern period it was restored under Mito domain patronage by Tokugawa Mitsukuni and Tokugawa Tsunaeda, with relocation to the current site. In 1885 it was ranked kokuhei chusha. The official modern name is Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine. === Divine rank === * 857-08-07: entered official shrine register * 857-10-15: granted title "Yakushi Bosatsu Meishin" === Precinct === Notable features include: * Carving of squirrels and grapes above the haiden front (traditionally attributed to Jingoro Hidari) * Komainu at the second torii by Showa-era stonemason Iizuka Hyokichi * Broadleaf tree-lined approach (camellia, tabunoki, sudajii), designated natural monument of Ibaraki Prefecture 酒列磯前神社 本殿.JPG|Honden 酒列磯前神社 拝殿.JPG|Haiden 酒列磯前神社 水戸斉昭公腰かけの石.JPG|Seat stone of Tokugawa Nariaki 酒列磯前神社 二の鳥居.JPG|Second torii 酒列磯前神社 参道.JPG|Approach woodland (prefectural natural monument) === Subsidiary shrines === * Sakatsura Chinreisha (for 506 war dead from Russo-Japanese War to WWII) * Inari Shrine * Tenmangu * Kotohira Shrine * Fuji Shrine * Suijin Shrine === Cultural properties === === Ibaraki Prefecture designated natural monument === * Woodland of Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine (designated 2005) === Site information === * Address: Isozaki-cho 4607-2, Hitachinaka, Ibaraki * Access: Hitachinaka Seaside Railway Minato Line, Ajigaura Station, about 15 minutes on foot === Notes === {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist}} === External links === * [https://sakatura.org/ Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine] (official site) * Ibaraki Association of Shinto Shrines page * Kokugakuin source compilation page {{神道 横}}{{茨城県の神社一覧目次}} {{Normdaten}} {{DEFAULTSORT:さかつらいそさきしんしや}} == Categories == [[Category:Wikidata generated shikinaisha pages|Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine]][[Category:Shikinaisha|Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine]][[Category:pages]][[Category:pages]] [[Category:Beppyo Shrine]] [[Category:Kokuhei-sha]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Hitachi Province]] [[Category:pages]] [[Category:茨城県の神社]] [[Category:ひたちなか市の歴史]] [[Category:ひたちなか市の建築物]] [[Category:名神大社]] [[Category:常陸国の式内社|名さかつらいそさきしんしや]] [[Category:国幣中社]] [[Category:別表神社]] [[Category:茨城百景]] [[Category:need translation]]

The plaque calligraphy is by Prince Akihito Komatsu.]] '''Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine''' (さかつらいそさきじんじゃ) is a Shinto shrine in Hitachinaka, Ibaraki. It is a Meishin-taisha listed in the Engishiki, formerly ranked kokuhei chusha, and currently a Beppyo shrine of Jinja Honcho. === Overview === The shrine stands on a coastal cape facing the Pacific Ocean. It is closely connected with {{jalink|Oarai Isosaki Shrine|Q11437230}} across the Naka River, and the two are often regarded as forming a paired cult. === Enshrined deities === ; Main deity * {{jalink|Sukunahikona|Q3275687|Sukunahikona-no-Mikoto}} ; Co-enshrined * {{jalink|Okuninushi|Q276944|Onamochi-no-Mikoto}} The two-deity pairing is common because both appear together in kuni-zukuri myths. At this shrine, Sukunahikona is also associated with Ebisu and Onamochi with Daikokuten. === History === According to the ''Nihon Montoku Tenno Jitsuroku'' (856), divine signs appeared at Oarai Isosaki, with miraculous stones and an oracle declaring the returning deities Onamochi and Sukunahikona. Tradition says Onamochi was enshrined at Oarai and Sukunahikona at Sakatsura, establishing both shrines. The shrine name is linked to a local "reverse-tilting" rock formation (saka-tsura). Later, it came to be written with the character for sake (酒). In the Engishiki, it appears as "Sakare Isosaki Yakushi Bosatsu Shrine" in Naka District, Hitachi Province, and is listed as Meishin-taisha. It declined in the medieval period and lost its buildings; in the early modern period it was restored under Mito domain patronage by Tokugawa Mitsukuni and Tokugawa Tsunaeda, with relocation to the current site. In 1885 it was ranked kokuhei chusha. The official modern name is Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine. === Divine rank === * 857-08-07: entered official shrine register * 857-10-15: granted title "Yakushi Bosatsu Meishin" === Precinct === Notable features include: * Carving of squirrels and grapes above the haiden front (traditionally attributed to Jingoro Hidari) * Komainu at the second torii by Showa-era stonemason Iizuka Hyokichi * Broadleaf tree-lined approach (camellia, tabunoki, sudajii), designated natural monument of Ibaraki Prefecture 酒列磯前神社 本殿.JPG|Honden 酒列磯前神社 拝殿.JPG|Haiden 酒列磯前神社 水戸斉昭公腰かけの石.JPG|Seat stone of Tokugawa Nariaki 酒列磯前神社 二の鳥居.JPG|Second torii 酒列磯前神社 参道.JPG|Approach woodland (prefectural natural monument) === Subsidiary shrines === * Sakatsura Chinreisha (for 506 war dead from Russo-Japanese War to WWII) * Inari Shrine * Tenmangu * Kotohira Shrine * Fuji Shrine * Suijin Shrine === Cultural properties === === Ibaraki Prefecture designated natural monument === * Woodland of Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine (designated 2005) === Site information === * Address: Isozaki-cho 4607-2, Hitachinaka, Ibaraki * Access: Hitachinaka Seaside Railway Minato Line, Ajigaura Station, about 15 minutes on foot === Notes === {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist}} === External links === * [https://sakatura.org/ Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine] (official site) * Ibaraki Association of Shinto Shrines page * Kokugakuin source compilation page {{神道 横}}{{茨城県の神社一覧目次}} {{Normdaten}} {{DEFAULTSORT:さかつらいそさきしんしや}} == Categories == [[Category:Wikidata generated shikinaisha pages|Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine]][[Category:Shikinaisha|Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine]][[Category:pages]][[Category:pages]] [[Category:Beppyo Shrine]] [[Category:Kokuhei-sha]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Hitachi Province]] [[Category:pages]] [[Category:茨城県の神社]] [[Category:ひたちなか市の歴史]] [[Category:ひたちなか市の建築物]] [[Category:名神大社]] [[Category:常陸国の式内社|名さかつらいそさきしんしや]] [[Category:国幣中社]] [[Category:別表神社]] [[Category:茨城百景]]

The plaque calligraphy is by Prince Akihito Komatsu.]] '''Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine''' (さかつらいそさきじんじゃ) is a Shinto shrine in Hitachinaka, Ibaraki. It is a Meishin-taisha listed in the Engishiki, formerly ranked kokuhei chusha, and currently a Beppyo shrine of Jinja Honcho. === Overview === The shrine stands on a coastal cape facing the Pacific Ocean. It is closely connected with {{jalink|Oarai Isosaki Shrine|Q11437230}} across the Naka River, and the two are often regarded as forming a paired cult. === Enshrined deities === ; Main deity * {{jalink|Sukunahikona|Q3275687|Sukunahikona-no-Mikoto}} ; Co-enshrined * {{jalink|Okuninushi|Q276944|Onamochi-no-Mikoto}} The two-deity pairing is common because both appear together in kuni-zukuri myths. At this shrine, Sukunahikona is also associated with Ebisu and Onamochi with Daikokuten. === History === According to the ''Nihon Montoku Tenno Jitsuroku'' (856), divine signs appeared at Oarai Isosaki, with miraculous stones and an oracle declaring the returning deities Onamochi and Sukunahikona. Tradition says Onamochi was enshrined at Oarai and Sukunahikona at Sakatsura, establishing both shrines. The shrine name is linked to a local "reverse-tilting" rock formation (saka-tsura). Later, it came to be written with the character for sake (酒). In the Engishiki, it appears as "Sakare Isosaki Yakushi Bosatsu Shrine" in Naka District, Hitachi Province, and is listed as Meishin-taisha. It declined in the medieval period and lost its buildings; in the early modern period it was restored under Mito domain patronage by Tokugawa Mitsukuni and Tokugawa Tsunaeda, with relocation to the current site. In 1885 it was ranked kokuhei chusha. The official modern name is Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine. === Divine rank === * 857-08-07: entered official shrine register * 857-10-15: granted title "Yakushi Bosatsu Meishin" === Precinct === Notable features include: * Carving of squirrels and grapes above the haiden front (traditionally attributed to Jingoro Hidari) * Komainu at the second torii by Showa-era stonemason Iizuka Hyokichi * Broadleaf tree-lined approach (camellia, tabunoki, sudajii), designated natural monument of Ibaraki Prefecture 酒列磯前神社 本殿.JPG|Honden 酒列磯前神社 拝殿.JPG|Haiden 酒列磯前神社 水戸斉昭公腰かけの石.JPG|Seat stone of Tokugawa Nariaki 酒列磯前神社 二の鳥居.JPG|Second torii 酒列磯前神社 参道.JPG|Approach woodland (prefectural natural monument) === Subsidiary shrines === * Sakatsura Chinreisha (for 506 war dead from Russo-Japanese War to WWII) * Inari Shrine * Tenmangu * Kotohira Shrine * Fuji Shrine * Suijin Shrine === Cultural properties === === Ibaraki Prefecture designated natural monument === * Woodland of Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine (designated 2005) === Site information === * Address: Isozaki-cho 4607-2, Hitachinaka, Ibaraki * Access: Hitachinaka Seaside Railway Minato Line, Ajigaura Station, about 15 minutes on foot === Notes === {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist}} === External links === * [https://sakatura.org/ Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine] (official site) * Ibaraki Association of Shinto Shrines page * Kokugakuin source compilation page {{神道 横}}{{茨城県の神社一覧目次}} {{Normdaten}} {{DEFAULTSORT:さかつらいそさきしんしや}} == Categories == [[Category:Wikidata generated shikinaisha pages|Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine]][[Category:Shikinaisha|Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine]][[Category:pages]][[Category:pages]] [[Category:Beppyo Shrine]] [[Category:Kokuhei-sha]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Hitachi Province]] [[Category:pages]] [[Category:茨城県の神社]] [[Category:ひたちなか市の歴史]] [[Category:ひたちなか市の建築物]] [[Category:名神大社]] [[Category:常陸国の式内社|名さかつらいそさきしんしや]] [[Category:国幣中社]] [[Category:別表神社]] [[Category:茨城百景]][[Category:qq]]

The plaque calligraphy is by Prince Akihito Komatsu.]] '''Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine''' (さかつらいそさきじんじゃ) is a Shinto shrine in Hitachinaka, Ibaraki. It is a Meishin-taisha listed in the Engishiki, formerly ranked kokuhei chusha, and currently a Beppyo shrine of Jinja Honcho. === Overview === The shrine stands on a coastal cape facing the Pacific Ocean. It is closely connected with {{jalink|Oarai Isosaki Shrine|Q11437230}} across the Naka River, and the two are often regarded as forming a paired cult. === Enshrined deities === ; Main deity * {{jalink|Sukunahikona|Q3275687|Sukunahikona-no-Mikoto}} ; Co-enshrined * {{jalink|Okuninushi|Q276944|Onamochi-no-Mikoto}} The two-deity pairing is common because both appear together in kuni-zukuri myths. At this shrine, Sukunahikona is also associated with Ebisu and Onamochi with Daikokuten. === History === According to the ''Nihon Montoku Tenno Jitsuroku'' (856), divine signs appeared at Oarai Isosaki, with miraculous stones and an oracle declaring the returning deities Onamochi and Sukunahikona. Tradition says Onamochi was enshrined at Oarai and Sukunahikona at Sakatsura, establishing both shrines. The shrine name is linked to a local "reverse-tilting" rock formation (saka-tsura). Later, it came to be written with the character for sake (酒). In the Engishiki, it appears as "Sakare Isosaki Yakushi Bosatsu Shrine" in Naka District, Hitachi Province, and is listed as Meishin-taisha. It declined in the medieval period and lost its buildings; in the early modern period it was restored under Mito domain patronage by Tokugawa Mitsukuni and Tokugawa Tsunaeda, with relocation to the current site. In 1885 it was ranked kokuhei chusha. The official modern name is Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine. === Divine rank === * 857-08-07: entered official shrine register * 857-10-15: granted title "Yakushi Bosatsu Meishin" === Precinct === Notable features include: * Carving of squirrels and grapes above the haiden front (traditionally attributed to Jingoro Hidari) * Komainu at the second torii by Showa-era stonemason Iizuka Hyokichi * Broadleaf tree-lined approach (camellia, tabunoki, sudajii), designated natural monument of Ibaraki Prefecture 酒列磯前神社 本殿.JPG|Honden 酒列磯前神社 拝殿.JPG|Haiden 酒列磯前神社 水戸斉昭公腰かけの石.JPG|Seat stone of Tokugawa Nariaki 酒列磯前神社 二の鳥居.JPG|Second torii 酒列磯前神社 参道.JPG|Approach woodland (prefectural natural monument) === Subsidiary shrines === * Sakatsura Chinreisha (for 506 war dead from Russo-Japanese War to WWII) * Inari Shrine * Tenmangu * Kotohira Shrine * Fuji Shrine * Suijin Shrine === Cultural properties === === Ibaraki Prefecture designated natural monument === * Woodland of Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine (designated 2005) === Site information === * Address: Isozaki-cho 4607-2, Hitachinaka, Ibaraki * Access: Hitachinaka Seaside Railway Minato Line, Ajigaura Station, about 15 minutes on foot === Notes === {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist}} === External links === * [https://sakatura.org/ Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine] (official site) * Ibaraki Association of Shinto Shrines page * Kokugakuin source compilation page {{神道 横}}{{茨城県の神社一覧目次}} {{Normdaten}} {{DEFAULTSORT:さかつらいそさきしんしや}} == Categories == [[Category:Wikidata generated shikinaisha pages|Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine]][[Category:Shikinaisha|Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine]][[Category:pages]][[Category:pages]] [[Category:Beppyo Shrine]] [[Category:Kokuhei-sha]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Hitachi Province]] [[Category:pages]] [[Category:茨城県の神社]] [[Category:ひたちなか市の歴史]] [[Category:ひたちなか市の建築物]] [[Category:名神大社]] [[Category:常陸国の式内社|名さかつらいそさきしんしや]] [[Category:国幣中社]] [[Category:別表神社]] [[Category:茨城百景]][[Category:qq]] [[Category:qqq]]

The plaque calligraphy is by Prince Akihito Komatsu.]] '''Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine''' (さかつらいそさきじんじゃ) is a Shinto shrine in Hitachinaka, Ibaraki. It is a Meishin-taisha listed in the Engishiki, formerly ranked kokuhei chusha, and currently a Beppyo shrine of Jinja Honcho. === Overview === The shrine stands on a coastal cape facing the Pacific Ocean. It is closely connected with {{ill|lt=Oarai Isosaki Shrine|Q11437230|WD=Q11437230}} across the Naka River, and the two are often regarded as forming a paired cult. === Enshrined deities === ; Main deity * {{ill|lt=Sukunahikona|Q3275687|WD=Q3275687|lt=Sukunahikona-no-Mikoto}} ; Co-enshrined * {{ill|lt=Okuninushi|Q276944|WD=Q276944|lt=Onamochi-no-Mikoto}} The two-deity pairing is common because both appear together in kuni-zukuri myths. At this shrine, Sukunahikona is also associated with Ebisu and Onamochi with Daikokuten. === History === According to the ''Nihon Montoku Tenno Jitsuroku'' (856), divine signs appeared at Oarai Isosaki, with miraculous stones and an oracle declaring the returning deities Onamochi and Sukunahikona. Tradition says Onamochi was enshrined at Oarai and Sukunahikona at Sakatsura, establishing both shrines. The shrine name is linked to a local "reverse-tilting" rock formation (saka-tsura). Later, it came to be written with the character for sake (酒). In the Engishiki, it appears as "Sakare Isosaki Yakushi Bosatsu Shrine" in Naka District, Hitachi Province, and is listed as Meishin-taisha. It declined in the medieval period and lost its buildings; in the early modern period it was restored under Mito domain patronage by Tokugawa Mitsukuni and Tokugawa Tsunaeda, with relocation to the current site. In 1885 it was ranked kokuhei chusha. The official modern name is Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine. === Divine rank === * 857-08-07: entered official shrine register * 857-10-15: granted title "Yakushi Bosatsu Meishin" === Precinct === Notable features include: * Carving of squirrels and grapes above the haiden front (traditionally attributed to Jingoro Hidari) * Komainu at the second torii by Showa-era stonemason Iizuka Hyokichi * Broadleaf tree-lined approach (camellia, tabunoki, sudajii), designated natural monument of Ibaraki Prefecture 酒列磯前神社 本殿.JPG|Honden 酒列磯前神社 拝殿.JPG|Haiden 酒列磯前神社 水戸斉昭公腰かけの石.JPG|Seat stone of Tokugawa Nariaki 酒列磯前神社 二の鳥居.JPG|Second torii 酒列磯前神社 参道.JPG|Approach woodland (prefectural natural monument) === Subsidiary shrines === * Sakatsura Chinreisha (for 506 war dead from Russo-Japanese War to WWII) * Inari Shrine * Tenmangu * Kotohira Shrine * Fuji Shrine * Suijin Shrine === Cultural properties === === Ibaraki Prefecture designated natural monument === * Woodland of Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine (designated 2005) === Site information === * Address: Isozaki-cho 4607-2, Hitachinaka, Ibaraki * Access: Hitachinaka Seaside Railway Minato Line, Ajigaura Station, about 15 minutes on foot === Notes === {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist}} === External links === * [https://sakatura.org/ Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine] (official site) * Ibaraki Association of Shinto Shrines page * Kokugakuin source compilation page {{神道 横}}{{茨城県の神社一覧目次}} {{Normdaten}} {{DEFAULTSORT:さかつらいそさきしんしや}} == Categories == [[Category:Wikidata generated shikinaisha pages|Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine]][[Category:Shikinaisha|Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine]][[Category:pages]][[Category:pages]] [[Category:Beppyo Shrine]] [[Category:Kokuhei-sha]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Hitachi Province]] [[Category:pages]] [[Category:茨城県の神社]] [[Category:ひたちなか市の歴史]] [[Category:ひたちなか市の建築物]] [[Category:名神大社]] [[Category:常陸国の式内社|名さかつらいそさきしんしや]] [[Category:国幣中社]] [[Category:別表神社]] [[Category:茨城百景]][[Category:qq]] [[Category:qqq]]

The plaque calligraphy is by Prince Akihito Komatsu.]] '''Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine''' (さかつらいそさきじんじゃ) is a Shinto shrine in Hitachinaka, Ibaraki. It is a Meishin-taisha listed in the Engishiki, formerly ranked kokuhei chusha, and currently a Beppyo shrine of Jinja Honcho. === Overview === The shrine stands on a coastal cape facing the Pacific Ocean. It is closely connected with {{ill|lt=Oarai Isosaki Shrine|Q11437230|WD=Q11437230}} across the Naka River, and the two are often regarded as forming a paired cult. === Enshrined deities === ; Main deity * {{ill|lt=Sukunahikona|Q3275687|WD=Q3275687|lt=Sukunahikona-no-Mikoto}} ; Co-enshrined * {{ill|lt=Okuninushi|Q276944|WD=Q276944|lt=Onamochi-no-Mikoto}} The two-deity pairing is common because both appear together in kuni-zukuri myths. At this shrine, Sukunahikona is also associated with Ebisu and Onamochi with Daikokuten. === History === According to the ''Nihon Montoku Tenno Jitsuroku'' (856), divine signs appeared at Oarai Isosaki, with miraculous stones and an oracle declaring the returning deities Onamochi and Sukunahikona. Tradition says Onamochi was enshrined at Oarai and Sukunahikona at Sakatsura, establishing both shrines. The shrine name is linked to a local "reverse-tilting" rock formation (saka-tsura). Later, it came to be written with the character for sake (酒). In the Engishiki, it appears as "Sakare Isosaki Yakushi Bosatsu Shrine" in Naka District, Hitachi Province, and is listed as Meishin-taisha. It declined in the medieval period and lost its buildings; in the early modern period it was restored under Mito domain patronage by Tokugawa Mitsukuni and Tokugawa Tsunaeda, with relocation to the current site. In 1885 it was ranked kokuhei chusha. The official modern name is Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine. === Divine rank === * 857-08-07: entered official shrine register * 857-10-15: granted title "Yakushi Bosatsu Meishin" === Precinct === Notable features include: * Carving of squirrels and grapes above the haiden front (traditionally attributed to Jingoro Hidari) * Komainu at the second torii by Showa-era stonemason Iizuka Hyokichi * Broadleaf tree-lined approach (camellia, tabunoki, sudajii), designated natural monument of Ibaraki Prefecture 酒列磯前神社 本殿.JPG|Honden 酒列磯前神社 拝殿.JPG|Haiden 酒列磯前神社 水戸斉昭公腰かけの石.JPG|Seat stone of Tokugawa Nariaki 酒列磯前神社 二の鳥居.JPG|Second torii 酒列磯前神社 参道.JPG|Approach woodland (prefectural natural monument) === Subsidiary shrines === * Sakatsura Chinreisha (for 506 war dead from Russo-Japanese War to WWII) * Inari Shrine * Tenmangu * Kotohira Shrine * Fuji Shrine * Suijin Shrine === Cultural properties === === Ibaraki Prefecture designated natural monument === * Woodland of Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine (designated 2005) === Site information === * Address: Isozaki-cho 4607-2, Hitachinaka, Ibaraki * Access: Hitachinaka Seaside Railway Minato Line, Ajigaura Station, about 15 minutes on foot === Notes === {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist}} === External links === * [https://sakatura.org/ Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine] (official site) * Ibaraki Association of Shinto Shrines page * Kokugakuin source compilation page {{神道 横}}{{茨城県の神社一覧目次}} {{Normdaten}} {{DEFAULTSORT:さかつらいそさきしんしや}} == Categories == [[Category:Wikidata generated shikinaisha pages|Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine]][[Category:Shikinaisha|Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine]][[Category:pages]][[Category:pages]] [[Category:Beppyo Shrine]] [[Category:Kokuhei-sha]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Hitachi Province]] [[Category:pages]] [[Category:茨城県の神社]] [[Category:ひたちなか市の歴史]] [[Category:ひたちなか市の建築物]] [[Category:名神大社]] [[Category:常陸国の式内社|名さかつらいそさきしんしや]] [[Category:国幣中社]] [[Category:別表神社]] [[Category:茨城百景]][[Category:qq]] [[Category:qqq]]

The plaque calligraphy is by Prince Akihito Komatsu.]] '''Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine''' (さかつらいそさきじんじゃ) is a Shinto shrine in Hitachinaka, Ibaraki. It is a Meishin-taisha listed in the Engishiki, formerly ranked kokuhei chusha, and currently a Beppyo shrine of Jinja Honcho. === Overview === The shrine stands on a coastal cape facing the Pacific Ocean. It is closely connected with {{ill|lt=Oarai Isosaki Shrine|Q11437230|WD=Q11437230}} across the Naka River, and the two are often regarded as forming a paired cult. === Enshrined deities === ; Main deity * {{ill|lt=Sukunahikona|Q3275687|WD=Q3275687|lt=Sukunahikona-no-Mikoto}} ; Co-enshrined * {{ill|lt=Okuninushi|Q276944|WD=Q276944|lt=Onamochi-no-Mikoto}} The two-deity pairing is common because both appear together in kuni-zukuri myths. At this shrine, Sukunahikona is also associated with Ebisu and Onamochi with Daikokuten. === History === According to the ''Nihon Montoku Tenno Jitsuroku'' (856), divine signs appeared at Oarai Isosaki, with miraculous stones and an oracle declaring the returning deities Onamochi and Sukunahikona. Tradition says Onamochi was enshrined at Oarai and Sukunahikona at Sakatsura, establishing both shrines. The shrine name is linked to a local "reverse-tilting" rock formation (saka-tsura). Later, it came to be written with the character for sake (酒). In the Engishiki, it appears as "Sakare Isosaki Yakushi Bosatsu Shrine" in Naka District, Hitachi Province, and is listed as Meishin-taisha. It declined in the medieval period and lost its buildings; in the early modern period it was restored under Mito domain patronage by Tokugawa Mitsukuni and Tokugawa Tsunaeda, with relocation to the current site. In 1885 it was ranked kokuhei chusha. The official modern name is Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine. === Divine rank === * 857-08-07: entered official shrine register * 857-10-15: granted title "Yakushi Bosatsu Meishin" === Precinct === Notable features include: * Carving of squirrels and grapes above the haiden front (traditionally attributed to Jingoro Hidari) * Komainu at the second torii by Showa-era stonemason Iizuka Hyokichi * Broadleaf tree-lined approach (camellia, tabunoki, sudajii), designated natural monument of Ibaraki Prefecture 酒列磯前神社 本殿.JPG|Honden 酒列磯前神社 拝殿.JPG|Haiden 酒列磯前神社 水戸斉昭公腰かけの石.JPG|Seat stone of Tokugawa Nariaki 酒列磯前神社 二の鳥居.JPG|Second torii 酒列磯前神社 参道.JPG|Approach woodland (prefectural natural monument) === Subsidiary shrines === * Sakatsura Chinreisha (for 506 war dead from Russo-Japanese War to WWII) * Inari Shrine * Tenmangu * Kotohira Shrine * Fuji Shrine * Suijin Shrine === Cultural properties === === Ibaraki Prefecture designated natural monument === * Woodland of Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine (designated 2005) === Site information === * Address: Isozaki-cho 4607-2, Hitachinaka, Ibaraki * Access: Hitachinaka Seaside Railway Minato Line, Ajigaura Station, about 15 minutes on foot === Notes === {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist}} === External links === * [https://sakatura.org/ Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine] (official site) * Ibaraki Association of Shinto Shrines page * Kokugakuin source compilation page {{神道 横}}{{茨城県の神社一覧目次}} {{Normdaten}} {{DEFAULTSORT:さかつらいそさきしんしや}} == Categories == [[Category:Wikidata generated shikinaisha pages|Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine]][[Category:Shikinaisha|Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine]][[Category:pages]][[Category:pages]] [[Category:Beppyo Shrine]] [[Category:Kokuhei-sha]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Hitachi Province]] [[Category:pages]] [[Category:茨城県の神社]] [[Category:ひたちなか市の歴史]] [[Category:ひたちなか市の建築物]] [[Category:名神大社]] [[Category:常陸国の式内社|名さかつらいそさきしんしや]] [[Category:国幣中社]] [[Category:別表神社]] [[Category:茨城百景]][[Category:qq]] [[Category:qqq]]

The plaque calligraphy is by Prince Akihito Komatsu.]] '''Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine''' (さかつらいそさきじんじゃ) is a Shinto shrine in Hitachinaka, Ibaraki. It is a Meishin-taisha listed in the Engishiki, formerly ranked kokuhei chusha, and currently a Beppyo shrine of Jinja Honcho. === Overview === The shrine stands on a coastal cape facing the Pacific Ocean. It is closely connected with {{ill|lt=Oarai Isosaki Shrine|Q11437230|WD=Q11437230}} across the Naka River, and the two are often regarded as forming a paired cult. === Enshrined deities === ; Main deity * {{ill|lt=Sukunahikona|Q3275687|WD=Q3275687|lt=Sukunahikona-no-Mikoto}} ; Co-enshrined * {{ill|lt=Okuninushi|Q276944|WD=Q276944|lt=Onamochi-no-Mikoto}} The two-deity pairing is common because both appear together in kuni-zukuri myths. At this shrine, Sukunahikona is also associated with Ebisu and Onamochi with Daikokuten. === History === According to the ''Nihon Montoku Tenno Jitsuroku'' (856), divine signs appeared at Oarai Isosaki, with miraculous stones and an oracle declaring the returning deities Onamochi and Sukunahikona. Tradition says Onamochi was enshrined at Oarai and Sukunahikona at Sakatsura, establishing both shrines. The shrine name is linked to a local "reverse-tilting" rock formation (saka-tsura). Later, it came to be written with the character for sake (酒). In the Engishiki, it appears as "Sakare Isosaki Yakushi Bosatsu Shrine" in Naka District, Hitachi Province, and is listed as Meishin-taisha. It declined in the medieval period and lost its buildings; in the early modern period it was restored under Mito domain patronage by Tokugawa Mitsukuni and Tokugawa Tsunaeda, with relocation to the current site. In 1885 it was ranked kokuhei chusha. The official modern name is Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine. === Divine rank === * 857-08-07: entered official shrine register * 857-10-15: granted title "Yakushi Bosatsu Meishin" === Precinct === Notable features include: * Carving of squirrels and grapes above the haiden front (traditionally attributed to Jingoro Hidari) * Komainu at the second torii by Showa-era stonemason Iizuka Hyokichi * Broadleaf tree-lined approach (camellia, tabunoki, sudajii), designated natural monument of Ibaraki Prefecture 酒列磯前神社 本殿.JPG|Honden 酒列磯前神社 拝殿.JPG|Haiden 酒列磯前神社 水戸斉昭公腰かけの石.JPG|Seat stone of Tokugawa Nariaki 酒列磯前神社 二の鳥居.JPG|Second torii 酒列磯前神社 参道.JPG|Approach woodland (prefectural natural monument) === Subsidiary shrines === * Sakatsura Chinreisha (for 506 war dead from Russo-Japanese War to WWII) * Inari Shrine * Tenmangu * Kotohira Shrine * Fuji Shrine * Suijin Shrine === Cultural properties === === Ibaraki Prefecture designated natural monument === * Woodland of Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine (designated 2005) === Site information === * Address: Isozaki-cho 4607-2, Hitachinaka, Ibaraki * Access: Hitachinaka Seaside Railway Minato Line, Ajigaura Station, about 15 minutes on foot === Notes === {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist}} === External links === * [https://sakatura.org/ Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine] (official site) * Ibaraki Association of Shinto Shrines page * Kokugakuin source compilation page {{神道 横}}{{茨城県の神社一覧目次}} {{Normdaten}} {{DEFAULTSORT:さかつらいそさきしんしや}} == Categories == [[Category:Wikidata generated shikinaisha pages|Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine]][[Category:Shikinaisha|Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine]][[Category:pages]][[Category:pages]] [[Category:Beppyo Shrine]] [[Category:Kokuhei-sha]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Hitachi Province]] [[Category:pages]] [[Category:茨城県の神社]] [[Category:ひたちなか市の歴史]] [[Category:ひたちなか市の建築物]] [[Category:名神大社]] [[Category:常陸国の式内社|名さかつらいそさきしんしや]] [[Category:国幣中社]] [[Category:別表神社]] [[Category:茨城百景]][[Category:qq]] [[Category:qqq]]

The plaque calligraphy is by Prince Akihito Komatsu.]] '''Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine''' (さかつらいそさきじんじゃ) is a Shinto shrine in Hitachinaka, Ibaraki. It is a Meishin-taisha listed in the Engishiki, formerly ranked kokuhei chusha, and currently a Beppyo shrine of Jinja Honcho. === Overview === The shrine stands on a coastal cape facing the Pacific Ocean. It is closely connected with {{ill|lt=Oarai Isosaki Shrine|Q11437230|WD=Q11437230}} across the Naka River, and the two are often regarded as forming a paired cult. === Enshrined deities === ; Main deity * {{ill|lt=Sukunahikona|Q3275687|WD=Q3275687|lt=Sukunahikona-no-Mikoto}} ; Co-enshrined * {{ill|WD=Q276944|lt=Okuninushi|Q276944|WD=Q276944|lt=Onamochi-no-Mikoto}} The two-deity pairing is common because both appear together in kuni-zukuri myths. At this shrine, Sukunahikona is also associated with Ebisu and Onamochi with Daikokuten. === History === According to the ''Nihon Montoku Tenno Jitsuroku'' (856), divine signs appeared at Oarai Isosaki, with miraculous stones and an oracle declaring the returning deities Onamochi and Sukunahikona. Tradition says Onamochi was enshrined at Oarai and Sukunahikona at Sakatsura, establishing both shrines. The shrine name is linked to a local "reverse-tilting" rock formation (saka-tsura). Later, it came to be written with the character for sake (酒). In the Engishiki, it appears as "Sakare Isosaki Yakushi Bosatsu Shrine" in Naka District, Hitachi Province, and is listed as Meishin-taisha. It declined in the medieval period and lost its buildings; in the early modern period it was restored under Mito domain patronage by Tokugawa Mitsukuni and Tokugawa Tsunaeda, with relocation to the current site. In 1885 it was ranked kokuhei chusha. The official modern name is Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine. === Divine rank === * 857-08-07: entered official shrine register * 857-10-15: granted title "Yakushi Bosatsu Meishin" === Precinct === Notable features include: * Carving of squirrels and grapes above the haiden front (traditionally attributed to Jingoro Hidari) * Komainu at the second torii by Showa-era stonemason Iizuka Hyokichi * Broadleaf tree-lined approach (camellia, tabunoki, sudajii), designated natural monument of Ibaraki Prefecture 酒列磯前神社 本殿.JPG|Honden 酒列磯前神社 拝殿.JPG|Haiden 酒列磯前神社 水戸斉昭公腰かけの石.JPG|Seat stone of Tokugawa Nariaki 酒列磯前神社 二の鳥居.JPG|Second torii 酒列磯前神社 参道.JPG|Approach woodland (prefectural natural monument) === Subsidiary shrines === * Sakatsura Chinreisha (for 506 war dead from Russo-Japanese War to WWII) * Inari Shrine * Tenmangu * Kotohira Shrine * Fuji Shrine * Suijin Shrine === Cultural properties === === Ibaraki Prefecture designated natural monument === * Woodland of Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine (designated 2005) === Site information === * Address: Isozaki-cho 4607-2, Hitachinaka, Ibaraki * Access: Hitachinaka Seaside Railway Minato Line, Ajigaura Station, about 15 minutes on foot === Notes === {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist}} === External links === * [https://sakatura.org/ Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine] (official site) * Ibaraki Association of Shinto Shrines page * Kokugakuin source compilation page {{神道 横}}{{茨城県の神社一覧目次}} {{Normdaten}} {{DEFAULTSORT:さかつらいそさきしんしや}} == Categories == [[Category:Wikidata generated shikinaisha pages|Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine]][[Category:Shikinaisha|Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine]][[Category:pages]][[Category:pages]] [[Category:Beppyo Shrine]] [[Category:Kokuhei-sha]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Hitachi Province]] [[Category:pages]] [[Category:茨城県の神社]] [[Category:ひたちなか市の歴史]] [[Category:ひたちなか市の建築物]] [[Category:名神大社]] [[Category:常陸国の式内社|名さかつらいそさきしんしや]] [[Category:国幣中社]] [[Category:別表神社]] [[Category:茨城百景]][[Category:qq]] [[Category:qqq]]

The plaque calligraphy is by Prince Akihito Komatsu.]] '''Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine''' (さかつらいそさきじんじゃ) is a Shinto shrine in Hitachinaka, Ibaraki. It is a Meishin-taisha listed in the Engishiki, formerly ranked kokuhei chusha, and currently a Beppyo shrine of Jinja Honcho. === Overview === The shrine stands on a coastal cape facing the Pacific Ocean. It is closely connected with {{ill|lt=Oarai Isosaki Shrine|Q11437230|WD=Q11437230}} across the Naka River, and the two are often regarded as forming a paired cult. === Enshrined deities === ; Main deity * {{ill|lt=Sukunahikona|Q3275687|WD=Q3275687|lt=Sukunahikona-no-Mikoto}} ; Co-enshrined * {{ill|WD=Q276944|lt=Okuninushi|Q276944|WD=Q276944|lt=Onamochi-no-Mikoto}} The two-deity pairing is common because both appear together in kuni-zukuri myths. At this shrine, Sukunahikona is also associated with Ebisu and Onamochi with Daikokuten. === History === According to the ''Nihon Montoku Tenno Jitsuroku'' (856), divine signs appeared at Oarai Isosaki, with miraculous stones and an oracle declaring the returning deities Onamochi and Sukunahikona. Tradition says Onamochi was enshrined at Oarai and Sukunahikona at Sakatsura, establishing both shrines. The shrine name is linked to a local "reverse-tilting" rock formation (saka-tsura). Later, it came to be written with the character for sake (酒). In the Engishiki, it appears as "Sakare Isosaki Yakushi Bosatsu Shrine" in Naka District, Hitachi Province, and is listed as Meishin-taisha. It declined in the medieval period and lost its buildings; in the early modern period it was restored under Mito domain patronage by Tokugawa Mitsukuni and Tokugawa Tsunaeda, with relocation to the current site. In 1885 it was ranked kokuhei chusha. The official modern name is Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine. === Divine rank === * 857-08-07: entered official shrine register * 857-10-15: granted title "Yakushi Bosatsu Meishin" === Precinct === Notable features include: * Carving of squirrels and grapes above the haiden front (traditionally attributed to Jingoro Hidari) * Komainu at the second torii by Showa-era stonemason Iizuka Hyokichi * Broadleaf tree-lined approach (camellia, tabunoki, sudajii), designated natural monument of Ibaraki Prefecture 酒列磯前神社 本殿.JPG|Honden 酒列磯前神社 拝殿.JPG|Haiden 酒列磯前神社 水戸斉昭公腰かけの石.JPG|Seat stone of Tokugawa Nariaki 酒列磯前神社 二の鳥居.JPG|Second torii 酒列磯前神社 参道.JPG|Approach woodland (prefectural natural monument) === Subsidiary shrines === * Sakatsura Chinreisha (for 506 war dead from Russo-Japanese War to WWII) * Inari Shrine * Tenmangu * Kotohira Shrine * Fuji Shrine * Suijin Shrine === Cultural properties === === Ibaraki Prefecture designated natural monument === * Woodland of Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine (designated 2005) === Site information === * Address: Isozaki-cho 4607-2, Hitachinaka, Ibaraki * Access: Hitachinaka Seaside Railway Minato Line, Ajigaura Station, about 15 minutes on foot === Notes === {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist}} === External links === * [https://sakatura.org/ Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine] (official site) * Ibaraki Association of Shinto Shrines page * Kokugakuin source compilation page {{神道 横}}{{茨城県の神社一覧目次}} {{Normdaten}} {{DEFAULTSORT:さかつらいそさきしんしや}} == Categories == [[Category:Wikidata generated shikinaisha pages|Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine]][[Category:Shikinaisha|Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine]][[Category:pages]][[Category:pages]] [[Category:Beppyo Shrine]] [[Category:Kokuhei-sha]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Hitachi Province]] [[Category:pages]] [[Category:茨城県の神社]] [[Category:ひたちなか市の歴史]] [[Category:ひたちなか市の建築物]] [[Category:名神大社]] [[Category:常陸国の式内社|名さかつらいそさきしんしや]] [[Category:国幣中社]] [[Category:別表神社]] [[Category:茨城百景]][[Category:qq]] [[Category:qqq]]

The plaque calligraphy is by Prince Akihito Komatsu.]] '''Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine''' (さかつらいそさきじんじゃ) is a Shinto shrine in Hitachinaka, Ibaraki. It is a Meishin-taisha listed in the Engishiki, formerly ranked kokuhei chusha, and currently a Beppyo shrine of Jinja Honcho. === Overview === The shrine stands on a coastal cape facing the Pacific Ocean. It is closely connected with {{ill|lt=Oarai Isosaki Shrine|Q11437230|WD=Q11437230|1=Oarai Isosaki Shrine}} across the Naka River, and the two are often regarded as forming a paired cult. === Enshrined deities === ; Main deity * {{ill|lt=Sukunahikona|Q3275687|WD=Q3275687|lt=Sukunahikona-no-Mikoto|1=Sukunabikona}} ; Co-enshrined * {{ill|WD=Q276944|lt=Okuninushi|Q276944|WD=Q276944|lt=Onamochi-no-Mikoto|1=Ōkuninushi}} The two-deity pairing is common because both appear together in kuni-zukuri myths. At this shrine, Sukunahikona is also associated with Ebisu and Onamochi with Daikokuten. === History === According to the ''Nihon Montoku Tenno Jitsuroku'' (856), divine signs appeared at Oarai Isosaki, with miraculous stones and an oracle declaring the returning deities Onamochi and Sukunahikona. Tradition says Onamochi was enshrined at Oarai and Sukunahikona at Sakatsura, establishing both shrines. The shrine name is linked to a local "reverse-tilting" rock formation (saka-tsura). Later, it came to be written with the character for sake (酒). In the Engishiki, it appears as "Sakare Isosaki Yakushi Bosatsu Shrine" in Naka District, Hitachi Province, and is listed as Meishin-taisha. It declined in the medieval period and lost its buildings; in the early modern period it was restored under Mito domain patronage by Tokugawa Mitsukuni and Tokugawa Tsunaeda, with relocation to the current site. In 1885 it was ranked kokuhei chusha. The official modern name is Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine. === Divine rank === * 857-08-07: entered official shrine register * 857-10-15: granted title "Yakushi Bosatsu Meishin" === Precinct === Notable features include: * Carving of squirrels and grapes above the haiden front (traditionally attributed to Jingoro Hidari) * Komainu at the second torii by Showa-era stonemason Iizuka Hyokichi * Broadleaf tree-lined approach (camellia, tabunoki, sudajii), designated natural monument of Ibaraki Prefecture 酒列磯前神社 本殿.JPG|Honden 酒列磯前神社 拝殿.JPG|Haiden 酒列磯前神社 水戸斉昭公腰かけの石.JPG|Seat stone of Tokugawa Nariaki 酒列磯前神社 二の鳥居.JPG|Second torii 酒列磯前神社 参道.JPG|Approach woodland (prefectural natural monument) === Subsidiary shrines === * Sakatsura Chinreisha (for 506 war dead from Russo-Japanese War to WWII) * Inari Shrine * Tenmangu * Kotohira Shrine * Fuji Shrine * Suijin Shrine === Cultural properties === === Ibaraki Prefecture designated natural monument === * Woodland of Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine (designated 2005) === Site information === * Address: Isozaki-cho 4607-2, Hitachinaka, Ibaraki * Access: Hitachinaka Seaside Railway Minato Line, Ajigaura Station, about 15 minutes on foot === Notes === {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist}} === External links === * [https://sakatura.org/ Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine] (official site) * Ibaraki Association of Shinto Shrines page * Kokugakuin source compilation page {{神道 横}}{{茨城県の神社一覧目次}} {{Normdaten}} {{DEFAULTSORT:さかつらいそさきしんしや}} == Categories == [[Category:Wikidata generated shikinaisha pages|Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine]][[Category:Shikinaisha|Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine]][[Category:pages]][[Category:pages]] [[Category:Beppyo Shrine]] [[Category:Kokuhei-sha]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Hitachi Province]] [[Category:pages]] [[Category:茨城県の神社]] [[Category:ひたちなか市の歴史]] [[Category:ひたちなか市の建築物]] [[Category:名神大社]] [[Category:常陸国の式内社|名さかつらいそさきしんしや]] [[Category:国幣中社]] [[Category:別表神社]] [[Category:茨城百景]][[Category:qq]] [[Category:qqq]]

The plaque calligraphy is by Prince Akihito Komatsu.]] '''Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine''' (さかつらいそさきじんじゃ) is a Shinto shrine in Hitachinaka, Ibaraki. It is a Meishin-taisha listed in the Engishiki, formerly ranked kokuhei chusha, and currently a Beppyo shrine of Jinja Honcho. === Overview === The shrine stands on a coastal cape facing the Pacific Ocean. It is closely connected with {{ill|lt=Oarai Isosaki Shrine|Q11437230|WD=Q11437230|1=Oarai Isosaki Shrine}} across the Naka River, and the two are often regarded as forming a paired cult. === Enshrined deities === ; Main deity * {{ill|lt=Sukunahikona|Q3275687|WD=Q3275687|lt=Sukunahikona-no-Mikoto|1=Sukunabikona}} ; Co-enshrined * {{ill|WD=Q276944|lt=Okuninushi|Q276944|WD=Q276944|lt=Onamochi-no-Mikoto|1=Ōkuninushi}} The two-deity pairing is common because both appear together in kuni-zukuri myths. At this shrine, Sukunahikona is also associated with Ebisu and Onamochi with Daikokuten. === History === According to the ''Nihon Montoku Tenno Jitsuroku'' (856), divine signs appeared at Oarai Isosaki, with miraculous stones and an oracle declaring the returning deities Onamochi and Sukunahikona. Tradition says Onamochi was enshrined at Oarai and Sukunahikona at Sakatsura, establishing both shrines. The shrine name is linked to a local "reverse-tilting" rock formation (saka-tsura). Later, it came to be written with the character for sake (酒). In the Engishiki, it appears as "Sakare Isosaki Yakushi Bosatsu Shrine" in Naka District, Hitachi Province, and is listed as Meishin-taisha. It declined in the medieval period and lost its buildings; in the early modern period it was restored under Mito domain patronage by Tokugawa Mitsukuni and Tokugawa Tsunaeda, with relocation to the current site. In 1885 it was ranked kokuhei chusha. The official modern name is Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine. === Divine rank === * 857-08-07: entered official shrine register * 857-10-15: granted title "Yakushi Bosatsu Meishin" === Precinct === Notable features include: * Carving of squirrels and grapes above the haiden front (traditionally attributed to Jingoro Hidari) * Komainu at the second torii by Showa-era stonemason Iizuka Hyokichi * Broadleaf tree-lined approach (camellia, tabunoki, sudajii), designated natural monument of Ibaraki Prefecture 酒列磯前神社 本殿.JPG|Honden 酒列磯前神社 拝殿.JPG|Haiden 酒列磯前神社 水戸斉昭公腰かけの石.JPG|Seat stone of Tokugawa Nariaki 酒列磯前神社 二の鳥居.JPG|Second torii 酒列磯前神社 参道.JPG|Approach woodland (prefectural natural monument) === Subsidiary shrines === * Sakatsura Chinreisha (for 506 war dead from Russo-Japanese War to WWII) * Inari Shrine * Tenmangu * Kotohira Shrine * Fuji Shrine * Suijin Shrine === Cultural properties === === Ibaraki Prefecture designated natural monument === * Woodland of Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine (designated 2005) === Site information === * Address: Isozaki-cho 4607-2, Hitachinaka, Ibaraki * Access: Hitachinaka Seaside Railway Minato Line, Ajigaura Station, about 15 minutes on foot === Notes === {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist}} === External links === * [https://sakatura.org/ Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine] (official site) * Ibaraki Association of Shinto Shrines page * Kokugakuin source compilation page {{神道 横}}{{茨城県の神社一覧目次}} {{Normdaten}} {{DEFAULTSORT:さかつらいそさきしんしや}} == Categories == [[Category:Wikidata generated shikinaisha pages|Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine]][[Category:Shikinaisha|Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine]][[Category:pages]][[Category:pages]] [[Category:Beppyo Shrine]] [[Category:Kokuhei-sha]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Hitachi Province]] [[Category:pages]] [[Category:茨城県の神社]] [[Category:ひたちなか市の歴史]] [[Category:ひたちなか市の建築物]] [[Category:名神大社]] [[Category:常陸国の式内社|名さかつらいそさきしんしや]] [[Category:国幣中社]] [[Category:別表神社]] [[Category:茨城百景]][[Category:qq]] [[Category:qqq]]

The plaque calligraphy is by Prince Akihito Komatsu.]] '''Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine''' (さかつらいそさきじんじゃ) is a Shinto shrine in Hitachinaka, Ibaraki. It is a Meishin-taisha listed in the Engishiki, formerly ranked kokuhei chusha, and currently a Beppyo shrine of Jinja Honcho. === Overview === The shrine stands on a coastal cape facing the Pacific Ocean. It is closely connected with {{ill|lt=Oarai Isosaki Shrine|Q11437230|WD=Q11437230|1=Oarai Isosaki Shrine}} across the Naka River, and the two are often regarded as forming a paired cult. === Enshrined deities === ; Main deity * {{ill|lt=Sukunahikona|Q3275687|WD=Q3275687|lt=Sukunahikona-no-Mikoto|1=Sukunabikona}} ; Co-enshrined * {{ill|WD=Q276944|lt=Okuninushi|Q276944|WD=Q276944|lt=Onamochi-no-Mikoto|1=Ōkuninushi}} The two-deity pairing is common because both appear together in kuni-zukuri myths. At this shrine, Sukunahikona is also associated with Ebisu and Onamochi with Daikokuten. === History === According to the ''Nihon Montoku Tenno Jitsuroku'' (856), divine signs appeared at Oarai Isosaki, with miraculous stones and an oracle declaring the returning deities Onamochi and Sukunahikona. Tradition says Onamochi was enshrined at Oarai and Sukunahikona at Sakatsura, establishing both shrines. The shrine name is linked to a local "reverse-tilting" rock formation (saka-tsura). Later, it came to be written with the character for sake (酒). In the Engishiki, it appears as "Sakare Isosaki Yakushi Bosatsu Shrine" in Naka District, Hitachi Province, and is listed as Meishin-taisha. It declined in the medieval period and lost its buildings; in the early modern period it was restored under Mito domain patronage by Tokugawa Mitsukuni and Tokugawa Tsunaeda, with relocation to the current site. In 1885 it was ranked kokuhei chusha. The official modern name is Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine. === Divine rank === * 857-08-07: entered official shrine register * 857-10-15: granted title "Yakushi Bosatsu Meishin" === Precinct === Notable features include: * Carving of squirrels and grapes above the haiden front (traditionally attributed to Jingoro Hidari) * Komainu at the second torii by Showa-era stonemason Iizuka Hyokichi * Broadleaf tree-lined approach (camellia, tabunoki, sudajii), designated natural monument of Ibaraki Prefecture 酒列磯前神社 本殿.JPG|Honden 酒列磯前神社 拝殿.JPG|Haiden 酒列磯前神社 水戸斉昭公腰かけの石.JPG|Seat stone of Tokugawa Nariaki 酒列磯前神社 二の鳥居.JPG|Second torii 酒列磯前神社 参道.JPG|Approach woodland (prefectural natural monument) === Subsidiary shrines === * Sakatsura Chinreisha (for 506 war dead from Russo-Japanese War to WWII) * Inari Shrine * Tenmangu * Kotohira Shrine * Fuji Shrine * Suijin Shrine === Cultural properties === === Ibaraki Prefecture designated natural monument === * Woodland of Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine (designated 2005) === Site information === * Address: Isozaki-cho 4607-2, Hitachinaka, Ibaraki * Access: Hitachinaka Seaside Railway Minato Line, Ajigaura Station, about 15 minutes on foot === Notes === {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist}} === External links === * [https://sakatura.org/ Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine] (official site) * Ibaraki Association of Shinto Shrines page * Kokugakuin source compilation page {{神道 横}}{{茨城県の神社一覧目次}} {{Normdaten}} {{DEFAULTSORT:さかつらいそさきしんしや}} == Categories == [[Category:Wikidata generated shikinaisha pages|Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine]][[Category:Shikinaisha|Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine]][[Category:pages]][[Category:pages]] [[Category:Beppyo Shrine]] [[Category:Kokuhei-sha]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Hitachi Province]] [[Category:pages]] [[Category:茨城県の神社]] [[Category:ひたちなか市の歴史]] [[Category:ひたちなか市の建築物]] [[Category:名神大社]] [[Category:常陸国の式内社|名さかつらいそさきしんしや]] [[Category:国幣中社]] [[Category:別表神社]] [[Category:茨城百景]][[Category:qq]]

The plaque calligraphy is by Prince Akihito Komatsu.]] '''Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine''' (さかつらいそさきじんじゃ) is a Shinto shrine in Hitachinaka, Ibaraki. It is a Meishin-taisha listed in the Engishiki, formerly ranked kokuhei chusha, and currently a Beppyo shrine of Jinja Honcho. === Overview === The shrine stands on a coastal cape facing the Pacific Ocean. It is closely connected with {{ill|lt=Oarai Isosaki Shrine|Q11437230|WD=Q11437230|1=Oarai Isosaki Shrine}} across the Naka River, and the two are often regarded as forming a paired cult. === Enshrined deities === ; Main deity * {{ill|lt=Sukunahikona|Q3275687|WD=Q3275687|lt=Sukunahikona-no-Mikoto|1=Sukunabikona}} ; Co-enshrined * {{ill|WD=Q276944|lt=Okuninushi|Q276944|WD=Q276944|lt=Onamochi-no-Mikoto|1=Ōkuninushi}} The two-deity pairing is common because both appear together in kuni-zukuri myths. At this shrine, Sukunahikona is also associated with Ebisu and Onamochi with Daikokuten. === History === According to the ''Nihon Montoku Tenno Jitsuroku'' (856), divine signs appeared at Oarai Isosaki, with miraculous stones and an oracle declaring the returning deities Onamochi and Sukunahikona. Tradition says Onamochi was enshrined at Oarai and Sukunahikona at Sakatsura, establishing both shrines. The shrine name is linked to a local "reverse-tilting" rock formation (saka-tsura). Later, it came to be written with the character for sake (酒). In the Engishiki, it appears as "Sakare Isosaki Yakushi Bosatsu Shrine" in Naka District, Hitachi Province, and is listed as Meishin-taisha. It declined in the medieval period and lost its buildings; in the early modern period it was restored under Mito domain patronage by Tokugawa Mitsukuni and Tokugawa Tsunaeda, with relocation to the current site. In 1885 it was ranked kokuhei chusha. The official modern name is Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine. === Divine rank === * 857-08-07: entered official shrine register * 857-10-15: granted title "Yakushi Bosatsu Meishin" === Precinct === Notable features include: * Carving of squirrels and grapes above the haiden front (traditionally attributed to Jingoro Hidari) * Komainu at the second torii by Showa-era stonemason Iizuka Hyokichi * Broadleaf tree-lined approach (camellia, tabunoki, sudajii), designated natural monument of Ibaraki Prefecture 酒列磯前神社 本殿.JPG|Honden 酒列磯前神社 拝殿.JPG|Haiden 酒列磯前神社 水戸斉昭公腰かけの石.JPG|Seat stone of Tokugawa Nariaki 酒列磯前神社 二の鳥居.JPG|Second torii 酒列磯前神社 参道.JPG|Approach woodland (prefectural natural monument) === Subsidiary shrines === * Sakatsura Chinreisha (for 506 war dead from Russo-Japanese War to WWII) * Inari Shrine * Tenmangu * Kotohira Shrine * Fuji Shrine * Suijin Shrine === Cultural properties === === Ibaraki Prefecture designated natural monument === * Woodland of Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine (designated 2005) === Site information === * Address: Isozaki-cho 4607-2, Hitachinaka, Ibaraki * Access: Hitachinaka Seaside Railway Minato Line, Ajigaura Station, about 15 minutes on foot === Notes === {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist}} === External links === * [https://sakatura.org/ Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine] (official site) * Ibaraki Association of Shinto Shrines page * Kokugakuin source compilation page {{神道 横}}{{茨城県の神社一覧目次}} {{Normdaten}} == Categories == [[Category:Wikidata generated shikinaisha pages|Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine]][[Category:Shikinaisha|Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine]][[Category:pages]][[Category:pages]] [[Category:Beppyo Shrine]] [[Category:Kokuhei-sha]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Hitachi Province]] [[Category:pages]] [[Category:茨城県の神社]] [[Category:ひたちなか市の歴史]] [[Category:ひたちなか市の建築物]] [[Category:名神大社]] [[Category:常陸国の式内社|名さかつらいそさきしんしや]] [[Category:国幣中社]] [[Category:別表神社]] [[Category:茨城百景]][[Category:qq]]

The plaque calligraphy is by Prince Akihito Komatsu.]] '''Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine''' (さかつらいそさきじんじゃ) is a Shinto shrine in Hitachinaka, Ibaraki. It is a Meishin-taisha listed in the Engishiki, formerly ranked kokuhei chusha, and currently a Beppyo shrine of Jinja Honcho. === Overview === The shrine stands on a coastal cape facing the Pacific Ocean. It is closely connected with {{ill|lt=Oarai Isosaki Shrine|Q11437230|WD=Q11437230|1=Oarai Isosaki Shrine}} across the Naka River, and the two are often regarded as forming a paired cult. === Enshrined deities === ; Main deity * {{ill|lt=Sukunahikona|Q3275687|WD=Q3275687|lt=Sukunahikona-no-Mikoto|1=Sukunabikona}} ; Co-enshrined * {{ill|WD=Q276944|lt=Okuninushi|Q276944|WD=Q276944|lt=Onamochi-no-Mikoto|1=Ōkuninushi}} The two-deity pairing is common because both appear together in kuni-zukuri myths. At this shrine, Sukunahikona is also associated with Ebisu and Onamochi with Daikokuten. === History === According to the ''Nihon Montoku Tenno Jitsuroku'' (856), divine signs appeared at Oarai Isosaki, with miraculous stones and an oracle declaring the returning deities Onamochi and Sukunahikona. Tradition says Onamochi was enshrined at Oarai and Sukunahikona at Sakatsura, establishing both shrines. The shrine name is linked to a local "reverse-tilting" rock formation (saka-tsura). Later, it came to be written with the character for sake (酒). In the Engishiki, it appears as "Sakare Isosaki Yakushi Bosatsu Shrine" in Naka District, Hitachi Province, and is listed as Meishin-taisha. It declined in the medieval period and lost its buildings; in the early modern period it was restored under Mito domain patronage by Tokugawa Mitsukuni and Tokugawa Tsunaeda, with relocation to the current site. In 1885 it was ranked kokuhei chusha. The official modern name is Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine. === Divine rank === * 857-08-07: entered official shrine register * 857-10-15: granted title "Yakushi Bosatsu Meishin" === Precinct === Notable features include: * Carving of squirrels and grapes above the haiden front (traditionally attributed to Jingoro Hidari) * Komainu at the second torii by Showa-era stonemason Iizuka Hyokichi * Broadleaf tree-lined approach (camellia, tabunoki, sudajii), designated natural monument of Ibaraki Prefecture 酒列磯前神社 本殿.JPG|Honden 酒列磯前神社 拝殿.JPG|Haiden 酒列磯前神社 水戸斉昭公腰かけの石.JPG|Seat stone of Tokugawa Nariaki 酒列磯前神社 二の鳥居.JPG|Second torii 酒列磯前神社 参道.JPG|Approach woodland (prefectural natural monument) === Subsidiary shrines === * Sakatsura Chinreisha (for 506 war dead from Russo-Japanese War to WWII) * Inari Shrine * Tenmangu * Kotohira Shrine * Fuji Shrine * Suijin Shrine === Cultural properties === === Ibaraki Prefecture designated natural monument === * Woodland of Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine (designated 2005) === Site information === * Address: Isozaki-cho 4607-2, Hitachinaka, Ibaraki * Access: Hitachinaka Seaside Railway Minato Line, Ajigaura Station, about 15 minutes on foot === Notes === {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist}} === External links === * [https://sakatura.org/ Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine] (official site) * Ibaraki Association of Shinto Shrines page * Kokugakuin source compilation page {{神道 横}}{{茨城県の神社一覧目次}} {{Normdaten}} == Categories == [[Category:Wikidata generated shikinaisha pages|Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine]][[Category:Shikinaisha|Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine]][[Category:pages]][[Category:pages]] [[Category:Beppyo Shrine]] [[Category:Kokuhei-sha]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Hitachi Province]] [[Category:pages]] [[Category:茨城県の神社]] [[Category:Municipal History of Hitachinaka]] [[Category:ひたちなか市の建築物]] [[Category:名神大社]] [[Category:常陸国の式内社|名さかつらいそさきしんしや]] [[Category:国幣中社]] [[Category:別表神社]] [[Category:茨城百景]][[Category:qq]]
