The plaque calligraphy is by Prince Akihito Komatsu.]] '''Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine''' (さかつらいそさきじんじゃ) is a Shinto shrine in Hitachinaka, Ibaraki. It is a Meishin-taisha listed in the Engishiki, formerly ranked kokuhei chusha, and currently a Beppyo shrine of Jinja Honcho. === Overview === The shrine stands on a coastal cape facing the Pacific Ocean. It is closely connected with {{ill|lt=Oarai Isosaki Shrine|Q11437230|WD=Q11437230|1=Oarai Isosaki Shrine}} across the Naka River, and the two are often regarded as forming a paired cult. === Enshrined deities === ; Main deity * {{ill|lt=Sukunahikona|Q3275687|WD=Q3275687|lt=Sukunahikona-no-Mikoto|1=Sukunabikona}} ; Co-enshrined * {{ill|WD=Q276944|lt=Okuninushi|Q276944|WD=Q276944|lt=Onamochi-no-Mikoto|1=Ōkuninushi}} The two-deity pairing is common because both appear together in kuni-zukuri myths. At this shrine, Sukunahikona is also associated with Ebisu and Onamochi with Daikokuten. === History === According to the ''Nihon Montoku Tenno Jitsuroku'' (856), divine signs appeared at Oarai Isosaki, with miraculous stones and an oracle declaring the returning deities Onamochi and Sukunahikona. Tradition says Onamochi was enshrined at Oarai and Sukunahikona at Sakatsura, establishing both shrines. The shrine name is linked to a local "reverse-tilting" rock formation (saka-tsura). Later, it came to be written with the character for sake (酒). In the Engishiki, it appears as "Sakare Isosaki Yakushi Bosatsu Shrine" in Naka District, Hitachi Province, and is listed as Meishin-taisha. It declined in the medieval period and lost its buildings; in the early modern period it was restored under Mito domain patronage by Tokugawa Mitsukuni and Tokugawa Tsunaeda, with relocation to the current site. In 1885 it was ranked kokuhei chusha. The official modern name is Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine. === Divine rank === * 857-08-07: entered official shrine register * 857-10-15: granted title "Yakushi Bosatsu Meishin" === Precinct === Notable features include: * Carving of squirrels and grapes above the haiden front (traditionally attributed to Jingoro Hidari) * Komainu at the second torii by Showa-era stonemason Iizuka Hyokichi * Broadleaf tree-lined approach (camellia, tabunoki, sudajii), designated natural monument of Ibaraki Prefecture 酒列磯前神社 本殿.JPG|Honden 酒列磯前神社 拝殿.JPG|Haiden 酒列磯前神社 水戸斉昭公腰かけの石.JPG|Seat stone of Tokugawa Nariaki 酒列磯前神社 二の鳥居.JPG|Second torii 酒列磯前神社 参道.JPG|Approach woodland (prefectural natural monument) === Subsidiary shrines === * Sakatsura Chinreisha (for 506 war dead from Russo-Japanese War to WWII) * Inari Shrine * Tenmangu * Kotohira Shrine * Fuji Shrine * Suijin Shrine === Cultural properties === === Ibaraki Prefecture designated natural monument === * Woodland of Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine (designated 2005) === Site information === * Address: Isozaki-cho 4607-2, Hitachinaka, Ibaraki * Access: Hitachinaka Seaside Railway Minato Line, Ajigaura Station, about 15 minutes on foot === Notes === {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist}} === External links === * [https://sakatura.org/ Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine] (official site) * Ibaraki Association of Shinto Shrines page * Kokugakuin source compilation page {{神道 横}}{{茨城県の神社一覧目次}} {{Normdaten}} == Categories == [[Category:Wikidata generated shikinaisha pages|Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine]][[Category:Shikinaisha|Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine]][[Category:pages]][[Category:pages]] [[Category:Beppyo Shrine]] [[Category:Kokuhei-sha]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Hitachi Province]] [[Category:pages]] [[Category:茨城県の神社]] [[Category:Municipal History of Hitachinaka]] [[Category:ひたちなか市の建築物]] [[Category:名神大社]] [[Category:常陸国の式内社|名さかつらいそさきしんしや]] [[Category:国幣中社]] [[Category:Beppyo shrines]] [[Category:茨城百景]][[Category:qq]]

The plaque calligraphy is by Prince Akihito Komatsu.]] '''Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine''' (さかつらいそさきじんじゃ) is a Shinto shrine in Hitachinaka, Ibaraki. It is a Meishin-taisha listed in the Engishiki, formerly ranked kokuhei chusha, and currently a Beppyo shrine of Jinja Honcho. === Overview === The shrine stands on a coastal cape facing the Pacific Ocean. It is closely connected with {{ill|lt=Oarai Isosaki Shrine|Q11437230|WD=Q11437230|1=Oarai Isosaki Shrine}} across the Naka River, and the two are often regarded as forming a paired cult. === Enshrined deities === ; Main deity * {{ill|lt=Sukunahikona|Q3275687|WD=Q3275687|lt=Sukunahikona-no-Mikoto|1=Sukunabikona}} ; Co-enshrined * {{ill|WD=Q276944|lt=Okuninushi|Q276944|WD=Q276944|lt=Onamochi-no-Mikoto|1=Ōkuninushi}} The two-deity pairing is common because both appear together in kuni-zukuri myths. At this shrine, Sukunahikona is also associated with Ebisu and Onamochi with Daikokuten. === History === According to the ''Nihon Montoku Tenno Jitsuroku'' (856), divine signs appeared at Oarai Isosaki, with miraculous stones and an oracle declaring the returning deities Onamochi and Sukunahikona. Tradition says Onamochi was enshrined at Oarai and Sukunahikona at Sakatsura, establishing both shrines. The shrine name is linked to a local "reverse-tilting" rock formation (saka-tsura). Later, it came to be written with the character for sake (酒). In the Engishiki, it appears as "Sakare Isosaki Yakushi Bosatsu Shrine" in Naka District, Hitachi Province, and is listed as Meishin-taisha. It declined in the medieval period and lost its buildings; in the early modern period it was restored under Mito domain patronage by Tokugawa Mitsukuni and Tokugawa Tsunaeda, with relocation to the current site. In 1885 it was ranked kokuhei chusha. The official modern name is Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine. === Divine rank === * 857-08-07: entered official shrine register * 857-10-15: granted title "Yakushi Bosatsu Meishin" === Precinct === Notable features include: * Carving of squirrels and grapes above the haiden front (traditionally attributed to Jingoro Hidari) * Komainu at the second torii by Showa-era stonemason Iizuka Hyokichi * Broadleaf tree-lined approach (camellia, tabunoki, sudajii), designated natural monument of Ibaraki Prefecture 酒列磯前神社 本殿.JPG|Honden 酒列磯前神社 拝殿.JPG|Haiden 酒列磯前神社 水戸斉昭公腰かけの石.JPG|Seat stone of Tokugawa Nariaki 酒列磯前神社 二の鳥居.JPG|Second torii 酒列磯前神社 参道.JPG|Approach woodland (prefectural natural monument) === Subsidiary shrines === * Sakatsura Chinreisha (for 506 war dead from Russo-Japanese War to WWII) * Inari Shrine * Tenmangu * Kotohira Shrine * Fuji Shrine * Suijin Shrine === Cultural properties === === Ibaraki Prefecture designated natural monument === * Woodland of Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine (designated 2005) === Site information === * Address: Isozaki-cho 4607-2, Hitachinaka, Ibaraki * Access: Hitachinaka Seaside Railway Minato Line, Ajigaura Station, about 15 minutes on foot === Notes === {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist}} === External links === * [https://sakatura.org/ Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine] (official site) * Ibaraki Association of Shinto Shrines page * Kokugakuin source compilation page {{神道 横}}{{茨城県の神社一覧目次}} {{Normdaten}} == Categories == [[Category:Wikidata generated shikinaisha pages|Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine]][[Category:Shikinaisha|Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine]][[Category:pages]][[Category:pages]] [[Category:Beppyo Shrine]] [[Category:Kokuhei-sha]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Hitachi Province]] [[Category:pages]] [[Category:茨城県の神社]] [[Category:Municipal History of Hitachinaka]] [[Category:ひたちなか市の建築物]] [[Category:Myōjin Taisha]] [[Category:常陸国の式内社|名さかつらいそさきしんしや]] [[Category:国幣中社]] [[Category:Beppyo shrines]] [[Category:茨城百景]][[Category:qq]]

The plaque calligraphy is by Prince Akihito Komatsu.]] '''Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine''' (さかつらいそさきじんじゃ) is a Shinto shrine in Hitachinaka, Ibaraki. It is a Meishin-taisha listed in the Engishiki, formerly ranked kokuhei chusha, and currently a Beppyo shrine of Jinja Honcho. === Overview === The shrine stands on a coastal cape facing the Pacific Ocean. It is closely connected with {{ill|lt=Oarai Isosaki Shrine|Q11437230|WD=Q11437230|1=Oarai Isosaki Shrine}} across the Naka River, and the two are often regarded as forming a paired cult. === Enshrined deities === ; Main deity * {{ill|lt=Sukunahikona|Q3275687|WD=Q3275687|lt=Sukunahikona-no-Mikoto|1=Sukunabikona}} ; Co-enshrined * {{ill|WD=Q276944|lt=Okuninushi|Q276944|WD=Q276944|lt=Onamochi-no-Mikoto|1=Ōkuninushi}} The two-deity pairing is common because both appear together in kuni-zukuri myths. At this shrine, Sukunahikona is also associated with Ebisu and Onamochi with Daikokuten. === History === According to the ''Nihon Montoku Tenno Jitsuroku'' (856), divine signs appeared at Oarai Isosaki, with miraculous stones and an oracle declaring the returning deities Onamochi and Sukunahikona. Tradition says Onamochi was enshrined at Oarai and Sukunahikona at Sakatsura, establishing both shrines. The shrine name is linked to a local "reverse-tilting" rock formation (saka-tsura). Later, it came to be written with the character for sake (酒). In the Engishiki, it appears as "Sakare Isosaki Yakushi Bosatsu Shrine" in Naka District, Hitachi Province, and is listed as Meishin-taisha. It declined in the medieval period and lost its buildings; in the early modern period it was restored under Mito domain patronage by Tokugawa Mitsukuni and Tokugawa Tsunaeda, with relocation to the current site. In 1885 it was ranked kokuhei chusha. The official modern name is Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine. === Divine rank === * 857-08-07: entered official shrine register * 857-10-15: granted title "Yakushi Bosatsu Meishin" === Precinct === Notable features include: * Carving of squirrels and grapes above the haiden front (traditionally attributed to Jingoro Hidari) * Komainu at the second torii by Showa-era stonemason Iizuka Hyokichi * Broadleaf tree-lined approach (camellia, tabunoki, sudajii), designated natural monument of Ibaraki Prefecture 酒列磯前神社 本殿.JPG|Honden 酒列磯前神社 拝殿.JPG|Haiden 酒列磯前神社 水戸斉昭公腰かけの石.JPG|Seat stone of Tokugawa Nariaki 酒列磯前神社 二の鳥居.JPG|Second torii 酒列磯前神社 参道.JPG|Approach woodland (prefectural natural monument) === Subsidiary shrines === * Sakatsura Chinreisha (for 506 war dead from Russo-Japanese War to WWII) * Inari Shrine * Tenmangu * Kotohira Shrine * Fuji Shrine * Suijin Shrine === Cultural properties === === Ibaraki Prefecture designated natural monument === * Woodland of Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine (designated 2005) === Site information === * Address: Isozaki-cho 4607-2, Hitachinaka, Ibaraki * Access: Hitachinaka Seaside Railway Minato Line, Ajigaura Station, about 15 minutes on foot === Notes === {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist}} === External links === * [https://sakatura.org/ Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine] (official site) * Ibaraki Association of Shinto Shrines page * Kokugakuin source compilation page {{神道 横}}{{茨城県の神社一覧目次}} {{Normdaten}} == Categories == [[Category:Wikidata generated shikinaisha pages|Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine]][[Category:Shikinaisha|Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine]][[Category:pages]][[Category:pages]] [[Category:Beppyo Shrine]] [[Category:Kokuhei-sha]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Hitachi Province]] [[Category:pages]] [[Category:茨城県の神社]] [[Category:Municipal History of Hitachinaka]] [[Category:ひたちなか市の建築物]] [[Category:Myōjin Taisha]] [[Category:常陸国の式内社|名さかつらいそさきしんしや]] [[Category:Kokuhei Chūsha]] [[Category:Beppyo shrines]] [[Category:茨城百景]][[Category:qq]]

The plaque calligraphy is by Prince Akihito Komatsu.]] '''Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine''' (さかつらいそさきじんじゃ) is a Shinto shrine in Hitachinaka, Ibaraki. It is a Meishin-taisha listed in the Engishiki, formerly ranked kokuhei chusha, and currently a Beppyo shrine of Jinja Honcho. === Overview === The shrine stands on a coastal cape facing the Pacific Ocean. It is closely connected with {{ill|lt=Oarai Isosaki Shrine|Q11437230|WD=Q11437230|1=Oarai Isosaki Shrine}} across the Naka River, and the two are often regarded as forming a paired cult. === Enshrined deities === ; Main deity * {{ill|lt=Sukunahikona|Q3275687|WD=Q3275687|lt=Sukunahikona-no-Mikoto|1=Sukunabikona}} ; Co-enshrined * {{ill|WD=Q276944|lt=Okuninushi|Q276944|WD=Q276944|lt=Onamochi-no-Mikoto|1=Ōkuninushi}} The two-deity pairing is common because both appear together in kuni-zukuri myths. At this shrine, Sukunahikona is also associated with Ebisu and Onamochi with Daikokuten. === History === According to the ''Nihon Montoku Tenno Jitsuroku'' (856), divine signs appeared at Oarai Isosaki, with miraculous stones and an oracle declaring the returning deities Onamochi and Sukunahikona. Tradition says Onamochi was enshrined at Oarai and Sukunahikona at Sakatsura, establishing both shrines. The shrine name is linked to a local "reverse-tilting" rock formation (saka-tsura). Later, it came to be written with the character for sake (酒). In the Engishiki, it appears as "Sakare Isosaki Yakushi Bosatsu Shrine" in Naka District, Hitachi Province, and is listed as Meishin-taisha. It declined in the medieval period and lost its buildings; in the early modern period it was restored under Mito domain patronage by Tokugawa Mitsukuni and Tokugawa Tsunaeda, with relocation to the current site. In 1885 it was ranked kokuhei chusha. The official modern name is Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine. === Divine rank === * 857-08-07: entered official shrine register * 857-10-15: granted title "Yakushi Bosatsu Meishin" === Precinct === Notable features include: * Carving of squirrels and grapes above the haiden front (traditionally attributed to Jingoro Hidari) * Komainu at the second torii by Showa-era stonemason Iizuka Hyokichi * Broadleaf tree-lined approach (camellia, tabunoki, sudajii), designated natural monument of Ibaraki Prefecture 酒列磯前神社 本殿.JPG|Honden 酒列磯前神社 拝殿.JPG|Haiden 酒列磯前神社 水戸斉昭公腰かけの石.JPG|Seat stone of Tokugawa Nariaki 酒列磯前神社 二の鳥居.JPG|Second torii 酒列磯前神社 参道.JPG|Approach woodland (prefectural natural monument) === Subsidiary shrines === * Sakatsura Chinreisha (for 506 war dead from Russo-Japanese War to WWII) * Inari Shrine * Tenmangu * Kotohira Shrine * Fuji Shrine * Suijin Shrine === Cultural properties === === Ibaraki Prefecture designated natural monument === * Woodland of Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine (designated 2005) === Site information === * Address: Isozaki-cho 4607-2, Hitachinaka, Ibaraki * Access: Hitachinaka Seaside Railway Minato Line, Ajigaura Station, about 15 minutes on foot === Notes === {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist}} === External links === * [https://sakatura.org/ Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine] (official site) * Ibaraki Association of Shinto Shrines page * Kokugakuin source compilation page {{神道 横}}{{茨城県の神社一覧目次}} {{Normdaten}} == Categories == [[Category:Wikidata generated shikinaisha pages|Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine]][[Category:Shikinaisha|Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine]][[Category:pages]][[Category:pages]] [[Category:Beppyo Shrine]] [[Category:Kokuhei-sha]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Hitachi Province]] [[Category:pages]] [[Category:茨城県の神社]] [[Category:Municipal History of Hitachinaka]] [[Category:ひたちなか市の建築物]] [[Category:Myōjin Taisha]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Hitachi Province]] [[Category:Kokuhei Chūsha]] [[Category:Beppyo shrines]] [[Category:茨城百景]][[Category:qq]]

The plaque calligraphy is by Prince Akihito Komatsu.]] '''Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine''' (さかつらいそさきじんじゃ) is a Shinto shrine in Hitachinaka, Ibaraki. It is a Meishin-taisha listed in the Engishiki, formerly ranked kokuhei chusha, and currently a Beppyo shrine of Jinja Honcho. === Overview === The shrine stands on a coastal cape facing the Pacific Ocean. It is closely connected with {{ill|lt=Oarai Isosaki Shrine|Q11437230|WD=Q11437230|1=Oarai Isosaki Shrine}} across the Naka River, and the two are often regarded as forming a paired cult. === Enshrined deities === ; Main deity * {{ill|lt=Sukunahikona|Q3275687|WD=Q3275687|lt=Sukunahikona-no-Mikoto|1=Sukunabikona}} ; Co-enshrined * {{ill|WD=Q276944|lt=Okuninushi|Q276944|WD=Q276944|lt=Onamochi-no-Mikoto|1=Ōkuninushi}} The two-deity pairing is common because both appear together in kuni-zukuri myths. At this shrine, Sukunahikona is also associated with Ebisu and Onamochi with Daikokuten. === History === According to the ''Nihon Montoku Tenno Jitsuroku'' (856), divine signs appeared at Oarai Isosaki, with miraculous stones and an oracle declaring the returning deities Onamochi and Sukunahikona. Tradition says Onamochi was enshrined at Oarai and Sukunahikona at Sakatsura, establishing both shrines. The shrine name is linked to a local "reverse-tilting" rock formation (saka-tsura). Later, it came to be written with the character for sake (酒). In the Engishiki, it appears as "Sakare Isosaki Yakushi Bosatsu Shrine" in Naka District, Hitachi Province, and is listed as Meishin-taisha. It declined in the medieval period and lost its buildings; in the early modern period it was restored under Mito domain patronage by Tokugawa Mitsukuni and Tokugawa Tsunaeda, with relocation to the current site. In 1885 it was ranked kokuhei chusha. The official modern name is Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine. === Divine rank === * 857-08-07: entered official shrine register * 857-10-15: granted title "Yakushi Bosatsu Meishin" === Precinct === Notable features include: * Carving of squirrels and grapes above the haiden front (traditionally attributed to Jingoro Hidari) * Komainu at the second torii by Showa-era stonemason Iizuka Hyokichi * Broadleaf tree-lined approach (camellia, tabunoki, sudajii), designated natural monument of Ibaraki Prefecture 酒列磯前神社 本殿.JPG|Honden 酒列磯前神社 拝殿.JPG|Haiden 酒列磯前神社 水戸斉昭公腰かけの石.JPG|Seat stone of Tokugawa Nariaki 酒列磯前神社 二の鳥居.JPG|Second torii 酒列磯前神社 参道.JPG|Approach woodland (prefectural natural monument) === Subsidiary shrines === * Sakatsura Chinreisha (for 506 war dead from Russo-Japanese War to WWII) * Inari Shrine * Tenmangu * Kotohira Shrine * Fuji Shrine * Suijin Shrine === Cultural properties === === Ibaraki Prefecture designated natural monument === * Woodland of Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine (designated 2005) === Site information === * Address: Isozaki-cho 4607-2, Hitachinaka, Ibaraki * Access: Hitachinaka Seaside Railway Minato Line, Ajigaura Station, about 15 minutes on foot === Notes === {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist}} === External links === * [https://sakatura.org/ Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine] (official site) * Ibaraki Association of Shinto Shrines page * Kokugakuin source compilation page {{神道 横}}{{茨城県の神社一覧目次}} {{Normdaten}} == Categories == [[Category:Wikidata generated shikinaisha pages|Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine]][[Category:Shikinaisha|Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine]][[Category:pages]][[Category:pages]] [[Category:Beppyo Shrine]] [[Category:Kokuhei-sha]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Hitachi Province]] [[Category:pages]] [[Category:茨城県の神社]] [[Category:Municipal History of Hitachinaka]] [[Category:ひたちなか市の建築物]] [[Category:Myōjin Taisha]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Hitachi Province]] [[Category:Kokuhei Chūsha]] [[Category:Beppyo shrines]] [[Category:100 Views of Ibaraki]][[Category:qq]]

The plaque calligraphy is by Prince Akihito Komatsu.]] '''Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine''' (さかつらいそさきじんじゃ) is a Shinto shrine in Hitachinaka, Ibaraki. It is a Meishin-taisha listed in the Engishiki, formerly ranked kokuhei chusha, and currently a Beppyo shrine of Jinja Honcho. === Overview === The shrine stands on a coastal cape facing the Pacific Ocean. It is closely connected with {{ill|lt=Oarai Isosaki Shrine|Q11437230|WD=Q11437230|1=Oarai Isosaki Shrine}} across the Naka River, and the two are often regarded as forming a paired cult. === Enshrined deities === ; Main deity * {{ill|lt=Sukunahikona|Q3275687|WD=Q3275687|lt=Sukunahikona-no-Mikoto|1=Sukunabikona}} ; Co-enshrined * {{ill|WD=Q276944|lt=Okuninushi|Q276944|WD=Q276944|lt=Onamochi-no-Mikoto|1=Ōkuninushi}} The two-deity pairing is common because both appear together in kuni-zukuri myths. At this shrine, Sukunahikona is also associated with Ebisu and Onamochi with Daikokuten. === History === According to the ''Nihon Montoku Tenno Jitsuroku'' (856), divine signs appeared at Oarai Isosaki, with miraculous stones and an oracle declaring the returning deities Onamochi and Sukunahikona. Tradition says Onamochi was enshrined at Oarai and Sukunahikona at Sakatsura, establishing both shrines. The shrine name is linked to a local "reverse-tilting" rock formation (saka-tsura). Later, it came to be written with the character for sake (酒). In the Engishiki, it appears as "Sakare Isosaki Yakushi Bosatsu Shrine" in Naka District, Hitachi Province, and is listed as Meishin-taisha. It declined in the medieval period and lost its buildings; in the early modern period it was restored under Mito domain patronage by Tokugawa Mitsukuni and Tokugawa Tsunaeda, with relocation to the current site. In 1885 it was ranked kokuhei chusha. The official modern name is Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine. === Divine rank === * 857-08-07: entered official shrine register * 857-10-15: granted title "Yakushi Bosatsu Meishin" === Precinct === Notable features include: * Carving of squirrels and grapes above the haiden front (traditionally attributed to Jingoro Hidari) * Komainu at the second torii by Showa-era stonemason Iizuka Hyokichi * Broadleaf tree-lined approach (camellia, tabunoki, sudajii), designated natural monument of Ibaraki Prefecture 酒列磯前神社 本殿.JPG|Honden 酒列磯前神社 拝殿.JPG|Haiden 酒列磯前神社 水戸斉昭公腰かけの石.JPG|Seat stone of Tokugawa The plaque calligraphy is by Prince Akihito Komatsu.]] '''Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine''' (さかつらいそさきじんじゃ) is a Shinto shrine in Hitachinaka, Ibaraki. It is a Meishin-taisha listed in the Engishiki, formerly ranked kokuhei chusha, and currently a Beppyo shrine of Jinja Honcho. === Overview === The shrine stands on a coastal cape facing the Pacific Ocean. It is closely connected with {{ill|lt=Oarai Isosaki Shrine|Q11437230|WD=Q11437230|1=Oarai Isosaki Shrine}} across the Naka River, and the two are often regarded as forming a paired cult. === Enshrined deities === ; Main deity * {{ill|lt=Sukunahikona|Q3275687|WD=Q3275687|lt=Sukunahikona-no-Mikoto|1=Sukunabikona}} ; Co-enshrined * {{ill|WD=Q276944|lt=Okuninushi|Q276944|WD=Q276944|lt=Onamochi-no-Mikoto|1=Ōkuninushi}} The two-deity pairing is common because both appear together in kuni-zukuri myths. At this shrine, Sukunahikona is also associated with Ebisu and Onamochi with Daikokuten. === History === According to the ''Nihon Montoku Tenno Jitsuroku'' (856), divine signs appeared at Oarai Isosaki, with miraculous stones and an oracle declaring the returning deities Onamochi and Sukunahikona. Tradition says Onamochi was enshrined at Oarai and Sukunahikona at Sakatsura, establishing both shrines. The shrine name is linked to a local "reverse-tilting" rock formation (saka-tsura). Later, it came to be written with the character for sake (酒). In the Engishiki, it appears as "Sakare Isosaki Yakushi Bosatsu Shrine" in Naka District, Hitachi Province, and is listed as Meishin-taisha. It declined in the medieval period and lost its buildings; in the early modern period it was restored under Mito domain patronage by Tokugawa Mitsukuni and Tokugawa Tsunaeda, with relocation to the current site. In 1885 it was ranked kokuhei chusha. The official modern name is Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine. === Divine rank === * 857-08-07: entered official shrine register * 857-10-15: granted title "Yakushi Bosatsu Meishin" === Precinct === Notable features include: * Carving of squirrels and grapes above the haiden front (traditionally attributed to Jingoro Hidari) * Komainu at the second torii by Showa-era stonemason Iizuka Hyokichi * Broadleaf tree-lined approach (camellia, tabunoki, sudajii), designated natural monument of Ibaraki Prefecture 酒列磯前神社 本殿.JPG|Honden 酒列磯前神社 拝殿.JPG|Haiden 酒列磯前神社 水戸斉昭公腰かけの石.JPG|Seat stone of Tokugawa Nariaki 酒列磯前神社 二の鳥居.JPG|Second torii 酒列磯前神社 参道.JPG|Approach woodland (prefectural natural monument) === Subsidiary shrines === * Sakatsura Chinreisha (for 506 war dead from Russo-Japanese War to WWII) * Inari Shrine * Tenmangu * Kotohira Shrine * Fuji Shrine * Suijin Shrine === Cultural properties === === Ibaraki Prefecture designated natural monument === * Woodland of Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine (designated 2005) === Site information === * Address: Isozaki-cho 4607-2, Hitachinaka, Ibaraki * Access: Hitachinaka Seaside Railway Minato Line, Ajigaura Station, about 15 minutes on foot === Notes === {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist}} === External links === * [https://sakatura.org/ Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine] (official site) * Ibaraki Association of Shinto Shrines page * Kokugakuin source compilation page {{神道 横}}{{茨城県の神社一覧目次}} {{Normdaten}} == Categories == [[Category:Wikidata generated shikinaisha pages|Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine]][[Category:Shikinaisha|Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine]][[Category:pages]][[Category:pages]] [[Category:Beppyo Shrine]] [[Category:Kokuhei-sha]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Hitachi Province]] [[Category:pages]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Ibaraki Prefecture]] [[Category:Municipal History of Hitachinaka]] [[Category:ひたちなか市の建築物]] [[Category:Myōjin Taisha]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Hitachi Province]] [[Category:Kokuhei Chūsha]] [[Category:Beppyo shrines]] [[Category:100 Views of Ibaraki]]

The plaque calligraphy is by Prince Akihito Komatsu.]] '''Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine''' (さかつらいそさきじんじゃ) is a Shinto shrine in Hitachinaka, Ibaraki. It is a Meishin-taisha listed in the Engishiki, formerly ranked kokuhei chusha, and currently a Beppyo shrine of Jinja Honcho. === Overview === The shrine stands on a coastal cape facing the Pacific Ocean. It is closely connected with {{ill|lt=Oarai Isosaki Shrine|Q11437230|WD=Q11437230|1=Oarai Isosaki Shrine}} across the Naka River, and the two are often regarded as forming a paired cult. === Enshrined deities === ; Main deity * {{ill|lt=Sukunahikona|Q3275687|WD=Q3275687|lt=Sukunahikona-no-Mikoto|1=Sukunabikona}} ; Co-enshrined * {{ill|WD=Q276944|lt=Okuninushi|Q276944|WD=Q276944|lt=Onamochi-no-Mikoto|1=Ōkuninushi}} The two-deity pairing is common because both appear together in kuni-zukuri myths. At this shrine, Sukunahikona is also associated with Ebisu and Onamochi with Daikokuten. === History === According to the ''Nihon Montoku Tenno Jitsuroku'' (856), divine signs appeared at Oarai Isosaki, with miraculous stones and an oracle declaring the returning deities Onamochi and Sukunahikona. Tradition says Onamochi was enshrined at Oarai and Sukunahikona at Sakatsura, establishing both shrines. The shrine name is linked to a local "reverse-tilting" rock formation (saka-tsura). Later, it came to be written with the character for sake (酒). In the Engishiki, it appears as "Sakare Isosaki Yakushi Bosatsu Shrine" in Naka District, Hitachi Province, and is listed as Meishin-taisha. It declined in the medieval period and lost its buildings; in the early modern period it was restored under Mito domain patronage by Tokugawa Mitsukuni and Tokugawa Tsunaeda, with relocation to the current site. In 1885 it was ranked kokuhei chusha. The official modern name is Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine. === Divine rank === * 857-08-07: entered official shrine register * 857-10-15: granted title "Yakushi Bosatsu Meishin" === Precinct === Notable features include: * Carving of squirrels and grapes above the haiden front (traditionally attributed to Jingoro Hidari) * Komainu at the second torii by Showa-era stonemason Iizuka Hyokichi * Broadleaf tree-lined approach (camellia, tabunoki, sudajii), designated natural monument of Ibaraki Prefecture 酒列磯前神社 本殿.JPG|Honden 酒列磯前神社 拝殿.JPG|Haiden 酒列磯前神社 水戸斉昭公腰かけの石.JPG|Seat stone of Tokugawa Nariaki 酒列磯前神社 二の鳥居.JPG|Second torii 酒列磯前神社 参道.JPG|Approach woodland (prefectural natural monument) === Subsidiary shrines === * Sakatsura Chinreisha (for 506 war dead from Russo-Japanese War to WWII) * Inari Shrine * Tenmangu * Kotohira Shrine * Fuji Shrine * Suijin Shrine === Cultural properties === === Ibaraki Prefecture designated natural monument === * Woodland of Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine (designated 2005) === Site information === * Address: Isozaki-cho 4607-2, Hitachinaka, Ibaraki * Access: Hitachinaka Seaside Railway Minato Line, Ajigaura Station, about 15 minutes on foot === Notes === {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist}} === External links === * [https://sakatura.org/ Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine] (official site) * Ibaraki Association of Shinto Shrines page * Kokugakuin source compilation page {{神道 横}}{{茨城県の神社一覧目次}} {{Normdaten}} == Categories == [[Category:Wikidata generated shikinaisha pages|Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine]][[Category:Shikinaisha|Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine]][[Category:Beppyo Shrine]] [[Category:Kokuhei-sha]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Hitachi Province]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Ibaraki Prefecture]] [[Category:Municipal History of Hitachinaka]] [[Category:ひたちなか市の建築物]] [[Category:Myōjin Taisha]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Hitachi Province]] [[Category:Kokuhei Chūsha]] [[Category:Beppyo shrines]] [[Category:100 Views of Ibaraki]]

The plaque calligraphy is by Prince Akihito Komatsu.]] '''Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine''' (さかつらいそさきじんじゃ) is a Shinto shrine in Hitachinaka, Ibaraki. It is a Meishin-taisha listed in the Engishiki, formerly ranked kokuhei chusha, and currently a Beppyo shrine of Jinja Honcho. === Overview === The shrine stands on a coastal cape facing the Pacific Ocean. It is closely connected with {{ill|lt=Oarai Isosaki Shrine|Q11437230|WD=Q11437230|1=Oarai Isosaki Shrine}} across the Naka River, and the two are often regarded as forming a paired cult. === Enshrined deities === ; Main deity * {{ill|lt=Sukunahikona|Q3275687|WD=Q3275687|lt=Sukunahikona-no-Mikoto|1=Sukunabikona}} ; Co-enshrined * {{ill|WD=Q276944|lt=Okuninushi|Q276944|WD=Q276944|lt=Onamochi-no-Mikoto|1=Ōkuninushi}} The two-deity pairing is common because both appear together in kuni-zukuri myths. At this shrine, Sukunahikona is also associated with Ebisu and Onamochi with Daikokuten. === History === According to the ''Nihon Montoku Tenno Jitsuroku'' (856), divine signs appeared at Oarai Isosaki, with miraculous stones and an oracle declaring the returning deities Onamochi and Sukunahikona. Tradition says Onamochi was enshrined at Oarai and Sukunahikona at Sakatsura, establishing both shrines. The shrine name is linked to a local "reverse-tilting" rock formation (saka-tsura). Later, it came to be written with the character for sake (酒). In the Engishiki, it appears as "Sakare Isosaki Yakushi Bosatsu Shrine" in Naka District, Hitachi Province, and is listed as Meishin-taisha. It declined in the medieval period and lost its buildings; in the early modern period it was restored under Mito domain patronage by Tokugawa Mitsukuni and Tokugawa Tsunaeda, with relocation to the current site. In 1885 it was ranked kokuhei chusha. The official modern name is Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine. === Divine rank === * 857-08-07: entered official shrine register * 857-10-15: granted title "Yakushi Bosatsu Meishin" === Precinct === Notable features include: * Carving of squirrels and grapes above the haiden front (traditionally attributed to Jingoro Hidari) * Komainu at the second torii by Showa-era stonemason Iizuka Hyokichi * Broadleaf tree-lined approach (camellia, tabunoki, sudajii), designated natural monument of Ibaraki Prefecture 酒列磯前神社 本殿.JPG|Honden 酒列磯前神社 拝殿.JPG|Haiden 酒列磯前神社 水戸斉昭公腰かけの石.JPG|Seat stone of Tokugawa Nariaki 酒列磯前神社 二の鳥居.JPG|Second torii 酒列磯前神社 参道.JPG|Approach woodland (prefectural natural monument) === Subsidiary shrines === * Sakatsura Chinreisha (for 506 war dead from Russo-Japanese War to WWII) * Inari Shrine * Tenmangu * Kotohira Shrine * Fuji Shrine * Suijin Shrine === Cultural properties === === Ibaraki Prefecture designated natural monument === * Woodland of Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine (designated 2005) === Site information === * Address: Isozaki-cho 4607-2, Hitachinaka, Ibaraki * Access: Hitachinaka Seaside Railway Minato Line, Ajigaura Station, about 15 minutes on foot === Notes === {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist}} === External links === * [https://sakatura.org/ Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine] (official site) * Ibaraki Association of Shinto Shrines page * Kokugakuin source compilation page {{神道 横}}{{茨城県の神社一覧目次}} {{Normdaten}} == Categories == [[Category:Wikidata generated shikinaisha pages|Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine]][[Category:Shikinaisha|Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine]][[Category:Beppyo Shrine]] [[Category:Kokuhei-sha]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Hitachi Province]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Ibaraki Prefecture]] [[Category:Municipal History of Hitachinaka]] [[Category:Buildings in Hitachinaka]] [[Category:Myōjin Taisha]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Hitachi Province]] [[Category:Kokuhei Chūsha]] [[Category:Beppyo shrines]] [[Category:100 Views of Ibaraki]]

The plaque calligraphy is by Prince Akihito Komatsu.]] '''Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine''' (さかつらいそさきじんじゃ) is a Shinto shrine in Hitachinaka, Ibaraki. It is a Meishin-taisha listed in the Engishiki, formerly ranked kokuhei chusha, and currently a Beppyo shrine of Jinja Honcho. === Overview === The shrine stands on a coastal cape facing the Pacific Ocean. It is closely connected with {{ill|lt=Oarai Isosaki Shrine|Q11437230|WD=Q11437230|1=Oarai Isosaki Shrine}} across the Naka River, and the two are often regarded as forming a paired cult. === Enshrined deities === ; Main deity * {{ill|lt=Sukunahikona|Q3275687|WD=Q3275687|lt=Sukunahikona-no-Mikoto|1=Sukunabikona}} ; Co-enshrined * {{ill|WD=Q276944|lt=Okuninushi|Q276944|WD=Q276944|lt=Onamochi-no-Mikoto|1=Ōkuninushi}} The two-deity pairing is common because both appear together in kuni-zukuri myths. At this shrine, Sukunahikona is also associated with Ebisu and Onamochi with Daikokuten. === History === According to the ''Nihon Montoku Tenno Jitsuroku'' (856), divine signs appeared at Oarai Isosaki, with miraculous stones and an oracle declaring the returning deities Onamochi and Sukunahikona. Tradition says Onamochi was enshrined at Oarai and Sukunahikona at Sakatsura, establishing both shrines. The shrine name is linked to a local "reverse-tilting" rock formation (saka-tsura). Later, it came to be written with the character for sake (酒). In the Engishiki, it appears as "Sakare Isosaki Yakushi Bosatsu Shrine" in Naka District, Hitachi Province, and is listed as Meishin-taisha. It declined in the medieval period and lost its buildings; in the early modern period it was restored under Mito domain patronage by Tokugawa Mitsukuni and Tokugawa Tsunaeda, with relocation to the current site. In 1885 it was ranked kokuhei chusha. The official modern name is Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine. === Divine rank === * 857-08-07: entered official shrine register * 857-10-15: granted title "Yakushi Bosatsu Meishin" === Precinct === Notable features include: * Carving of squirrels and grapes above the haiden front (traditionally attributed to Jingoro Hidari) * Komainu at the second torii by Showa-era stonemason Iizuka Hyokichi * Broadleaf tree-lined approach (camellia, tabunoki, sudajii), designated natural monument of Ibaraki Prefecture 酒列磯前神社 本殿.JPG|Honden 酒列磯前神社 拝殿.JPG|Haiden 酒列磯前神社 水戸斉昭公腰かけの石.JPG|Seat stone of Tokugawa Nariaki 酒列磯前神社 二の鳥居.JPG|Second torii 酒列磯前神社 参道.JPG|Approach woodland (prefectural natural monument) === Subsidiary shrines === * Sakatsura Chinreisha (for 506 war dead from Russo-Japanese War to WWII) * Inari Shrine * Tenmangu * Kotohira Shrine * Fuji Shrine * Suijin Shrine === Cultural properties === === Ibaraki Prefecture designated natural monument === * Woodland of Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine (designated 2005) === Site information === * Address: Isozaki-cho 4607-2, Hitachinaka, Ibaraki * Access: Hitachinaka Seaside Railway Minato Line, Ajigaura Station, about 15 minutes on foot === Notes === {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist}} === External links === * [https://sakatura.org/ Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine] (official site) * Ibaraki Association of Shinto Shrines page * Kokugakuin source compilation page {{神道 横}}{{茨城県の神社一覧目次}} {{Normdaten}} == Categories == [[Category:Wikidata generated shikinaisha pages|Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine]][[Category:Shikinaisha|Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine]][[Category:Kokuhei-sha]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Hitachi Province]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Ibaraki Prefecture]] [[Category:Municipal History of Hitachinaka]] [[Category:Buildings in Hitachinaka]] [[Category:Myōjin Taisha]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Hitachi Province]] [[Category:Kokuhei Chūsha]] [[Category:Beppyo shrines]] [[Category:100 Views of Ibaraki]]

The plaque calligraphy is by Prince Akihito Komatsu.]] '''Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine''' (さかつらいそさきじんじゃ) is a Shinto shrine in Hitachinaka, Ibaraki. It is a Meishin-taisha listed in the Engishiki, formerly ranked kokuhei chusha, and currently a Beppyo shrine of Jinja Honcho. === Overview === The shrine stands on a coastal cape facing the Pacific Ocean. It is closely connected with {{ill|lt=Oarai Isosaki Shrine|Q11437230|qid=Q11437230|1=Oarai Isosaki Shrine}} across the Naka River, and the two are often regarded as forming a paired cult. === Enshrined deities === ; Main deity * {{ill|lt=Sukunahikona|Q3275687|qid=Q3275687|lt=Sukunahikona-no-Mikoto|1=Sukunabikona}} ; Co-enshrined * {{ill|qid=Q276944|lt=Okuninushi|Q276944|qid=Q276944|lt=Onamochi-no-Mikoto|1=Ōkuninushi}} The two-deity pairing is common because both appear together in kuni-zukuri myths. At this shrine, Sukunahikona is also associated with Ebisu and Onamochi with Daikokuten. === History === According to the ''Nihon Montoku Tenno Jitsuroku'' (856), divine signs appeared at Oarai Isosaki, with miraculous stones and an oracle declaring the returning deities Onamochi and Sukunahikona. Tradition says Onamochi was enshrined at Oarai and Sukunahikona at Sakatsura, establishing both shrines. The shrine name is linked to a local "reverse-tilting" rock formation (saka-tsura). Later, it came to be written with the character for sake (酒). In the Engishiki, it appears as "Sakare Isosaki Yakushi Bosatsu Shrine" in Naka District, Hitachi Province, and is listed as Meishin-taisha. It declined in the medieval period and lost its buildings; in the early modern period it was restored under Mito domain patronage by Tokugawa Mitsukuni and Tokugawa Tsunaeda, with relocation to the current site. In 1885 it was ranked kokuhei chusha. The official modern name is Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine. === Divine rank === * 857-08-07: entered official shrine register * 857-10-15: granted title "Yakushi Bosatsu Meishin" === Precinct === Notable features include: * Carving of squirrels and grapes above the haiden front (traditionally attributed to Jingoro Hidari) * Komainu at the second torii by Showa-era stonemason Iizuka Hyokichi * Broadleaf tree-lined approach (camellia, tabunoki, sudajii), designated natural monument of Ibaraki Prefecture 酒列磯前神社 本殿.JPG|Honden 酒列磯前神社 拝殿.JPG|Haiden 酒列磯前神社 水戸斉昭公腰かけの石.JPG|Seat stone of Tokugawa Nariaki 酒列磯前神社 二の鳥居.JPG|Second torii 酒列磯前神社 参道.JPG|Approach woodland (prefectural natural monument) === Subsidiary shrines === * Sakatsura Chinreisha (for 506 war dead from Russo-Japanese War to WWII) * Inari Shrine * Tenmangu * Kotohira Shrine * Fuji Shrine * Suijin Shrine === Cultural properties === === Ibaraki Prefecture designated natural monument === * Woodland of Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine (designated 2005) === Site information === * Address: Isozaki-cho 4607-2, Hitachinaka, Ibaraki * Access: Hitachinaka Seaside Railway Minato Line, Ajigaura Station, about 15 minutes on foot === Notes === {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist}} === External links === * [https://sakatura.org/ Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine] (official site) * Ibaraki Association of Shinto Shrines page * Kokugakuin source compilation page {{神道 横}}{{茨城県の神社一覧目次}} {{Normdaten}} == Categories == [[Category:Wikidata generated shikinaisha pages|Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine]][[Category:Shikinaisha|Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine]][[Category:Kokuhei-sha]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Hitachi Province]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Ibaraki Prefecture]] [[Category:Municipal History of Hitachinaka]] [[Category:Buildings in Hitachinaka]] [[Category:Myōjin Taisha]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Hitachi Province]] [[Category:Kokuhei Chūsha]] [[Category:Beppyo shrines]] [[Category:100 Views of Ibaraki]]

The plaque calligraphy is by Prince Akihito Komatsu.]] '''Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine''' (さかつらいそさきじんじゃ) is a Shinto shrine in Hitachinaka, Ibaraki. It is a Meishin-taisha listed in the Engishiki, formerly ranked kokuhei chusha, and currently a Beppyo shrine of Jinja Honcho. === Overview === The shrine stands on a coastal cape facing the Pacific Ocean. It is closely connected with {{ill|lt=Oarai Isosaki Shrine|Q11437230|qid=Q11437230|1=Oarai Isosaki Shrine}} across the Naka River, and the two are often regarded as forming a paired cult. === Enshrined deities === ; Main deity * {{ill|lt=Sukunahikona|Q3275687|qid=Q3275687|lt=Sukunahikona-no-Mikoto|1=Sukunabikona}} ; Co-enshrined * {{ill|qid=Q276944|lt=Okuninushi|Q276944|qid=Q276944|lt=Onamochi-no-Mikoto|1=Ōkuninushi}} The two-deity pairing is common because both appear together in kuni-zukuri myths. At this shrine, Sukunahikona is also associated with Ebisu and Onamochi with Daikokuten. === History === According to the ''Nihon Montoku Tenno Jitsuroku'' (856), divine signs appeared at Oarai Isosaki, with miraculous stones and an oracle declaring the returning deities Onamochi and Sukunahikona. Tradition says Onamochi was enshrined at Oarai and Sukunahikona at Sakatsura, establishing both shrines. The shrine name is linked to a local "reverse-tilting" rock formation (saka-tsura). Later, it came to be written with the character for sake (酒). In the Engishiki, it appears as "Sakare Isosaki Yakushi Bosatsu Shrine" in Naka District, Hitachi Province, and is listed as Meishin-taisha. It declined in the medieval period and lost its buildings; in the early modern period it was restored under Mito domain patronage by Tokugawa Mitsukuni and Tokugawa Tsunaeda, with relocation to the current site. In 1885 it was ranked kokuhei chusha. The official modern name is Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine. === Divine rank === * 857-08-07: entered official shrine register * 857-10-15: granted title "Yakushi Bosatsu Meishin" === Precinct === Notable features include: * Carving of squirrels and grapes above the haiden front (traditionally attributed to Jingoro Hidari) * Komainu at the second torii by Showa-era stonemason Iizuka Hyokichi * Broadleaf tree-lined approach (camellia, tabunoki, sudajii), designated natural monument of Ibaraki Prefecture 酒列磯前神社 本殿.JPG|Honden 酒列磯前神社 拝殿.JPG|Haiden 酒列磯前神社 水戸斉昭公腰かけの石.JPG|Seat stone of Tokugawa Nariaki 酒列磯前神社 二の鳥居.JPG|Second torii 酒列磯前神社 参道.JPG|Approach woodland (prefectural natural monument) === Subsidiary shrines === * Sakatsura Chinreisha (for 506 war dead from Russo-Japanese War to WWII) * Inari Shrine * Tenmangu * Kotohira Shrine * Fuji Shrine * Suijin Shrine === Cultural properties === === Ibaraki Prefecture designated natural monument === * Woodland of Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine (designated 2005) === Site information === * Address: Isozaki-cho 4607-2, Hitachinaka, Ibaraki * Access: Hitachinaka Seaside Railway Minato Line, Ajigaura Station, about 15 minutes on foot === Notes === {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist}} === External links === * [https://sakatura.org/ Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine] (official site) * Ibaraki Association of Shinto Shrines page * Kokugakuin source compilation page {{神道 横}}{{茨城県の神社一覧目次}} {{Normdaten}} == Categories == [[Category:Wikidata generated shikinaisha pages|Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine]][[Category:Shikinaisha|Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine]][[Category:Kokuhei-sha]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Hitachi Province]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Ibaraki Prefecture]] [[Category:Municipal History of Hitachinaka]] [[Category:Buildings in Hitachinaka]] [[Category:Myōjin Taisha]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Hitachi Province]] [[Category:Kokuhei Chūsha]] [[Category:Beppyo shrines]] [[Category:100 Views of Ibaraki]]

The plaque calligraphy is by Prince Akihito Komatsu.]] '''Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine''' (さかつらいそさきじんじゃ) is a Shinto shrine in Hitachinaka, Ibaraki. It is a Meishin-taisha listed in the Engishiki, formerly ranked kokuhei chusha, and currently a Beppyo shrine of Jinja Honcho. === Overview === The shrine stands on a coastal cape facing the Pacific Ocean. It is closely connected with {{ill|lt=Oarai Isosaki Shrine|Q11437230|qid=Q11437230|1=Oarai Isosaki Shrine}} across the Naka River, and the two are often regarded as forming a paired cult. === Enshrined deities === ; Main deity * {{ill|lt=Sukunahikona|Q3275687|qid=Q3275687|lt=Sukunahikona-no-Mikoto|1=Sukunabikona}} ; Co-enshrined * {{ill|qid=Q276944|lt=Okuninushi|Q276944|qid=Q276944|lt=Onamochi-no-Mikoto|1=Ōkuninushi}} The two-deity pairing is common because both appear together in kuni-zukuri myths. At this shrine, Sukunahikona is also associated with Ebisu and Onamochi with Daikokuten. === History === According to the ''Nihon Montoku Tenno Jitsuroku'' (856), divine signs appeared at Oarai Isosaki, with miraculous stones and an oracle declaring the returning deities Onamochi and Sukunahikona. Tradition says Onamochi was enshrined at Oarai and Sukunahikona at Sakatsura, establishing both shrines. The shrine name is linked to a local "reverse-tilting" rock formation (saka-tsura). Later, it came to be written with the character for sake (酒). In the Engishiki, it appears as "Sakare Isosaki Yakushi Bosatsu Shrine" in Naka District, Hitachi Province, and is listed as Meishin-taisha. It declined in the medieval period and lost its buildings; in the early modern period it was restored under Mito domain patronage by Tokugawa Mitsukuni and Tokugawa Tsunaeda, with relocation to the current site. In 1885 it was ranked kokuhei chusha. The official modern name is Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine. === Divine rank === * 857-08-07: entered official shrine register * 857-10-15: granted title "Yakushi Bosatsu Meishin" === Precinct === Notable features include: * Carving of squirrels and grapes above the haiden front (traditionally attributed to Jingoro Hidari) * Komainu at the second torii by Showa-era stonemason Iizuka Hyokichi * Broadleaf tree-lined approach (camellia, tabunoki, sudajii), designated natural monument of Ibaraki Prefecture 酒列磯前神社 本殿.JPG|Honden 酒列磯前神社 拝殿.JPG|Haiden 酒列磯前神社 水戸斉昭公腰かけの石.JPG|Seat stone of Tokugawa Nariaki 酒列磯前神社 二の鳥居.JPG|Second torii 酒列磯前神社 参道.JPG|Approach woodland (prefectural natural monument) === Subsidiary shrines === * Sakatsura Chinreisha (for 506 war dead from Russo-Japanese War to WWII) * Inari Shrine * Tenmangu * Kotohira Shrine * Fuji Shrine * Suijin Shrine === Cultural properties === === Ibaraki Prefecture designated natural monument === * Woodland of Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine (designated 2005) === Site information === * Address: Isozaki-cho 4607-2, Hitachinaka, Ibaraki * Access: Hitachinaka Seaside Railway Minato Line, Ajigaura Station, about 15 minutes on foot === Notes === {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist}} === External links === * [https://sakatura.org/ Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine] (official site) * Ibaraki Association of Shinto Shrines page * Kokugakuin source compilation page {{神道 横}}{{茨城県の神社一覧目次}} {{Normdaten}} == Categories == [[Category:Wikidata generated shikinaisha pages|Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine]][[Category:Shikinaisha|Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine]][[Category:Kokuhei-sha]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Hitachi Province]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Ibaraki Prefecture]] [[Category:Municipal History of Hitachinaka]] [[Category:Buildings in Hitachinaka]] [[Category:Myōjin Taisha]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Hitachi Province]] [[Category:Kokuhei Chūsha]] [[Category:Beppyo shrines]] [[Category:100 Views of Ibaraki]]
